158.s:
puṣkara uvāca
srāvāśaucaṃ pravakṣyāmi manvādimunisammataṃ /
:n
1 siddhārthakaistilair viprān yajadvāso 'paraṃ dadhaditi gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca /
siddhārthastilair vidvān snāyādvāso 'paraṃ dadhaditi ga.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 134
rātribhirmāsatulyābhirgarbhasrāve tryaheṇa yā //
158.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
स्रावाशौचं प्रवक्ष्यामि मन्वादिमुनिसम्मतं /
:न्
1 सिद्धार्थकैस्तिलैर् विप्रान् यजद्वासो ऽपरं दधदिति घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च /
सिद्धार्थस्तिलैर् विद्वान् स्नायाद्वासो ऽपरं दधदिति ग.. , ट.. च
:प् 134
रात्रिभिर्मासतुल्याभिर्गर्भस्रावे त्र्यहेण या //
158.m:
Puṣkara said:
I shall explain the ritual impurity from miscarriage, as agreed upon by sages such as Manu.
[Footnote]
1. "siddhārthakaistilair viprān yajadvāso 'paraṃ dadhat" in gha, ṅa, and ña; / "siddhārthastilair vidvān snāyādvāso 'paraṃ dadhat" in ga and ṭa.
[Page] 134
In a miscarriage [in the first three months, ritual impurity lasts] for three days, or for nights equal to the number of months.

158.s:
cāturmāsikapātānte daśāhaṃ pañcamāsataḥ /
rājanye ca catūrātraṃ vaiśye pañcāhameva ca //
158.d:
चातुर्मासिकपातान्ते दशाहं पञ्चमासतः /
राजन्ये च चतूरात्रं वैश्ये पञ्चाहमेव च //
158.m:
At the end of a four-month miscarriage, [impurity lasts four days]; from the fifth month, it is ten days.
For a Kṣatriya it is four nights, and for a Vaiśya it is five days;

158.s:
aṣṭāhena tu śūdrasya dvādaśāhādataḥ paraṃ /
strīṇāṃ viśuddhiruditā(1) snānamātreṇa vai pituḥ //
158.d:
अष्टाहेन तु शूद्रस्य द्वादशाहादतः परं /
स्त्रीणां विशुद्धिरुदिता(1) स्नानमात्रेण वै पितुः //
158.m:
for a Śūdra it is eight days, and beyond this it is twelve days.
Purification is declared for women [in this manner]; for the father it is indeed by a simple bath.

158.s:
na snānaṃ hi sapiṇḍe syāttrirātraṃ saptamāṣṭayoḥ /
sadyaḥ śaucaṃ sapiṇḍānāmādantajananāttathā //
158.d:
न स्नानं हि सपिण्डे स्यात्त्रिरात्रं सप्तमाष्टयोः /
सद्यः शौचं सपिण्डानामादन्तजननात्तथा //
158.m:
There is no bathing [required] for a sapinda [relative]; in the seventh and eighth [months], it is three nights.
Immediate purity is prescribed for sapindas [upon the death of a child] prior to the eruption of teeth.

158.s:
ācūḍādekarātraṃ syādāvratācca trirātrakaṃ /
daśarātraṃ bhavedasmānmātāpitrostrirātrakaṃ //
158.d:
आचूडादेकरात्रं स्यादाव्रताच्च त्रिरात्रकं /
दशरात्रं भवेदस्मान्मातापित्रोस्त्रिरात्रकं //
158.m:
Until tonsure, it is one night; until initiation into vows, it is three nights;
after this, it is ten nights; for the mother and father, it is three nights.

158.s:
ajātadante tu mṛte kṛtacūḍe 'rbhake tathā /
prete nyūne tribhirvarṣair mṛte śuddhistu naiśilkī //
158.d:
अजातदन्ते तु मृते कृतचूडे ऽर्भके तथा /
प्रेते न्यूने त्रिभिर्वर्षैर् मृते शुद्धिस्तु नैशिल्की //
158.m:
When a child dies without erupted teeth, or an infant whose tonsure has been performed,
or if the deceased died when under three years of age, purification takes one night.

158.s:
dvyaheṇa kṣatriye śuddhistribhirvaiśye mṛte tathā /
śuddhiḥ śūdre pañcabhiḥ syāt prāgvivāhad dviṣaṭtvahaḥ(2) //
158.d:
द्व्यहेण क्षत्रिये शुद्धिस्त्रिभिर्वैश्ये मृते तथा /
शुद्धिः शूद्रे पञ्चभिः स्यात् प्राग्विवाहद् द्विषट्त्वहः(2) //
158.m:
Purification for a Kṣatriya is in two days, and when a Vaiśya dies, in three;
purification for a Śūdra is in five; prior to marriage, it is twelve days.

158.s:
yatra trirātraṃ viprāṇāmaśaucaṃ sampradṛśyate /
tatra śūdre dvādaśāhaḥ ṣaṇṇava kṣatravaiśayyoḥ //
158.d:
यत्र त्रिरात्रं विप्राणामशौचं सम्प्रदृश्यते /
तत्र शूद्रे द्वादशाहः षण्णव क्षत्रवैशय्योः //
158.m:
Where three nights of ritual impurity are observed for Brahmins,
there it is twelve days for a Śūdra, and six and nine for a Kṣatriya and a Vaiśya [respectively].

158.s:
dvyabde naivāgnisaṃskāro mṛte tannikhaned bhuvi /
na codakakriyā tasya nāmni cāpi kṛte sati //
158.d:
द्व्यब्दे नैवाग्निसंस्कारो मृते तन्निखनेद् भुवि /
न चोदकक्रिया तस्य नाम्नि चापि कृते सति //
158.m:
When [a child] dies at two years of age, cremation is not performed; one should bury it in the ground;
and there is no rite of water for him, even if the naming rite has been performed.

158.s:
jātadantasya vā kāryā syādupanayanāddaśa /
ekāhācchuddhyate vipro yo 'gnivedasamanvitaḥ //
158.d:
जातदन्तस्य वा कार्या स्यादुपनयनाद्दश /
एकाहाच्छुद्ध्यते विप्रो यो ऽग्निवेदसमन्वितः //
158.m:
Or it should be performed for one whose teeth have erupted; up to the sacred thread ceremony, it is ten [days].
A Brahmin who is endowed with the sacred fires and the Veda is purified in one day.

158.s:
hīne hīnatare caiva tryahaś caturahas tathā /
pañcāhenāgnihīnastu daśāhādbrāhmaṇavruvaḥ //
:n
1 viśuddhiḥ kathiteti gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
2 dviṣaṭkakamiti ṭa..
:p 135
158.d:
हीने हीनतरे चैव त्र्यहश् चतुरहस् तथा /
पञ्चाहेनाग्निहीनस्तु दशाहाद्ब्राह्मणव्रुवः //
:न्
1 विशुद्धिः कथितेति घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
2 द्विषट्ककमिति ट..
:प् 135
158.m:
For one lacking in these and further lacking, it is three days and four days respectively;
one without sacred fires is purified in five days, and a nominal Brahmin in ten days.
[Footnote]
1. "viśuddhiḥ kathitā" in gha, ṅa, and ña.
2. "dviṣaṭkakam" in ṭa.
[Page] 135

158.s:
kṣatriyo navasaptāhacchuddhyedvipro guṇair yutaḥ /
daśāhāt saguṇo vaiśyo viṃśāhācchūdra eva ca //
158.d:
क्षत्रियो नवसप्ताहच्छुद्ध्येद्विप्रो गुणैर् युतः /
दशाहात् सगुणो वैश्यो विंशाहाच्छूद्र एव च //
158.m:
A Kṣatriya endowed with virtues is purified in nine or seven days, a Brahmin in one,
a virtuous Vaiśya in ten days, and a Śūdra in twenty days.

158.s:
daśāhācchuddhyate vipro dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ /
vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhena śūdro māsena śuddhyati //
158.d:
दशाहाच्छुद्ध्यते विप्रो द्वादशाहेन भूमिपः /
वैश्यः पञ्चदशाहेन शूद्रो मासेन शुद्ध्यति //
158.m:
A Brahmin is purified in ten days, a king in twelve days,
a Vaiśya in fifteen days, and a Śūdra is purified in a month.

158.s:
guṇotkarṣe daśāhāptau tryahamekāhakaṃ tryahe /
ekāhāptau sadyaḥ śaucaṃ sarvatraivaṃ samūhayet //
158.d:
गुणोत्कर्षे दशाहाप्तौ त्र्यहमेकाहकं त्र्यहे /
एकाहाप्तौ सद्यः शौचं सर्वत्रैवं समूहयेत् //
158.m:
Where ten days apply, through excellence of virtues it is three days; where three days apply, it is one day;
where one day applies, it becomes immediate purity; one should deduce similarly everywhere.

158.s:
dāsāntevāsibhṛtakāḥ śiṣyāś caivātra vāsinaḥ /
svāmitulyamaśaucaṃ syānmṛte pṛthak pṛthagbhavet //
158.d:
दासान्तेवासिभृतकाः शिष्याश् चैवात्र वासिनः /
स्वामितुल्यमशौचं स्यान्मृते पृथक् पृथग्भवेत् //
158.m:
Slaves, resident pupils, hired servants, disciples, and those residing here
have ritual impurity equal to the master's; upon death, each should be separate.

158.s:
maraṇādeva kartavyaṃ saṃyogo yasya nāgnibhiḥ /
dāhādūrdhvamaśaucaṃ syādyasya vaitāniko vidhiḥ //
158.d:
मरणादेव कर्तव्यं संयोगो यस्य नाग्निभिः /
दाहादूर्ध्वमशौचं स्याद्यस्य वैतानिको विधिः //
158.m:
[Impurity] is to be reckoned from death itself for one who has no connection with the [sacred] fires;
for one who follows the solemn rites of the Veda, ritual impurity begins after cremation.

158.s:
sarveṣāmeva varṇānāntribhāgāt sparśanambhavet /
tricatuḥpañcadaśabhiḥ spṛśyavarṇāḥ krameṇa tu //
158.d:
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानान्त्रिभागात् स्पर्शनम्भवेत् /
त्रिचतुःपञ्चदशभिः स्पृश्यवर्णाः क्रमेण तु //
158.m:
For all castes, touching is allowed after a third [of the impurity period has passed];
the castes become touchable after three, four, five, and ten [days] in order.

158.s:
caturthe pañcame caiva saptame navame tathā /
asthisañcayanaṃ kāryaṃ varṇānāmanupūrvaśaḥ //
158.d:
चतुर्थे पञ्चमे चैव सप्तमे नवमे तथा /
अस्थिसञ्चयनं कार्यं वर्णानामनुपूर्वशः //
158.m:
On the fourth, fifth, seventh, and ninth [day] respectively,
the collection of bones should be performed for the castes in order.

158.s:
ahastvadattakanyāsu pradattāsu tryahaṃ bhavet /
pakṣiṇī saṃskṛtāsveva svasrādiṣu vidhīyate //
158.d:
अहस्त्वदत्तकन्यासु प्रदत्तासु त्र्यहं भवेत् /
पक्षिणी संस्कृतास्वेव स्वस्रादिषु विधीयते //
158.m:
In the case of unbetrothed maidens, it is one day; for betrothed ones, it is three days.
A day and two nights is prescribed for married women, sisters, and the like.

158.s:
pitṛgotraṃ kumārīṇāṃ vyūḍhānāṃ bhartṛgotratā /
jalapradānaṃ pitre ca udvāhe cobhayatra tu //
158.d:
पितृगोत्रं कुमारीणां व्यूढानां भर्तृगोत्रता /
जलप्रदानं पित्रे च उद्वाहे चोभयत्र तु //
158.m:
Unmarried girls belong to the lineage of the father; married women belong to the lineage of the husband.
The offering of water is to the father, but at marriage it is to both.

158.s:
daśāhopari pitroś ca duhiturmaraṇe tryahaṃ /
sadyaḥ śaucaṃ sapiṇḍānāṃ pūrvaṃ cūḍākṛterdvija //
158.d:
दशाहोपरि पित्रोश् च दुहितुर्मरणे त्र्यहं /
सद्यः शौचं सपिण्डानां पूर्वं चूडाकृतेर्द्विज //
158.m:
Upon the death of a daughter after ten days [of life], it is three days for the parents.
Prior to the tonsure rite, O twice-born, there is immediate purity for sapindas.

158.s:
ekāhato hy āvivihādūrdhvaṃ hastodakāt tryahaṃ /
pakṣiṇī bhrātṛputrasya sapiṇḍānāṃ ca sadyataḥ //
158.d:
एकाहतो ह्य् आविविहादूर्ध्वं हस्तोदकात् त्र्यहं /
पक्षिणी भ्रातृपुत्रस्य सपिण्डानां च सद्यतः //
158.m: [Ritual impurity lasts] for one day prior to marriage, but for three days after the ritual pouring of water on the bride's hand; / for a brother's son it lasts a day and a night with the intervening night or day, and for sapindas [it terminates] immediately.

158.s:
daśāhācchuddhyate vipro janmahānau svayoniṣu /
:p 136
ṣadbhistribhirahaikena kṣatraviṭśūdrayoniṣu //
158.d:
दशाहाच्छुद्ध्यते विप्रो जन्महानौ स्वयोनिषु /
:प् 136
षद्भिस्त्रिभिरहैकेन क्षत्रविट्शूद्रयोनिषु //
158.m:
A Brahmin is purified after ten days in the event of birth or death among his own kin,
[Page 136]
[and] after six days, three days, and a single day [respectively] among Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra kin.

158.s:
etajjñeyaṃ sapiṇḍānāṃ vakṣye cānaurasādiṣu /
anauraseṣu putreṣu bhāryāsvanyagatāsu ca //
158.d:
एतज्ज्ञेयं सपिण्डानां वक्ष्ये चानौरसादिषु /
अनौरसेषु पुत्रेषु भार्यास्वन्यगतासु च //
158.m: This is to be known regarding sapindas; and I shall state [it] regarding non-aurasa sons and others: / in the case of non-aurasa sons, and wives who have gone to another,

158.s:
parapūrvāsu ca strīṣu trirātrācchuddhiriṣyate /
vṛthāsaṅkarajātānāṃ pravrajyāsu ca tiṣṭhatāṃ //
158.d:
परपूर्वासु च स्त्रीषु त्रिरात्राच्छुद्धिरिष्यते /
वृथासङ्करजातानां प्रव्रज्यासु च तिष्ठतां //
158.m: and in the case of women who previously had another husband, purification is prescribed after three nights. / For those born of improper miscegenation, and those residing in the ascetic life,

158.s:
ātmanastyāgināñcaiva nivartetodakakriyā /
mātraikayā dvipitarau bhratarāvanyagāminau //
158.d:
आत्मनस्त्यागिनाञ्चैव निवर्तेतोदकक्रिया /
मात्रैकया द्विपितरौ भ्रतरावन्यगामिनौ //
158.m: and for those who commit suicide, the water-libation rite ceases. / Two brothers with different fathers by one mother, who have gone to another,

158.s:
ekāhaḥ sūtake tatra mṛtake tu dvyaho bhavet(1) /
sapiṇḍānāmaśaucaṃ hi samānodakatāṃ vade //
158.d:
एकाहः सूतके तत्र मृतके तु द्व्यहो भवेत्(1) /
सपिण्डानामशौचं हि समानोदकतां वदे //
158.m: in that case have [ritual impurity of] one day upon birth, but upon death there would be two days. / Indeed, I shall now declare the ritual impurity of sapindas and samānodakas.

158.s:
bāle deśāntarasthe ca pṛthakpiṇḍe ca saṃsthite /
savāsā jalamāplutya sadya eva viśuddhyati //
158.d:
बाले देशान्तरस्थे च पृथक्पिण्डे च संस्थिते /
सवासा जलमाप्लुत्य सद्य एव विशुद्ध्यति //
158.m: When a child, or one residing in a distant country, or a relative offering separate funerary cakes dies, / one becomes purified immediately upon bathing in water together with one's clothes.

158.s:
daśāhena sapiṇḍāstu śuddhyanti pretasūtake /
trirātreṇa sukulyāstu snānāt(2) śuddhyanti gotriṇaḥ //
158.d:
दशाहेन सपिण्डास्तु शुद्ध्यन्ति प्रेतसूतके /
त्रिरात्रेण सुकुल्यास्तु स्नानात्(2) शुद्ध्यन्ति गोत्रिणः //
158.m: Sapindas are purified in ten days upon birth or death; / relatives of good family [are purified] in three nights, and clan-members are purified through bathing.

158.s:
sapiṇḍatā tu puruṣe saptame vinivartate /
samānodakabhāvastu nivartetācaturdaśāt //
158.d:
सपिण्डता तु पुरुषे सप्तमे विनिवर्तते /
समानोदकभावस्तु निवर्तेताचतुर्दशात् //
158.m: The status of sapinda ceases in the seventh generation, / but the status of samānodaka ceases up to the fourteenth [generation],

158.s:
janmanāmasmṛte vaitat tatparaṃ gotramucyate /
vigatantu videśasthaṃ śṛṇuyādyo hy anirdaśaṃ //
158.d:
जन्मनामस्मृते वैतत् तत्परं गोत्रमुच्यते /
विगतन्तु विदेशस्थं शृणुयाद्यो ह्य् अनिर्दशं //
158.m: or when the birth and name are forgotten; beyond that, it is merely called a gotra. / If one hears of a deceased person living abroad before ten days have elapsed,

158.s:
yaccheṣaṃ daśarātrasya tāvadevāśucirbhavet /
atikrānte daśāhe tu trirātramaśucirbhavet //
158.d:
यच्छेषं दशरात्रस्य तावदेवाशुचिर्भवेत् /
अतिक्रान्ते दशाहे तु त्रिरात्रमशुचिर्भवेत् //
158.m: he remains impure only for whatever is left of the ten nights; / but if the ten days have elapsed, he remains impure for three nights.

158.s:
saṃvatsare vyatīte tu spṛṣṭvaivāpo viśuddhyati /
:n
1 mṛtake tu tryaho bhavediti gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca / matake tu tathā bhavediti
jha..
2 snātā iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
:p 137
mātule pakṣiṇo rātriḥ śiṣyatvigbāndhaveṣu ca //
158.d:
संवत्सरे व्यतीते तु स्पृष्ट्वैवापो विशुद्ध्यति /
:न्
1 मृतके तु त्र्यहो भवेदिति घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च / मतके तु तथा भवेदिति
झ..
2 स्नाता इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. च
:प् 137
मातुले पक्षिणो रात्रिः शिष्यत्विग्बान्धवेषु च //
158.m:
When a year has elapsed, he is purified simply by touching water.
[Note]
1 In manuscripts gha, ṅa, and ña: "mṛtake tu tryaho bhaved" [there would be three days upon death]; in jha: "matake tu tathā bhaved".
2 In manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cha, and ja: "snātā" [having bathed].
[Page 137]
Upon [the death of] a maternal uncle, a day and two nights, and likewise for a pupil, an officiating priest, and a relative.

158.s:
mṛṭe jāmātari prete daihitre bhaginīsute(1) /
śyālake tatsute caiva snānamātraṃ vidhīyate //
158.d:
मृटे जामातरि प्रेते दैहित्रे भगिनीसुते(1) /
श्यालके तत्सुते चैव स्नानमात्रं विधीयते //
158.m: When a son-in-law dies, or a daughter's son, or a sister's son, / or a brother-in-law, or his son, mere bathing is prescribed.

158.s:
mātāmahyāṃ tathācārye mṛte mātāmahe tryahaṃ /
durbhikṣe rāṣṭrasampāte āgatāyāṃ tathāpadi //
158.d:
मातामह्यां तथाचार्ये मृते मातामहे त्र्यहं /
दुर्भिक्षे राष्ट्रसम्पाते आगतायां तथापदि //
158.m: Upon the death of a maternal grandmother, or likewise a teacher, or a maternal grandfather, [it lasts] three days. / In a famine, a calamity in the kingdom, or when a sudden disaster has arrived,

158.s:
upasargamṛtānāñca dāhe brahmavidāntathā /
satrivrati(2) brahmattārisaṅgrāme deśaviplave //
158.d:
उपसर्गमृतानाञ्च दाहे ब्रह्मविदान्तथा /
सत्रिव्रति(2) ब्रह्मत्तारिसङ्ग्रामे देशविप्लवे //
158.m: at the cremation of those who died of a pestilence, and likewise of knowers of the Veda, / during a sacrifice, an observance, for a student of the Veda, in battle, in the devastation of the land,

158.s:
dāne yajñe vivāhe ca sadyaḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate /
vipragonṛpahantṝṇāmanuktaṃ cātmaghātināṃ //
158.d:
दाने यज्ञे विवाहे च सद्यः शौचं विधीयते /
विप्रगोनृपहन्तॄणामनुक्तं चात्मघातिनां //
158.m: in making a gift, at a sacrifice, and during a marriage, immediate ritual purity is prescribed. / None is declared for the killers of Brahmins, cows, or kings, or for suicides.

158.s:
asādhyavyādhiyuktasya svādhyāye cākṣamasya ca /
prāyaścittamanujñātamagnitoyapraveśanaṃ //
158.d:
असाध्यव्याधियुक्तस्य स्वाध्याये चाक्षमस्य च /
प्रायश्चित्तमनुज्ञातमग्नितोयप्रवेशनं //
158.m: For one afflicted with an incurable disease and unable to perform sacred study, / entering into fire or water is permitted as an expiation.

158.s:
apamānāttathā(3) krodhāt snehātparibhavādbhayāt /
udbadhya mriyate nārī puruṣo vā kathañcana //
158.d:
अपमानात्तथा(3) क्रोधात् स्नेहात्परिभवाद्भयात् /
उद्बध्य म्रियते नारी पुरुषो वा कथञ्चन //
158.m: If out of insult, anger, attachment, humilation, or fear, / a woman or a man dies by hanging in any way,

158.s:
ātmaghātī caikalakṣaṃ vasetsa narake śucau /
vṛddhaḥ śrautasmṛterluptaḥ parityajati yastvasūn //
158.d:
आत्मघाती चैकलक्षं वसेत्स नरके शुचौ /
वृद्धः श्रौतस्मृतेर्लुप्तः परित्यजति यस्त्वसून् //
158.m: such a suicide will dwell for one hundred thousand [years] in a terrifying hell. / An elderly person, whose Vedic and traditional duties have lapsed, who abandons his life,

158.s:
trirātraṃ tatra śāśaucaṃ dvitīye cāsthisañcayaṃ /
tṛtīye tūdakaṃ kāryaṃ caturthe śrāddhamācaret //
158.d:
त्रिरात्रं तत्र शाशौचं द्वितीये चास्थिसञ्चयं /
तृतीये तूदकं कार्यं चतुर्थे श्राद्धमाचरेत् //
158.m: in that case there is ritual impurity for three nights, collection of the bones on the second [day], / water offering to be performed on the third, and on the fourth one should perform the ancestral rite.

158.s:
vidyudagnihatānāñca tryahaṃ śuddhiḥ sapiṇḍike(4) /
pāṣaṇḍāśritā bhartṛghnyo nāśaucodakagāḥ striyaḥ //
158.d:
विद्युदग्निहतानाञ्च त्र्यहं शुद्धिः सपिण्डिके(4) /
पाषण्डाश्रिता भर्तृघ्न्यो नाशौचोदकगाः स्त्रियः //
158.m: For those killed by lightning or fire, purification among sapindas takes three days. / Women who have taken refuge in heretical sects or who are husband-slayers are not entitled to rites of ritual impurity or water libations.

158.s:
pitṛmātrādipāte tu ārdravāsā hy upoṣitaḥ /
:n
1 prete, bhaginīsuta ity api iti ṭa..
2 yativratīti ja..
3 apamānādatheti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
4 vidyudādihatānāñca tryahācchuddhirvidhīyate iti ṭa..
:p 138
atītebde prakurvīta pretakāryaṃ yathāvidhi //
158.d:
पितृमात्रादिपाते तु आर्द्रवासा ह्य् उपोषितः /
:न्
1 प्रेते, भगिनीसुत इत्य् अपि इति ट..
2 यतिव्रतीति ज..
3 अपमानादथेति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. च
4 विद्युदादिहतानाञ्च त्र्यहाच्छुद्धिर्विधीयते इति ट..
:प् 138
अतीतेब्दे प्रकुर्वीत प्रेतकार्यं यथाविधि //
158.m:
Upon the demise of one's father, mother, or others, having wet garments and having fasted,
[Note]
1 Manuscript ṭa reads: "prete, bhaginīsuta ity api".
2 Manuscript ja reads: "yativratī".
3 Manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cha, and ja read: "apamānādathe".
4 Manuscript ṭa reads: "vidyudādihatānāñca tryahācchuddhirvidhīyate".
[Page 138]
when a year has passed, one should perform the funeral rites according to the rule.

158.s:
yaḥ kaścittu haret pretamasapiṇḍaṃ kathañcana /
snātvā scelaḥ spṛṣṭvāgniṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśuddhyati //
158.d:
यः कश्चित्तु हरेत् प्रेतमसपिण्डं कथञ्चन /
स्नात्वा स्चेलः स्पृष्ट्वाग्निं घृतं प्राश्य विशुद्ध्यति //
158.m: Whoever carries a deceased person who is not a sapinda in any manner, / having bathed with his clothes on, touched fire, and tasted clarified butter, becomes purified.

158.s:
yadyannamatti teṣāntu daśāhenaiva śuddhyati /
anadannannamahnyeva na vai tasmin gṛhe vaset //
158.d:
यद्यन्नमत्ति तेषान्तु दशाहेनैव शुद्ध्यति /
अनदन्नन्नमह्न्येव न वै तस्मिन् गृहे वसेत् //
158.m: If he eats their food, he is purified only after ten days; / if not eating their food, [he is purified] on that very day, but he must not dwell in that house.

158.s:
anāthaṃ vrāhmaṇaṃ pretaṃ ye vahanti dvijātayaḥ /
pade pade yajñaphalaṃ śuddhiḥ syāt snānamātrataḥ //
158.d:
अनाथं व्राह्मणं प्रेतं ये वहन्ति द्विजातयः /
पदे पदे यज्ञफलं शुद्धिः स्यात् स्नानमात्रतः //
158.m: Whatever twice-born persons carry a deceased Brahmin who is destitute, / at every step they obtain the fruit of a sacrifice, and purity is attained merely by bathing.

158.s:
pretībhūtaṃ dvijaḥ śūdramanugacchaṃstryahācchuciḥ /
mṛtasya bāndhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ kṛtvā ca paridevanaṃ //
158.d:
प्रेतीभूतं द्विजः शूद्रमनुगच्छंस्त्र्यहाच्छुचिः /
मृतस्य बान्धवैः सार्धं कृत्वा च परिदेवनं //
158.m: A twice-born person who follows a Śūdra corpse becomes pure after three days, / having made lamentation together with the deceased's relatives.

158.s:
varjayettadahorātraṃ dānaśrāddhādi kāmataḥ(1) /
śūdrāyāḥ prasavo gehe śūdrasya maraṇaṃ tathā //
158.d:
वर्जयेत्तदहोरात्रं दानश्राद्धादि कामतः(1) /
शूद्रायाः प्रसवो गेहे शूद्रस्य मरणं तथा //
158.m: For that day and night he should intentionally avoid gifts, ancestral rites, and the like. / When there is a birth from a Śūdra woman or the death of a Śūdra in the house,

158.s:
bhāṇḍāni tu parityajya tryahādbhūlepataḥ śuciḥ /
na vipraṃ sveṣu tiṣṭhatsu mṛtaṃ śūdreṇa nāyayet //
158.d:
भाण्डानि तु परित्यज्य त्र्यहाद्भूलेपतः शुचिः /
न विप्रं स्वेषु तिष्ठत्सु मृतं शूद्रेण नाययेत् //
158.m: having abandoned the earthen vessels, one becomes pure after three days by smearing the ground. / One should not have a deceased Brahmin carried by a Śūdra when his own kin are present.

158.s:
nayet pretaṃ snāpitañca pūjitaṃ kusumair dahet /
nagnadehaṃ dahen naiva kiñciddehaṃ parityajet //
158.d:
नयेत् प्रेतं स्नापितञ्च पूजितं कुसुमैर् दहेत् /
नग्नदेहं दहेन् नैव किञ्चिद्देहं परित्यजेत् //
158.m: One should carry the corpse, bathe it, and burn it after worshiping it with flowers; / one should not burn the body naked, nor leave behind any part of the body.

158.s:
gotrajastu gṛhītvā tu citāṃ cāropayettadā /
āhitāgniryathānyāyaṃ dagdhavyastibhiragnibhiḥ //
158.d:
गोत्रजस्तु गृहीत्वा तु चितां चारोपयेत्तदा /
आहिताग्निर्यथान्यायं दग्धव्यस्तिभिरग्निभिः //
158.m: A clan member should then take [the corpse] and raise it onto the pyre. / A maintainer of the sacred fires should be burned with the three fires according to the rule,

158.s:
anāhitāgnirekena laukikenāparas tathā /
asmāt tvamabhijāto 'si tvadayaṃ jāyatāṃ punaḥ //
158.d:
अनाहिताग्निरेकेन लौकिकेनापरस् तथा /
अस्मात् त्वमभिजातो ऽसि त्वदयं जायतां पुनः //
158.m: and one who is not a maintainer of the sacred fires with one, while another [ordinary person is burned] with the worldly fire: / "From this you were born; may this be born again from you!"

158.s:
asau svargāya lokāya sukhāgniṃ pradadetsutaḥ /
sakṛtprasiñcantyudakaṃ nāmagotreṇa bāndhavāḥ //
:n
1 dānaśrāddhādikarma ceti jha..
:p 139
158.d:
असौ स्वर्गाय लोकाय सुखाग्निं प्रददेत्सुतः /
सकृत्प्रसिञ्चन्त्युदकं नामगोत्रेण बान्धवाः //
:न्
1 दानश्राद्धादिकर्म चेति झ..
:प् 139
158.m:
For the sake of that heavenly realm, the son should present the auspicious fire. / The relatives pour water once with the name and clan name [of the deceased].
[Note]
1 Manuscript jha reads: "dānaśrāddhādikarma ca".
[Page 139]

158.s:
evaṃ mātāmahācāryapretānāñcodakakriyā /
kāmyodakaṃ sakhipretasvasrīyaśvaśrurartvijāṃ //
158.d:
एवं मातामहाचार्यप्रेतानाञ्चोदकक्रिया /
काम्योदकं सखिप्रेतस्वस्रीयश्वश्रुरर्त्विजां //
158.m: Such is the water rite for a deceased maternal grandfather or teacher. / Water is optionally offered for a deceased friend, a sister's son, mother-in-law, father-in-law, or officiating priests.

158.s:
apo naḥ śośucidayaṃ daśāhañca suto 'rpayet /
brāhmaṇe daśapiṇḍāḥ syuḥ kṣatriye dvādaśa smṛtāḥ //
158.d:
अपो नः शोशुचिदयं दशाहञ्च सुतो ऽर्पयेत् /
ब्राह्मणे दशपिण्डाः स्युः क्षत्रिये द्वादश स्मृताः //
158.m: Reciting "apo naḥ śośucad aghaṃ", the son should offer [water] for ten days. / For a Brahmin there should be ten funerary cakes, for a Kṣatriya twelve are prescribed,

158.s:
vaiśye pañcadaśa proktāḥ śūdre triṃśat prakīrtitā /
putro vā putrikānyo vā piṇḍaṃ dadyācca putravat //
158.d:
वैश्ये पञ्चदश प्रोक्ताः शूद्रे त्रिंशत् प्रकीर्तिता /
पुत्रो वा पुत्रिकान्यो वा पिण्डं दद्याच्च पुत्रवत् //
158.m: for a Vaiśya fifteen are stated, and for a Śūdra thirty are proclaimed. / A son, an appointed daughter, or another should offer the funerary cake like a son.

158.s:
vidiśya nimbapatrāṇi niyato dvāri veśmanaḥ /
ācamya cāgnimudakaṃ gomayaṃ gaurasarṣapān //
158.d:
विदिश्य निम्बपत्राणि नियतो द्वारि वेश्मनः /
आचम्य चाग्निमुदकं गोमयं गौरसर्षपान् //
158.m: Restrained at the doorway of the house, chewing neem leaves, / sipping water, touching fire, water, cow dung, and white mustard seeds,

158.s:
praviśeyuḥ samālabhya kṛtvāśmani padaṃ śanaiḥ /
akṣaralavaṇānnaḥ syur nirmāṃsā bhūmiśāyinaḥ //
158.d:
प्रविशेयुः समालभ्य कृत्वाश्मनि पदं शनैः /
अक्षरलवणान्नः स्युर् निर्मांसा भूमिशायिनः //
158.m: they should enter, placing their foot slowly upon a stone. / They should eat food without alkaline or salt, abstain from meat, and sleep on the ground,

158.s:
krītalabdhāśanāḥ snātā ādikartā daśāhakṛt /
abhāve brahmacārī tu kuryātpiṇḍodakādikaṃ //
158.d:
क्रीतलब्धाशनाः स्नाता आदिकर्ता दशाहकृत् /
अभावे ब्रह्मचारी तु कुर्यात्पिण्डोदकादिकं //
158.m: eating food that is bought or obtained [unasked], having bathed; the primary performer observes the ten days. / In the absence [of a son], a student of the Veda may perform the funerary cake, water offerings, and other rites.

158.s:
yathedaṃ śāvamāśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vidhīyate /
jananepyevaṃ syānnipuṇāṃ śuddhimicchatāṃ //
158.d:
यथेदं शावमाशौचं सपिण्डेषु विधीयते /
जननेप्येवं स्यान्निपुणां शुद्धिमिच्छतां //
158.m: Just as this ritual impurity from death is prescribed among sapindas, / so it should be upon a birth for those desiring complete purity.

158.s:
sarveṣāṃ śāvamāśaucaṃ mātāpitroś ca sūtakaṃ /
sūtakaṃ mātureva syādupaspṛśya pitā śuciḥ //
158.d:
सर्वेषां शावमाशौचं मातापित्रोश् च सूतकं /
सूतकं मातुरेव स्यादुपस्पृश्य पिता शुचिः //
158.m: For all relatives there is ritual impurity from death, but ritual impurity from birth applies to the mother and father; / ritual impurity from birth [properly] pertains only to the mother; the father is pure upon sipping water.

158.s:
putrajanmadine śrāddhaṃ kartavyamiti niścitaṃ /
tadahastatpradānārthaṃ gohiraṇyādivāsasāṃ //
158.d:
पुत्रजन्मदिने श्राद्धं कर्तव्यमिति निश्चितं /
तदहस्तत्प्रदानार्थं गोहिरण्यादिवाससां //
158.m: On the day of a son's birth, an ancestral rite must certainly be performed; / that day is for the purpose of giving gifts of cows, gold, garments, and the like.

158.s:
maraṇaṃ maraṇenaiva sūtakaṃ sūtakena tu /
ubhayorapi yat pūrvaṃ tenāśaucena śuddhyati //
158.d:
मरणं मरणेनैव सूतकं सूतकेन तु /
उभयोरपि यत् पूर्वं तेनाशौचेन शुद्ध्यति //
158.m: A death overlaps with a death, and a birth with a birth; / one is purified by that ritual impurity which occurred first among the two.

158.s:
sūtake mṛtakaṃ cetsyān mṛtake tvatha sūtakaṃ /
tatrādhikṛtya mṛtakaṃ śaucaṃ kuryānna sūtakaṃ //
158.d:
सूतके मृतकं चेत्स्यान् मृतके त्वथ सूतकं /
तत्राधिकृत्य मृतकं शौचं कुर्यान्न सूतकं //
158.m: If a death occurs during [impurity from] a birth, or a birth during [impurity from] a death, / one should observe ritual purity concerning the death, not the birth.

158.s:
samānaṃ laghvaśaucantu prathamena samāpayet /
:p 140
asamānaṃ dvitīyena dharmarājavaco yathā //
158.d:
समानं लघ्वशौचन्तु प्रथमेन समापयेत् /
:प् 140
असमानं द्वितीयेन धर्मराजवचो यथा //

158.s:
śāvāntaḥ śāva āyāte(1) pūrvāśaucena śuddhyati /
guruṇā laghu bādhyeta laghunā naiva tadguru //
158.d:
शावान्तः शाव आयाते(1) पूर्वाशौचेन शुद्ध्यति /
गुरुणा लघु बाध्येत लघुना नैव तद्गुरु //
158.m: When a death occurs within the period of ritual impurity for a death, one becomes pure by the first ritual impurity. / A lighter [period] is superseded by a heavier one; a heavier one is never [superseded] by a lighter.

158.s:
mṛtake sūtake vāpi rātrimadhye 'nyadāpatet /
taccheṣeṇaiva suddhyeran rātriśeṣe dvyahādhikāt //
158.d:
मृतके सूतके वापि रात्रिमध्ये ऽन्यदापतेत् /
तच्छेषेणैव सुद्ध्येरन् रात्रिशेषे द्व्यहाधिकात् //
158.m: If another [death] occurs during the night in the case of a death or birth, / they become pure with the remainder of that [period], or by two extra days if it falls at the end of the night.

158.s:
prabhāte yadyaśaucaṃ syācchuddheraṃś ca tribhirdinaiḥ /
ubhayatra daśāhāni kulasyānnaṃ na bhujyate //
158.d:
प्रभाते यद्यशौचं स्याच्छुद्धेरंश् च त्रिभिर्दिनैः /
उभयत्र दशाहानि कुलस्यान्नं न भुज्यते //
158.m: If ritual impurity arises at dawn, they become pure after three days. / In both cases, for ten days the family's food is not to be eaten.

158.s:
dānādi ninivarteta kulasyānnaṃ na bhujyate /
ajñāte pātakaṃ nādye bhokturekamaho 'nyathā(2) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe srāvādyaśaucaṃ nāma
aṣṭapañcāśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikonaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
asaṃskṛtādiśaucaṃ
158.d:
दानादि निनिवर्तेत कुलस्यान्नं न भुज्यते /
अज्ञाते पातकं नाद्ये भोक्तुरेकमहो ऽन्यथा(2) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे स्रावाद्यशौचं नाम
अष्टपञ्चाशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकोनषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
असंस्कृतादिशौचं
158.m:
Gifts and other [acts] cease; the family's food is not to be eaten. / If it is unknown, the eater incurs no sin; otherwise, [ritual impurity lasts] for one day.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-eighth chapter, entitled "Ritual Impurity Caused by Death and Other Occurrences," in the great Āgneya Purāṇa.
Now begins the one hundred and fifty-ninth chapter.
Ritual purity for the unconsecrated and others.

159.s:
puṣkara uvāca
saṃskṛtasyāsaṃskṛtasya svargo mokṣo harimmṛteḥ /
asthnāṅgaṅgāmbhasi kṣepāt pretasyābhyudayo bhavet //
:n
1 āpāta iti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 ananepyevamevaṃ syādityādiḥ, bhokturekamahonyathetyantaḥ
pāṭhaḥ gha.. , jha.. , ña.. pustakatrayeṣu nāsti
:p 141
159.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
संस्कृतस्यासंस्कृतस्य स्वर्गो मोक्षो हरिम्मृतेः /
अस्थ्नाङ्गङ्गाम्भसि क्षेपात् प्रेतस्याभ्युदयो भवेत् //
:न्
1 आपात इति ख.. , छ.. च
2 अननेप्येवमेवं स्यादित्यादिः, भोक्तुरेकमहोन्यथेत्यन्तः
पाठः घ.. , झ.. , ञ.. पुस्तकत्रयेषु नास्ति
:प् 141
159.m:
Puṣkara said: / For one consecrated or unconsecrated, heaven and liberation come from remembering Hari at death. / From casting the bones into the waters of the Gaṅgā, the deceased prospers.
[Apparatus]
1 āpātaḥ in manuscripts kha and cha.
2 The reading beginning with ananepyevamevaṃ syād and ending with bhokturekamahonyathā is absent in the three manuscripts gha, jha, and ña. / [Page 141]

159.s:
gaṅgātoye narasyāsthi yāvattāvaddivi sthatiḥ /
ātmanastyāgināṃ nāsti patitānāṃ tathā kriyā //
159.d:
गङ्गातोये नरस्यास्थि यावत्तावद्दिवि स्थतिः /
आत्मनस्त्यागिनां नास्ति पतितानां तथा क्रिया //
159.m: For as long as a person's bone remains in the water of the Gaṅgā, so long is their stay in heaven. / For those who commit suicide and those who have fallen, there are no rites.

159.s:
teṣāmapi tathā gāṅge toye 'sthnāṃ patanaṃ hitaṃ /
teṣāṃ dattaṃ jalaṃ cānnaṃ gagane tat pralīyate //
159.d:
तेषामपि तथा गाङ्गे तोये ऽस्थ्नां पतनं हितं /
तेषां दत्तं जलं चान्नं गगने तत् प्रलीयते //
159.m: Yet for them too, the falling of their bones into the water of the Gaṅgā is beneficial. / Water and food offered to them vanishes in the sky.

159.s:
anugraheṇa mahatā pretasya patitasya ca /
nārāyaṇabaliḥ kāryastenānugrahamaśnute //
159.d:
अनुग्रहेण महता प्रेतस्य पतितस्य च /
नारायणबलिः कार्यस्तेनानुग्रहमश्नुते //
159.m: Out of great compassion for a deceased person or a fallen person, / the Nārāyaṇa-bali should be performed; through it, one obtains grace.

159.s:
akṣayaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣastatra dattaṃ na naśyati /
patanātrāyate yasmāt tasmāt pātraṃ janārdanaḥ //
159.d:
अक्षयः पुण्डरीकाक्षस्तत्र दत्तं न नश्यति /
पतनात्रायते यस्मात् तस्मात् पात्रं जनार्दनः //
159.m: The lotus-eyed one is imperishable; what is offered there does not perish. / Because he protects from falling, Janārdana is the recipient.

159.s:
patatāṃ bhuktimuktyādiprada eko harirdhruvaṃ /
dṛṣṭvā lokān mriyamāṇān sahāyaṃ dharmamācaret //
159.d:
पततां भुक्तिमुक्त्यादिप्रद एको हरिर्ध्रुवं /
दृष्ट्वा लोकान् म्रियमाणान् सहायं धर्ममाचरेत् //
159.m: For those who are falling, Hari alone is certainly the bestower of worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Seeing people dying, one should practice dharma as one's companion.

159.s:
mṛto 'pi bāndhavaḥ śakto nānugantuṃ naraṃ mṛtaṃ /
jāyāvarjaṃ hi sarvasya yāmyaḥ panthā vibhidyate(1) //
159.d:
मृतो ऽपि बान्धवः शक्तो नानुगन्तुं नरं मृतं /
जायावर्जं हि सर्वस्य याम्यः पन्था विभिद्यते(1) //
159.m: Even a kinsman who has died cannot follow a dead man; / for, except for a wife, the path to Yama is different for everyone.

159.s:
dharma eko(2) vrajatyenaṃ yatra kvacana gāminaṃ /
śvaḥ kāryamadya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇikaṃ //
159.d:
धर्म एको(2) व्रजत्येनं यत्र क्वचन गामिनं /
श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकं //
159.m: Dharma alone accompanies him wherever he goes. / One should do today what is to be done tomorrow, and in the morning what is to be done in the afternoon.

159.s:
na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaḥ vāsya na vā kṛtaṃ /
kṣetrāpaṇagṛhāsaktamanyatragatamānasaṃ //
159.d:
न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतः वास्य न वा कृतं /
क्षेत्रापणगृहासक्तमन्यत्रगतमानसं //
159.m: For death does not wait to see whether a person's work is done or not done. / Death seizes and carries off one who is attached to fields, markets, and homes,

159.s:
vṛkīvīraṇamāsādya mṛtyurādāya gacchati /
na kālasya priyaḥ kaścid dveṣyaścāsya na vidyate //
159.d:
वृकीवीरणमासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति /
न कालस्य प्रियः कश्चिद् द्वेष्यश्चास्य न विद्यते //
159.m: whose mind is directed elsewhere, as a wolf seizes and carries off a sheep. / Death has no favorite, nor does he possess any enemy.

159.s:
āyuṣye karmaṇi kṣīṇe prasahya harite janaṃ /
nāprāptakālo mriyate biddhaḥ śaraśatair api //
159.d:
आयुष्ये कर्मणि क्षीणे प्रसह्य हरिते जनं /
नाप्राप्तकालो म्रियते बिद्धः शरशतैर् अपि //
159.m: When life-span and karmic merit are exhausted, he forcefully snatches the person away. / One whose time has not come does not die, even when pierced by hundreds of arrows;

159.s:
kuśāgreṇāpi saṃspṛṣṭaḥ prāptakālo na jīvati /
:n
1 panthā vibhajyate iti ga..
2 dharma eveti ja..
:p 142
auṣadhāni(1) na mantrādyāstrāyante mṛtyunānvitaṃ //
159.d:
कुशाग्रेणापि संस्पृष्टः प्राप्तकालो न जीवति /
:न्
1 पन्था विभज्यते इति ग..
2 धर्म एवेति ज..
:प् 142
औषधानि(1) न मन्त्राद्यास्त्रायन्ते मृत्युनान्वितं //
159.m:
one whose time has come does not live, even if merely touched by the tip of a kuśa blade.
[Apparatus]
1 panthā vibhajyate in manuscript ga.
2 dharma eva in manuscript ja. / [Page 142]
Medicines, mantras, and the like do not protect one overtaken by death.

159.s:
vatsavat prākṛtaṃ karma kartāraṃ vindati dhruvaṃ /
avyaktādi vyaktamadhyamavyaktanidhanaṃ jagat //
159.d:
वत्सवत् प्राकृतं कर्म कर्तारं विन्दति ध्रुवं /
अव्यक्तादि व्यक्तमध्यमव्यक्तनिधनं जगत् //
159.m: Past karma certainly finds its doer, just as a calf [finds its mother]. / The universe has an unmanifest beginning, a manifest middle, and an unmanifest end.

159.s:
kaumārādi yathā dehe tathā dehāntarāgamaḥ /
navamanyadyathā vastraṃ gṛhṇātyevaṃ śarīrikaṃ //
159.d:
कौमारादि यथा देहे तथा देहान्तरागमः /
नवमन्यद्यथा वस्त्रं गृह्णात्येवं शरीरिकं //
159.m: Just as childhood and [other stages occur] in the body, so is the arrival of another body. / Just as one takes on new, different clothing, so does the embodied self.

159.s:
dehī nityamabadhyo 'yaṃ yataḥ śokaṃ tatastyajet //15//
:e ity ādyāgneye mahāpurāṇe śaucaṃ
nāmaikonaṣṭyadhikataśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vānaprasthāśramaḥ
159.d:
देही नित्यमबध्यो ऽयं यतः शोकं ततस्त्यजेत् //15//
:ए इत्य् आद्याग्नेये महापुराणे शौचं
नामैकोनष्ट्यधिकतशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ षष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
वानप्रस्थाश्रमः
159.m:
Since this embodied self is eternally indestructible, one should therefore cast off grief.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-ninth chapter, entitled "Ritual Purity," in the great Āgneya Purāṇa.
Now begins the one hundred and sixtieth chapter.
The stage of life of the forest hermit.

160.s:
puṣkara uvāca
vānaprasthayatīnāñca(2) dharmaṃ vakṣye 'dhunā śṛṇu /
jaṭitvamagnihotritvaṃ bhūśayyājinadhāraṇaṃ //
160.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
वानप्रस्थयतीनाञ्च(2) धर्मं वक्ष्ये ऽधुना शृणु /
जटित्वमग्निहोत्रित्वं भूशय्याजिनधारणं //
160.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall now declare the duty of forest hermits and ascetics; listen: / wearing matted hair, maintaining the sacred fire, sleeping on the ground, wearing an animal hide,

160.s:
vane vāsaḥ payomūlanīvāraphalavṛttitā /
pratigrahanivṛttiś ca triḥsnānaṃ brahmacāritā //
160.d:
वने वासः पयोमूलनीवारफलवृत्तिता /
प्रतिग्रहनिवृत्तिश् च त्रिःस्नानं ब्रह्मचारिता //
160.m: dwelling in the forest, subsisting on milk, roots, wild rice, and fruits, / abstaining from accepting gifts, bathing three times a day, practicing celibacy,

160.s:
devātithīnāṃ pūjā ca dharmo 'yaṃ vanavāsinaḥ /
:n
1 auṣadhādīti ka..
2 yatīnāntu iti ṅa..
:p 143
gṛhī hy apatyāpatyañca dṛṣṭvāraṇyaṃ(1) samāśrayet //
160.d:
देवातिथीनां पूजा च धर्मो ऽयं वनवासिनः /
:न्
1 औषधादीति क..
2 यतीनान्तु इति ङ..
:प् 143
गृही ह्य् अपत्यापत्यञ्च दृष्ट्वारण्यं(1) समाश्रयेत् //
160.m:
and worship of deities and guests—this is the duty of a forest dweller.
[Apparatus]
1 auṣadhādi in manuscript ka.
2 yatīnāntu in manuscript ṅa. / [Page 143]
Having seen the offspring of his offspring, a householder should indeed resort to the forest.

160.s:
tṛtīyamāyuṣo bhāgamekākī vā sabhāryakaḥ /
grīṣme pañcatapā nityaṃ varṣāsvabhrāvikāśikaḥ //
160.d:
तृतीयमायुषो भागमेकाकी वा सभार्यकः /
ग्रीष्मे पञ्चतपा नित्यं वर्षास्वभ्राविकाशिकः //
160.m: [He should spend] the third part of his life alone or with his wife; / in summer, constantly practicing the five fires penance; in the rainy season, exposed to the rain from the clouds;

160.s:
ārdravāsāś ca hemante tapaścograñcaredbalī(2) /
aparāvṛttimāsthāya vrajeddiśamajihmagaḥ(3) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vānaprasthāśramo nāma
ṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yatidharmaḥ
160.d:
आर्द्रवासाश् च हेमन्ते तपश्चोग्रञ्चरेद्बली(2) /
अपरावृत्तिमास्थाय व्रजेद्दिशमजिह्मगः(3) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे वानप्रस्थाश्रमो नाम
षष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
यतिधर्मः
160.m:
in winter, wearing wet clothes; and a strong man should practice severe ascetic austerity. / Resolving upon never returning, he should go straight in whatever direction he chooses.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixtieth chapter, entitled "The Stage of Life of the Forest Hermit," in the great Āgneya Purāṇa.
Now begins the one hundred and sixty-first chapter.
The duty of an ascetic.

161.s:
puṣkara uvāca
yatirdharmaṃ pravakṣyāmi jñānamokṣādidarśakaṃ /
caturdhamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ prāpya saṅgāt parivarjayet(4) //
161.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
यतिर्धर्मं प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानमोक्षादिदर्शकं /
चतुर्धमायुषो भागं प्राप्य सङ्गात् परिवर्जयेत्(4) //
161.m: Puṣkara said: / I will proclaim the duty of an ascetic, which leads to knowledge, liberation, and the like. / Having reached the fourth portion of life, he should completely abandon attachments.

161.s:
yadahni virajeddhīrastadahni(5) ca parivrajet /
prajāpatyāṃ nirūpyeṣṭiṃ sarvadevasadakṣiṇāṃ //
161.d:
यदह्नि विरजेद्धीरस्तदह्नि(5) च परिव्रजेत् /
प्रजापत्यां निरूप्येष्टिं सर्वदेवसदक्षिणां //
161.m: On whichever day the wise man becomes detached, on that day he should renounce the world. / Having performed the sacrifice to Prajāpati with all his possessions given as sacrificial fee,

161.s:
ātmanyagnīn samāropya pravrajedbrāhmaṇo gṛhāt /
:n
1 dṛṣṭvāvaśyamiti ṅa..
2 tapaścograṃ vane carediti ṅa..
3 bhajeddiśamajimhaga iti ṅa..
4 saṅgān parityajediti ṅa..
5 virajedvāpi tadahni iti ṅa..
:p 144
eka eva carennityaṃ grāsamannāthamāśrayet //
161.d:
आत्मन्यग्नीन् समारोप्य प्रव्रजेद्ब्राह्मणो गृहात् /
:न्
1 दृष्ट्वावश्यमिति ङ..
2 तपश्चोग्रं वने चरेदिति ङ..
3 भजेद्दिशमजिम्हग इति ङ..
4 सङ्गान् परित्यजेदिति ङ..
5 विरजेद्वापि तदह्नि इति ङ..
:प् 144
एक एव चरेन्नित्यं ग्रासमन्नाथमाश्रयेत् //
161.m:
and having deposited the sacred fires within himself, the brāhmaṇa should renounce his home.
[Apparatus]
1 dṛṣṭvāvaśyam in manuscript ṅa.
2 tapaścograṃ vane caret in manuscript ṅa.
3 bhajeddiśamajimhagaḥ in manuscript ṅa.
4 saṅgān parityajet in manuscript ṅa.
5 virajedvāpi tadahni in manuscript ṅa. / [Page 144]
He should always wander alone and rely on mouthfuls of food only for sustenance.

161.s:
upekṣako 'siñcayiko munirjñānasamanvitaḥ /
kapālaṃ vṛkṣamūlañca(1) kucelamasahāyātā //
161.d:
उपेक्षको ऽसिञ्चयिको मुनिर्ज्ञानसमन्वितः /
कपालं वृक्षमूलञ्च(1) कुचेलमसहायाता //
161.m: Indifferent, accumulating nothing, a sage endowed with knowledge, / having a skull bowl, the foot of a tree, ragged clothes, solitude,

161.s:
samatā caiva sarvasminnetanmuktasya(2) lakṣaṇaṃ /
nābhinandena maraṇaṃ nābhinandeta jīvanaṃ(3) //
161.d:
समता चैव सर्वस्मिन्नेतन्मुक्तस्य(2) लक्षणं /
नाभिनन्देन मरणं नाभिनन्देत जीवनं(3) //
161.m: and equanimity towards everything—this is the characteristic of one who is liberated. / He should not rejoice at death, nor should he rejoice at life;

161.s:
kālameva pratīkṣeta nideśaṃ bhṛtako yathā /
dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyasetpādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pivet //
161.d:
कालमेव प्रतीक्षेत निदेशं भृतको यथा /
दृष्टिपूतं न्यसेत्पादं वस्त्रपूतं जलं पिवेत् //
161.m: he should simply await his time, just as a servant awaits his order. / He should place his foot down purified by sight, and drink water purified by a cloth.

161.s:
satyapūtāṃ vadedvācaṃ manaḥpūtaṃ samācaret /
alāvudārupatrāṇi mṛṇmayaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ yateḥ //
161.d:
सत्यपूतां वदेद्वाचं मनःपूतं समाचरेत् /
अलावुदारुपत्राणि मृण्मयं वैष्णवं यतेः //
161.m: He should speak words purified by truth; he should act [in a manner] purified by the mind. / [Vessels made of] bottle-gourds, wood, and earthenware belong to a renunciant devoted to Viṣṇu.

161.s:
vidhūme nyastamuṣale vyaṅgāre bhuktavajjane /
vṛtte śarāvasampāte bhikṣāṃ nityaṃ yatiś caret //
161.d:
विधूमे न्यस्तमुषले व्यङ्गारे भुक्तवज्जने /
वृत्ते शरावसम्पाते भिक्षां नित्यं यतिश् चरेत् //
161.m: When the smoke has cleared, the pestle is laid down, the embers are extinguished, and people have finished eating, / when the clearing away of bowls is completed, the renunciant should always wander for alms.

161.s:
madhūkaramasaṅkliptaṃ prākpraṇītamayācitaṃ /
tātkālikañcopapannaṃ bhaikṣaṃ pañcavidhaṃ smṛtaṃ //
161.d:
मधूकरमसङ्क्लिप्तं प्राक्प्रणीतमयाचितं /
तात्कालिकञ्चोपपन्नं भैक्षं पञ्चविधं स्मृतं //
161.m: Gathered like a bee, unplanned, previously prepared, unasked for, / and obtained at that very moment—alms is traditionally considered fivefold.

161.s:
pāṇipātrī bhavedvāpi pātre pātrāt samācaret /
avekṣeta gatiṃ nṝṇāṃ karmadoṣasamudbhavāṃ //
161.d:
पाणिपात्री भवेद्वापि पात्रे पात्रात् समाचरेत् /
अवेक्षेत गतिं नॄणां कर्मदोषसमुद्भवां //
161.m: He may use his hands as a bowl, or eat from bowl to bowl. / He should observe the fate of men arising from the faults of their actions.

161.s:
śuddhabhāvaś caredbharmaṃ yatra tatrāśrame rataḥ /
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu na liṅgaṃ dharmakāraṇaṃ //
161.d:
शुद्धभावश् चरेद्भर्मं यत्र तत्राश्रमे रतः /
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु न लिङ्गं धर्मकारणं //
161.m: Pure in intention, one should practice dharma, devoted to whatever stage of life [he is in], / equal toward all beings; the outward mark is not the cause of dharma.

161.s:
phalaṃ katakavṛkṣasya yadyapyambuprasādakaṃ /
na nāmagrahaṇādeva tasya vāri prasīdati //
:n
1 vṛkṣamūlāni kha.. , gha.. , cha.. , jha.. ca / vṛkṣamūlādi iti
ṭa..
2 etacchuddhasyeti ṅa..
3 jīvitamiti kha.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
:p 145
161.d:
फलं कतकवृक्षस्य यद्यप्यम्बुप्रसादकं /
न नामग्रहणादेव तस्य वारि प्रसीदति //
:न्
1 वृक्षमूलानि ख.. , घ.. , छ.. , झ.. च / वृक्षमूलादि इति
ट..
2 एतच्छुद्धस्येति ङ..
3 जीवितमिति ख.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. च
:प् 145
161.m:
Although the fruit of the clearing-nut tree purifies water, / water does not become clear merely by uttering its name.
[Footnotes]
1 "vṛkṣamūlāni" in manuscripts kha, gha, cha, and jha; "vṛkṣamūlādi" in ṭa.
2 "etacchuddhasya" in ṅa.
3 "jīvitam" in kha, gha, ṅa, cha, and ja. / [page 145]

161.s:
ajihmaḥ paṇḍakaḥ paṅgurandho badhira eva ca /
sadbhiś ca mucyate madbhirajñānāt saṃsṛto dvijaḥ //
161.d:
अजिह्मः पण्डकः पङ्गुरन्धो बधिर एव च /
सद्भिश् च मुच्यते मद्भिरज्ञानात् संसृतो द्विजः //
161.m: Straightforward, [acting as if] a eunuch, lame, blind, or deaf— / [such a person] is freed by the virtuous and wise; out of ignorance the twice-born transmigrates.

161.s:
ahni rātryāñca yān jantūn hinastyajñānato yatiḥ /
teṣāṃ snātvā viśuddhyarthaṃ prāṇāyāmān ṣaḍācaret(1) //
161.d:
अह्नि रात्र्याञ्च यान् जन्तून् हिनस्त्यज्ञानतो यतिः /
तेषां स्नात्वा विशुद्ध्यर्थं प्राणायामान् षडाचरेत्(1) //
161.m: The creatures that an ascetic kills out of ignorance by day or by night, / for their purification he should bathe and perform six breath-controls.

161.s:
asthisthūṇaṃ snāyuyutaṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepanaṃ /
carmāvanaddhaṃ durgandhaṃ pūrṇaṃ mūtrapurīṣayoḥ //
161.d:
अस्थिस्थूणं स्नायुयुतं मांसशोणितलेपनं /
चर्मावनद्धं दुर्गन्धं पूर्णं मूत्रपुरीषयोः //
161.m: Supported by pillars of bone, bound with sinews, plastered with flesh and blood, / covered with skin, foul-smelling, full of urine and feces,

161.s:
jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ rogāyatanamāturaṃ /
rajasvalamanityañca bhūtāvāsamimantyajet //
161.d:
जराशोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनमातुरं /
रजस्वलमनित्यञ्च भूतावासमिमन्त्यजेत् //
161.m: afflicted by old age and sorrow, an abode of disease, miserable, / tainted with impurity and impermanent: this dwelling-place of the elements one should abandon.

161.s:
dhṛtiḥ kṣamā damo 'steyaṃ(2) śaucamindriyanigrahaḥ /
hrīrvidyā satyamakrodho daśakaṃ dharmalakṣaṇaṃ //
161.d:
धृतिः क्षमा दमो ऽस्तेयं(2) शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः /
ह्रीर्विद्या सत्यमक्रोधो दशकं धर्मलक्षणं //
161.m: Steadfastness, forgiveness, self-restraint, non-stealing, ritual purity, control of the senses, / modesty, knowledge, truth, and absence of anger: this is the tenfold mark of dharma.

161.s:
caturvidhaṃ bhaikṣavastu kuṭīrakavahūdake /
haṃsaḥ paramahaṃsaś ca yo yaḥ paścāt sa uttamaḥ //
161.d:
चतुर्विधं भैक्षवस्तु कुटीरकवहूदके /
हंसः परमहंसश् च यो यः पश्चात् स उत्तमः //
161.m: The mendicant [stage] is of four kinds: the Kuṭīcaka, the Bahūdaka, / the Haṃsa, and the Paramahaṃsa; each later one is superior [to the previous].

161.s:
ekadaṇḍī tridaṇḍī vā(3) yogī mucyate bandhanāt /
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryāparigrahau //
161.d:
एकदण्डी त्रिदण्डी वा(3) योगी मुच्यते बन्धनात् /
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहौ //
161.m: Bearing a single staff or bearing three staves, the yogin is released from bondage. / Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness:

161.s:
yamāḥ pañcātha niyamāḥ śaucaṃ santoṣaṇantapaḥ /
svādhyāyeśvarapūjā ca padmakādyāsanaṃ yateḥ(4) //
161.d:
यमाः पञ्चाथ नियमाः शौचं सन्तोषणन्तपः /
स्वाध्यायेश्वरपूजा च पद्मकाद्यासनं यतेः(4) //
161.m: these are the five restraints; then the observances: ritual purity, contentment, ascetic austerity, / Vedic study, and worship of God; and the lotus posture and others for an ascetic.

161.s:
prāṇāyāmastu dvividhaḥ sa garbho 'garbha eva ca /
japadhyānayuto garbho viparītastvagarbhakaḥ //
161.d:
प्राणायामस्तु द्विविधः स गर्भो ऽगर्भ एव च /
जपध्यानयुतो गर्भो विपरीतस्त्वगर्भकः //
161.m: Breath-control is of two kinds: with seed and without seed; / accompanied by recitation and meditation it is with seed, while the opposite is without seed.

161.s:
pratyekaṃ trividhaṃ sopi pūrakumbhakarecakaiḥ /
pūraṇāt pūrako vāyor niś calatvācca kumbhakaḥ //
:n
1 samācarediti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 dayāsteyamiti ṅa..
3 tridaṇḍī ceti ṅa..
4 padmakādyāsanaṃ mahat iti ṭa..
:p 146
161.d:
प्रत्येकं त्रिविधं सोपि पूरकुम्भकरेचकैः /
पूरणात् पूरको वायोर् निश् चलत्वाच्च कुम्भकः //
:न्
1 समाचरेदिति ख.. , छ.. च
2 दयास्तेयमिति ङ..
3 त्रिदण्डी चेति ङ..
4 पद्मकाद्यासनं महत् इति ट..
:प् 146
161.m:
Each [kind] is also threefold: through inhalation, retention, and exhalation; / it is an inhalation from filling with air, and a retention from [air's] motionless state;
[Footnotes]
1 "samācaret" in kha and cha.
2 "dayāsteyam" in ṅa.
3 "tridaṇḍī ca" in ṅa.
4 "padmakādyāsanaṃ mahat" in ṭa. / [page 146]

161.s:
recanādrecakaḥ prokto mātrābhedena ca tridhā /
dvādaśāttu caturviṃśaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśanmātriko 'paraḥ //
161.d:
रेचनाद्रेचकः प्रोक्तो मात्राभेदेन च त्रिधा /
द्वादशात्तु चतुर्विंशः षट्त्रिंशन्मात्रिको ऽपरः //
161.m: it is called an exhalation from expelling [the air]; and it is threefold by difference of duration: / one of twelve [measures], another of twenty-four, and another consisting of thirty-six measures.

161.s:
tālo laghvakṣaro mātrā praṇavādi carecchanaiḥ /
pratyāhāro jāpakānāṃ dhyānamīśvaracintanaṃ //
161.d:
तालो लघ्वक्षरो मात्रा प्रणवादि चरेच्छनैः /
प्रत्याहारो जापकानां ध्यानमीश्वरचिन्तनं //
161.m: A measure is the duration of a short syllable; one should practice slowly with the praṇava and the like. / Withdrawal of the senses belongs to those who recite; meditation is contemplation of God.

161.s:
manodhṛtirdhāraṇā syāt samādhirbrahmaṇi sthitiḥ /
ayamātmā paraṃ brahma satyaṃ jñānamanantakaṃ //
161.d:
मनोधृतिर्धारणा स्यात् समाधिर्ब्रह्मणि स्थितिः /
अयमात्मा परं ब्रह्म सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तकं //
161.m: Fixation of the mind is concentration; absorption is abiding in Brahman: / "This self is the supreme Brahman, truth, knowledge, endless,

161.s:
vijñānamānandaṃ brahma tattvamasya.ahamasmi tat /
param brahma jyotirātmā vāsudevo vimukta oṃ //
161.d:
विज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमस्य.अहमस्मि तत् /
परम् ब्रह्म ज्योतिरात्मा वासुदेवो विमुक्त ओं //
161.m: consciousness, bliss, Brahman; you are that; I am that; / the supreme Brahman, the light, the Self, Vāsudeva, liberated, Oṃ,

161.s:
dehendriyamanobuddhiprāṇāhaṅkāravarjitaṃ /
jāgratsvapnasusuptyādimuktaṃ(1) brahma turoyakaṃ //
161.d:
देहेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिप्राणाहङ्कारवर्जितं /
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुसुप्त्यादिमुक्तं(1) ब्रह्म तुरोयकं //
161.m: devoid of body, sense-organs, mind, intellect, vital breath, and ego, / freed from waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the rest: Brahman, the fourth [state],

161.s:
nityaśuddhabuddhayuktasatyamānandamadvayaṃ(2) /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirakṣaraṃ sarvagaṃ hariḥ //
161.d:
नित्यशुद्धबुद्धयुक्तसत्यमानन्दमद्वयं(2) /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिरक्षरं सर्वगं हरिः //
161.m: ever pure, endowed with awakening, truth, bliss, non-dual; / I am Brahman, the supreme light, the imperishable, all-pervading Hari,

161.s:
so 'sāvādityapuruṣaḥ so 'sāvahamakhaṇḍa oṃ /
sarvārambhaparityāgī samaduḥkhasukhaṃ kṣamī //
161.d:
सो ऽसावादित्यपुरुषः सो ऽसावहमखण्ड ओं /
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी समदुःखसुखं क्षमी //
161.m: that Person in the sun is he, that am I, undivided, Oṃ." / Abandoning all undertakings, equal in sorrow and joy, forgiving,

161.s:
bhāvaśuddhaś ca brahmāṇḍaṃ bhittvā brahma bhavennaraḥ /
āṣaḍhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāñca cāturmāsyaṃ vratañcaret //
161.d:
भावशुद्धश् च ब्रह्माण्डं भित्त्वा ब्रह्म भवेन्नरः /
आषढ्यां पौर्णमास्याञ्च चातुर्मास्यं व्रतञ्चरेत् //
161.m: and pure in intention, a man, piercing the cosmic egg, becomes Brahman. / On the full moon day of Āṣāḍha he should observe the four-month votive observance.

161.s:
tato jrajet navamyādau hy ṛtusandhiṣu vāpayet /
prāyaścittaṃ yatīnāñca dhyānaṃ vāyuyamas tathā //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yatirdharmā
nāmaikaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 āgratsvapnasusuptyāntamuktamiti ṅa.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
2 ity āgneye aśaucanirṇaya ity ādiḥ, satyamānandamadvayamityantaḥ
pāṭho ga.. pustake nāsti
:p 147
:ś atha dviṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dharmaśāstrakathanaṃ
161.d:
ततो ज्रजेत् नवम्यादौ ह्य् ऋतुसन्धिषु वापयेत् /
प्रायश्चित्तं यतीनाञ्च ध्यानं वायुयमस् तथा //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे यतिर्धर्मा
नामैकषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 आग्रत्स्वप्नसुसुप्त्यान्तमुक्तमिति ङ.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
2 इत्य् आग्नेये अशौचनिर्णय इत्य् आदिः, सत्यमानन्दमद्वयमित्यन्तः
पाठो ग.. पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 147
:श् अथ द्विषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
धर्मशास्त्रकथनं
161.m:
Then he should wander; on the ninth [day] and so forth, at the junctions of the seasons, he should have his hair shaved; / and for ascetics, expiation is meditation as well as control of the breath.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the one hundred and sixty-first chapter, entitled "The Duties of an Ascetic."
[Footnotes]
1 "jāgratsvapnasusuptyāntamuktam" in ṅa, cha, and ña.
2 The passage beginning "ity āgneye aśaucanirṇaya" and ending "satyamānandamadvayam" is missing in manuscript ga. / [page 147]
Now the one hundred and sixty-second chapter.
The Exposition of the Dharmaśāstras.

162.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
मनुर्विष्णुर्याज्ञवल्को हारीतो ऽत्रिर्यमो ऽङिगिराः /
वसिष्ठदक्षसंवर्तशातातपपराशराः //
162.m: Puṣkara said: / Manu, Viṣṇu, Yājñavalkya, Hārīta, Atri, Yama, Aṅgiras, / Vasiṣṭha, Dakṣa, Saṃvarta, Śātātapa, Parāśara,

162.s:
āpastambośanovyāsāḥ kātyayanabṛhaspatī /
gotamaḥ śaṅkhalikhitau dharmamete yathābruvan //
162.d:
आपस्तम्बोशनोव्यासाः कात्ययनबृहस्पती /
गोतमः शङ्खलिखितौ धर्ममेते यथाब्रुवन् //
162.m: Āpastamba, Uśanas, Vyāsa, Kātyāyana, Bṛhaspati, / Gautama, Śaṅkha, and Likhita—as these declared dharma,

162.s:
tathā vakṣye samāsena bhuktimuktipradaṃ śṛṇu /
pravṛttañca nivṛttañca dvividhaṅkarma vaidikaṃ //
162.d:
तथा वक्ष्ये समासेन भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं शृणु /
प्रवृत्तञ्च निवृत्तञ्च द्विविधङ्कर्म वैदिकं //
162.m: so I shall declare it in brief, bestowing worldly enjoyment and liberation; listen! / Vedic action is of two kinds: directed toward engagement and directed toward cessation.

162.s:
kāmyaṃ karma pravṛttaṃ syānnivṛttaṃ jñānapūrvakaṃ /
vedābhyāsastapo jñānamindiyāṇāñca saṃyamaḥ //
162.d:
काम्यं कर्म प्रवृत्तं स्यान्निवृत्तं ज्ञानपूर्वकं /
वेदाभ्यासस्तपो ज्ञानमिन्दियाणाञ्च संयमः //
162.m: Action done with desire is directed toward engagement, while that preceded by knowledge is directed toward cessation. / Study of the Veda, ascetic austerity, knowledge, and restraint of the senses,

162.s:
ahiṃsā gurusevā ca niḥśreyasakaraṃ paraṃ /
sarveṣāmapi caiteṣāmatmajñānaṃ paraṃ smṛtaṃ //
162.d:
अहिंसा गुरुसेवा च निःश्रेयसकरं परं /
सर्वेषामपि चैतेषामत्मज्ञानं परं स्मृतं //
162.m: non-violence, and service to the guru are the supreme cause of the highest good. / And of all these, knowledge of the Self is declared to be supreme.

162.s:
taccagryaṃ sarvavidyānāṃ prāpyate hy amṛtaṃ tataḥ /
sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani //
162.d:
तच्चग्र्यं सर्वविद्यानां प्राप्यते ह्य् अमृतं ततः /
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि //
162.m: For that is the foremost of all sciences; immortality is indeed attained from it. / Seeing the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self

162.s:
samampaśyannātmayājī svārājyamadhigacchati /
ātmajñāne same ca syādvedābhyāse ca yatnavān //
162.d:
समम्पश्यन्नात्मयाजी स्वाराज्यमधिगच्छति /
आत्मज्ञाने समे च स्याद्वेदाभ्यासे च यत्नवान् //
162.m: equally, one who sacrifices to the Self attains autonomy. / One should be steadfast in knowledge of the Self and equanimity, and diligent in the study of the Veda.

162.s:
etaddvijanmasāmarthyaṃ(1) brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ /
:n
1 etaddvijanmasāgryamiti kha.. , ṅa.. , jha.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca /
etaddvijanmasāmagrīti gha.
:p 148
vedaśāstrārthatattvajño yatra tatrāśrame vasan //
162.d:
एतद्द्विजन्मसामर्थ्यं(1) ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः /
:न्
1 एतद्द्विजन्मसाग्र्यमिति ख.. , ङ.. , झ.. , ञ.. , ट.. च /
एतद्द्विजन्मसामग्रीति घ.
:प् 148
वेदशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञो यत्र तत्राश्रमे वसन् //
162.m:
This is the capability of the twice-born, especially of a brāhmaṇa,
[Footnotes]
1 "etaddvijanmasāgryam" in kha, ṅa, jha, ña, and ṭa; "etaddvijanmasāmagrī" in gha. / [page 148]
knowing the true meaning of the Veda and the Śāstras, residing in whatever stage of life [he is in].

162.s:
ihaiva loke tiṣṭhan hi brahmabhūyāya kalpyate(1) /
svādhyāyānāmupākarma śrāvaṇyāṃ śrāvaṇena tu //
162.d:
इहैव लोके तिष्ठन् हि ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्प्यते(1) /
स्वाध्यायानामुपाकर्म श्रावण्यां श्रावणेन तु //
162.m: Abiding right here in this world, he is fit to become Brahman. / The commencement rite of Vedic studies [is performed] on the full moon day of Śrāvaṇa, under [the asterism] Śravaṇa,

162.s:
haste cauṣadhivāre ca pañcamyāṃ śrāvaṇasya vā /
pauṣamāsasya rohiṇyāmaṣṭakāyāmathāpi vā //
162.d:
हस्ते चौषधिवारे च पञ्चम्यां श्रावणस्य वा /
पौषमासस्य रोहिण्यामष्टकायामथापि वा //
162.m: or on [the asterism] Hasta, on the day of herbs, or on the fifth lunar day of Śrāvaṇa; / or on [the asterism] Rohiṇī in the month of Pauṣa, or on an aṣṭakā day,

162.s:
jalānte chandasāṅkuryādutsargaṃ vidhivadvahiḥ /
tryahaṃ preteṣvanadhyāyaḥ śiṣyartviggurubandhuṣu //
162.d:
जलान्ते छन्दसाङ्कुर्यादुत्सर्गं विधिवद्वहिः /
त्र्यहं प्रेतेष्वनध्यायः शिष्यर्त्विग्गुरुबन्धुषु //
162.m: he should perform the suspension rite of the metres outdoors near water according to the rule. / There is a suspension of study for three days when pupils, officiating priests, gurus, or relatives have died,

162.s:
upākarmaṇi cotsargaṃ svaśākhāśrotriye tathā(2) /
sandhyāgarjitanirghāte bhūkampolkānipātane //
162.d:
उपाकर्मणि चोत्सर्गं स्वशाखाश्रोत्रिये तथा(2) /
सन्ध्यागर्जितनिर्घाते भूकम्पोल्कानिपातने //
162.m: and at the commencement and suspension rites, and likewise [on the death of] a Vedic scholar of one's own branch; / when there is thunder at twilight, a thunderbolt, an earthquake, or the fall of a meteor;

162.s:
samāpya vedaṃ hy aniśamāraṇyakamadhītya ca /
pañcadaśyāṃ caturdaśyāmaṣṭamyāṃ rāhusūtake //
162.d:
समाप्य वेदं ह्य् अनिशमारण्यकमधीत्य च /
पञ्चदश्यां चतुर्दश्यामष्टम्यां राहुसूतके //
162.m: and having completed the Veda, having studied the Āraṇyaka by night, / on the fifteenth, fourteenth, or eighth lunar day, during an eclipse of Rāhu,

162.s:
ṛtusandhiṣu bhuktvā vā śrādvikaṃ pratigṛhya ca /
paśumaṇḍūkanakulaśvāhimārjāraśūkaraiḥ(3) //
162.d:
ऋतुसन्धिषु भुक्त्वा वा श्राद्विकं प्रतिगृह्य च /
पशुमण्डूकनकुलश्वाहिमार्जारशूकरैः(3) //
162.m: or at the junctions of the seasons; having eaten food of an ancestral rite or accepted [a gift for it]; / when an interruption has been caused by an animal, a frog, a mongoose, a dog, a snake, a cat, or a boar,
[suspension lasts] for a day and a night; likewise at the fall or raising of Indra's banner; / when there is the sound of a dog, a jackal, a donkey, an owl, a wine-pipe, or a musical instrument;
near impure things, a corpse, a śūdra, an outcaste, a cremation ground, or a fallen person; / under inauspicious stars, during a confluence of lightning and thunder,
having eaten with wet hands, in water, at midnight, in a violent wind, / during a shower of dust, a burning of the directions, at twilight, in fog, or in times of fear,

162.s:
dhāvataḥ prāṇibādhe ca viśiṣṭe gṛhamāgate /
:n
1 brahmacaryāya kalpyate iti ṅa..
2 svaśākhāśrotriye mṛte iti gha.. , jha.. , ña.. , ṭa ca
3 śaśamārjāraśūkarair iti ṅa..
:p 149
kharoṣṭrayānahastyaśvanaukāvṛkṣādirohaṇe //
162.d:
धावतः प्राणिबाधे च विशिष्टे गृहमागते /
:न्
1 ब्रह्मचर्याय कल्प्यते इति ङ..
2 स्वशाखाश्रोत्रिये मृते इति घ.. , झ.. , ञ.. , ट च
3 शशमार्जारशूकरैर् इति ङ..
:प् 149
खरोष्ट्रयानहस्त्यश्वनौकावृक्षादिरोहणे //
162.m:
while running, when living beings are distressed, and when a distinguished guest has arrived at the house.
[Footnote]
1. ṅa reads 'brahmacaryāya kalpyate'.
2 "Upon the death of a Vedic scholar of one's own branch" in gha, jha, ña, and ṭa.
3 "By hares, cats, and pigs" in ṅa. / [p. 149]
[and] upon mounting a donkey, camel, vehicle, elephant, horse, boat, tree, and the like.

162.s:
saptatriṃśadanadhyāyānetāṃstātkālikānviduḥ
//19//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dharmaśāstraṃ nāma
dviṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha triṣaṣṭhyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śrāddhakalpakathanaṃ
162.d:
सप्तत्रिंशदनध्यायानेतांस्तात्कालिकान्विदुः
//19//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे धर्मशास्त्रं नाम
द्विषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिषष्ठ्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
श्राद्धकल्पकथनं
162.m:
These thirty-seven are known as temporary suspensions of Vedic study. //19
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-second chapter, entitled "Dharmaśāstra", in the Mahāpurāṇa called the Āgneya.
Now follows the one hundred and sixty-third chapter.
Explanation of the Rules for the Ancestral Rite

163.s:
puṣkara uvāca
śrāddhakalpaṃ pravakṣyāmi bhuktimuktipradaṃ śṛṇu /
nimantrya viprān pūrvedyuḥ svāgatenāparāhṇataḥ //
163.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
श्राद्धकल्पं प्रवक्ष्यामि भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं शृणु /
निमन्त्र्य विप्रान् पूर्वेद्युः स्वागतेनापराह्णतः //
163.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare the rules for the ancestral rite, which grant worldly enjoyment and liberation; listen. / Having invited the brāhmaṇas on the preceding day in the afternoon with a welcome,

163.s:
prācyopaveśayet pīṭhe yugmāndaive 'tha pitrake /
ayugmān prāṅmukhāndaive trīn paitre caikameva vā //
163.d:
प्राच्योपवेशयेत् पीठे युग्मान्दैवे ऽथ पित्रके /
अयुग्मान् प्राङ्मुखान्दैवे त्रीन् पैत्रे चैकमेव वा //
163.m: he should seat an even number facing east on a seat for the gods, and for the ancestors, / an odd number facing east for the gods, or three for the ancestors, or even one.

163.s:
mātāmahānāmapyevantantraṃ vā vaiśyadevikaṃ /
prāṇiprakṣālanaṃ dattvā viṣṭarārthaṃ kuśānapi //
163.d:
मातामहानामप्येवन्तन्त्रं वा वैश्यदेविकं /
प्राणिप्रक्षालनं दत्त्वा विष्टरार्थं कुशानपि //
163.m: The procedure is the same for the maternal grandfathers, or the rite for the gods may be common to both. / Having offered water for washing hands and also kuśa grass for seats,

163.s:
āvāhayedanujñāto viśve devāsa ity ṛcā /
yavairanvavakīryātha(?) bhājane sapavitrake //
163.d:
आवाहयेदनुज्ञातो विश्वे देवास इत्य् ऋचा /
यवैरन्ववकीर्याथ(?) भाजने सपवित्रके //
163.m: he should invoke [the deities], being permitted, with the verse "viśve devāsaḥ". / Having scattered barley grains into a vessel containing a purifier,

163.s:
śannodevyā payaḥ kṣiptvā yavosīti yavāṃs tathā /
yādivyā itimantreṇa haste hy arghaṃ vinikṣipet //
163.d:
शन्नोदेव्या पयः क्षिप्त्वा यवोसीति यवांस् तथा /
यादिव्या इतिमन्त्रेण हस्ते ह्य् अर्घं विनिक्षिपेत् //
163.m: pouring water with "śan no devī" and barley with "yavo 'si", / he should indeed pour the water offering into the hand with the mantra "yā divyāḥ".

163.s:
datvodakaṃ gandhamālyaṃ dhūpadānaṃ pradīpakaṃ /
apasavyaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā pitṝṇāmapradakṣiṇaṃ //
:p 150
163.d:
दत्वोदकं गन्धमाल्यं धूपदानं प्रदीपकं /
अपसव्यं ततः कृत्वा पितॄणामप्रदक्षिणं //
:प् 150
163.m:
Having offered water, perfume, a garland, the presentation of incense, and a lamp, / then placing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, he performs the rites counter-clockwise for the ancestors.
[p. 150]

163.s:
dviguṇāṃstu kuśān kṛtvā hy uśantastvetyṛcā pitṝn /
āvāhya tadanujñāto japedāyāntu nastataḥ //
163.d:
द्विगुणांस्तु कुशान् कृत्वा ह्य् उशन्तस्त्वेत्यृचा पितॄन् /
आवाह्य तदनुज्ञातो जपेदायान्तु नस्ततः //
163.m: Having folded kuśa grasses double, he invokes the ancestors with the verse "uśantas tvā"; / having been permitted by them, he should then recite "ā yāntu naḥ".

163.s:
yavārthāstu tilaiḥ kāryāḥ kuryādarghyādi pūrvavat /
dattvārghyaṃ saṃśravān śeṣān pātre kṛtvā vidhānataḥ //
163.d:
यवार्थास्तु तिलैः कार्याः कुर्यादर्घ्यादि पूर्ववत् /
दत्त्वार्घ्यं संश्रवान् शेषान् पात्रे कृत्वा विधानतः //
163.m: The purposes of barley are to be served with sesame seeds; he should perform the water offering and other rites as before. / Having offered the water offering and poured the remaining wash-waters into a vessel according to rule,

163.s:
pitṛbhyaḥ sthānamasīti nyubjaṃ pātraṃ karotyadhaḥ /
agnau kariṣya ādāya pṛcchatyannaṃ ghṛtaplutaṃ //
163.d:
पितृभ्यः स्थानमसीति न्युब्जं पात्रं करोत्यधः /
अग्नौ करिष्य आदाय पृच्छत्यन्नं घृतप्लुतं //
163.m: he turns the vessel upside down below with "pitṛbhyaḥ sthānam asi". / Taking food steeped in clarified butter, he asks, "I shall make the offering into fire."

163.s:
kuruṣveti hy anujñāto hutvāgnau pitṛyajñavat /
hutaśeṣaṃ pradadyāttu bhājaneṣu samāhitaḥ //
163.d:
कुरुष्वेति ह्य् अनुज्ञातो हुत्वाग्नौ पितृयज्ञवत् /
हुतशेषं प्रदद्यात्तु भाजनेषु समाहितः //
163.m: Having been permitted with "Perform it!", having offered into fire as in the ancestral sacrifice, / attentive, he should distribute what remains of the oblation into the dishes,

163.s:
yathālābhopapanneṣu raupyeṣu tu viśeṣataḥ /
datvānnaṃ pṛthivīpātramiti pātrābhimantraṇaṃ //
163.d:
यथालाभोपपन्नेषु रौप्येषु तु विशेषतः /
दत्वान्नं पृथिवीपात्रमिति पात्राभिमन्त्रणं //
163.m: which are obtained according to means, but especially silver ones. / Having offered the food, consecrating the vessel with "pṛthivīpātram",

163.s:
kṛtvedaṃ viṣṇurityanne dvijāṅguṣṭhaṃ niveśayet /
savyāhṛtikāṃ gāyatrīṃ madhuvātā iti tyacaṃ //
163.d:
कृत्वेदं विष्णुरित्यन्ने द्विजाङ्गुष्ठं निवेशयेत् /
सव्याहृतिकां गायत्रीं मधुवाता इति त्यचं //
163.m: and having recited "idam viṣṇuḥ", he should place the brāhmaṇa's thumb in the food. / Having recited the Gāyatrī with the sacred utterances and the triplet "madhu vātāḥ",

163.s:
japtvā yathāsukhaṃ vācyaṃ bhuñjīraṃste 'pi vāgyatāḥ /
annamiṣṭaṃ haviṣyañca dadyājjaptvā pavitrakaṃ //
163.d:
जप्त्वा यथासुखं वाच्यं भुञ्जीरंस्ते ऽपि वाग्यताः /
अन्नमिष्टं हविष्यञ्च दद्याज्जप्त्वा पवित्रकं //
163.m: he should say, "Eat at your ease," and they should eat, restraining their speech. / Having recited the purifier, he should give the food they desire and sacrificial food.

163.s:
annamādāya tṛptāḥ stha śeṣaṃ caivānnamasya ca /
tadannaṃ vikired bhūmau dadyāccāpaḥ sakṛt sakṛt //
163.d:
अन्नमादाय तृप्ताः स्थ शेषं चैवान्नमस्य च /
तदन्नं विकिरेद् भूमौ दद्याच्चापः सकृत् सकृत् //
163.m: Taking the food, [he asks,] "Are you satisfied?" and [they reply,] "Let the remainder of the food be his." / He should scatter that food on the ground and offer water once each time.

163.s:
sarvamannamupādāya satilaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ /
ucchiṣṭasannidhau piṇḍān pradadyāt pitṛyajñavat //
163.d:
सर्वमन्नमुपादाय सतिलं दक्षिणामुखः /
उच्छिष्टसन्निधौ पिण्डान् प्रदद्यात् पितृयज्ञवत् //
163.m: Taking all the food mixed with sesame, facing south, / he should offer rice balls near the leftovers, as in the ancestral sacrifice.

163.s:
mātāmahānāmapyevaṃ dadyādācamanaṃ tataḥ /
svasti vācyaṃ tataḥ kuryādakṣayyodakameva ca //
163.d:
मातामहानामप्येवं दद्यादाचमनं ततः /
स्वस्ति वाच्यं ततः कुर्यादक्षय्योदकमेव च //
163.m: He should do likewise for the maternal grandfathers; then he should give sipping-water. / Then he should recite the svasti-blessing and offer water for imperishable satisfaction.

163.s:
datvā tu dakṣiṇāṃ śaktyā svadhākāramudāharet /
vācyatāmityanujñātaḥ svapitṛbhyaḥ svadhocyatāṃ(1) //
:n
1 mātāmahānāmityādiḥ, svapitṛbhyaḥ svadhocyatāmityantaḥ
pāṭhaḥ jha.. pustake nāsti
:p 151
163.d:
दत्वा तु दक्षिणां शक्त्या स्वधाकारमुदाहरेत् /
वाच्यतामित्यनुज्ञातः स्वपितृभ्यः स्वधोच्यतां(1) //
:न्
1 मातामहानामित्यादिः, स्वपितृभ्यः स्वधोच्यतामित्यन्तः
पाठः झ.. पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 151
163.m:
Having given the sacrificial fee according to ability, he should utter the word "svadhā". / Being permitted with "Let it be uttered", [he says,] "Let svadhā be uttered to one's own ancestors!"
[Footnote]
1 The text beginning with "mātāmahānām" and ending with "svapitṛbhyaḥ svadhocyatām" is absent in manuscript jha. / [p. 151]

163.s:
kuryurastu svadhetyukte bhūmau siñcettato jalaṃ /
prīyantāmiti vā daivaṃ viśve devā jalaṃ dadet //
163.d:
कुर्युरस्तु स्वधेत्युक्ते भूमौ सिञ्चेत्ततो जलं /
प्रीयन्तामिति वा दैवं विश्वे देवा जलं ददेत् //
163.m: When they say, "Let there be svadhā," he should then sprinkle water on the ground, / or he should offer water to the divine All-Gods with "May they be pleased!"

163.s:
dātāro no 'bhivardhantāṃ vedāḥ santatireva ca /
śraddhā ca no māvyagamadbahudeyaṃ ca no .stviti //
163.d:
दातारो नो ऽभिवर्धन्तां वेदाः सन्ततिरेव च /
श्रद्धा च नो माव्यगमद्बहुदेयं च नो .स्त्विति //
163.m: "May our benefactors prosper, and also the Vedas and progeny; / and may our faith never waver, and may we have much to give."

163.s:
ityuktvā tu priyā vācaḥ praṇipatya visarjayet /
vāje vāja iti prītapitṛpūrvaṃ visarjanaṃ(1) //
163.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तु प्रिया वाचः प्रणिपत्य विसर्जयेत् /
वाजे वाज इति प्रीतपितृपूर्वं विसर्जनं(1) //
163.m: Having spoken these pleasant words and bowed down, he should dismiss them. / The dismissal is preceded by the ancestors being pleased, with "vāje vāje".

163.s:
yasmiṃstu saṃśravāḥ pūrvamarghapātre nipātitāḥ /
pitṛpātraṃ taduttānaṃ kṛtvā viprān visarjayet //
163.d:
यस्मिंस्तु संश्रवाः पूर्वमर्घपात्रे निपातिताः /
पितृपात्रं तदुत्तानं कृत्वा विप्रान् विसर्जयेत् //
163.m: Having turned upright that ancestral vessel in which the wash-waters were previously collected, / he should dismiss the brāhmaṇas.

163.s:
pradakṣiṇamanubrajya bhaktvā tu pitṛsevitaṃ /
brahmacārī bhavettāntu rajanīṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha //
163.d:
प्रदक्षिणमनुब्रज्य भक्त्वा तु पितृसेवितं /
ब्रह्मचारी भवेत्तान्तु रजनीं ब्राह्मणैः सह //
163.m: Having circumambulated them and walked after them, and having eaten what was enjoyed by the ancestors, / he should remain celibate for that night, together with the brāhmaṇas.

163.s:
evaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā vṛddhau nāndīmukhān pitṝn /
yajeta dadhikarkandhumiśrān piṇḍān yavaiḥ kriyā //
163.d:
एवं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा वृद्धौ नान्दीमुखान् पितॄन् /
यजेत दधिकर्कन्धुमिश्रान् पिण्डान् यवैः क्रिया //
163.m: Having circumambulated thus, at an auspicious occasion he should worship the Nāndīmukha ancestors / with rice balls mixed with curds and jujube fruits; the rite is performed with barley.

163.s:
ekoddiṣṭaṃ daivahīnamekārghaikapavitrakaṃ /
āvāhanāgnaukaraṇarahitaṃ hy apasavyavat //
163.d:
एकोद्दिष्टं दैवहीनमेकार्घैकपवित्रकं /
आवाहनाग्नौकरणरहितं ह्य् अपसव्यवत् //
163.m: The rite for a single ancestor is devoid of the rite for the gods, has a single water offering and a single purifier, / is without invocation and the offering into fire, and is performed with the sacred thread over the right shoulder.

163.s:
upatiṣṭhatāmityakṣayyasthāne pitṛvisarjane /
abhiramyatāmiti vaded brūyuste 'bhiratāḥ sma ha //
163.d:
उपतिष्ठतामित्यक्षय्यस्थाने पितृविसर्जने /
अभिरम्यतामिति वदेद् ब्रूयुस्ते ऽभिरताः स्म ह //
163.m: Instead of "akṣayya", he says "upatiṣṭhatām"; at the dismissal of the ancestors, / he should say, "Be pleased!", and they should say, "We are pleased."

163.s:
gandhodakatilair yuktaṃ kuryāt pātracatuṣṭayaṃ /
arghārthapitṛpātreṣu pretapātraṃ prasecayet //
163.d:
गन्धोदकतिलैर् युक्तं कुर्यात् पात्रचतुष्टयं /
अर्घार्थपितृपात्रेषु प्रेतपात्रं प्रसेचयेत् //
163.m: He should prepare four vessels supplied with scented water and sesame seeds; / into the ancestors' vessels meant for the water offering, he should pour the vessel for the newly deceased,

163.s:
ye samānā iti dvābhyāṃ śeṣaṃ pūrvavadācaret /
etat sapiṇḍīkaraṇamekoddiṣṭaṃ stiyā saha(2) //
163.d:
ये समाना इति द्वाभ्यां शेषं पूर्ववदाचरेत् /
एतत् सपिण्डीकरणमेकोद्दिष्टं स्तिया सह(2) //
163.m: with the two verses "ye samānāḥ"; the rest he should perform as before. / This is the rite of sapindisation, or the rite for a single deceased woman.

163.s:
arvāksapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ yasya saṃvatsarād bhavet /
:n
1 pitṛpūrvaṃ visarjayediti kha.. , cha.. , jha.. ca
2 stryā apīti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 152
tasyāpyannaṃ sodakumbhaṃ dadyāt saṃvatsaraṃ dvije //
163.d:
अर्वाक्सपिण्डीकरणं यस्य संवत्सराद् भवेत् /
:न्
1 पितृपूर्वं विसर्जयेदिति ख.. , छ.. , झ.. च
2 स्त्र्या अपीति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 152
तस्याप्यन्नं सोदकुम्भं दद्यात् संवत्सरं द्विजे //
163.m:
He whose sapindisation takes place within a year—
[Footnote]
1 "pitṛpūrvaṃ visarjayet" in kha, cha, and jha.
2 "stryā api" in kha and cha. / [p. 152]
food and a water-pot should be given to a brāhmaṇa for him for a year.

163.s:
mṛtāhani ca kartavyaṃ pratimāsantu vatsaraṃ /
pratisaṃvatsaraṃ kāryaṃ śrāddhaṃ vai māsikānnavat //
163.d:
मृताहनि च कर्तव्यं प्रतिमासन्तु वत्सरं /
प्रतिसंवत्सरं कार्यं श्राद्धं वै मासिकान्नवत् //
163.m: And the rite is to be performed on the day of death every month for a year; / an ancestral rite is to be performed every year, just like the monthly food.

163.s:
haviṣyānnena vai māsaṃ pāyasena tu vatsaraṃ /
mātsyahāriṇakaurabhraśākunacchāgapārṣataiḥ(1) //
163.d:
हविष्यान्नेन वै मासं पायसेन तु वत्सरं /
मात्स्यहारिणकौरभ्रशाकुनच्छागपार्षतैः(1) //
163.m: With sacrificial food [they are satisfied] for a month, but with milk-rice for a year; / with the meat of fish, deer, sheep, birds, goats, and spotted deer,

163.s:
aiṇarauravavārāhaśāśair māṃsair yathākramaṃ /
māsavṛddhyābhitṛpyanti dattair eva(2) pitāmahāḥ //
163.d:
ऐणरौरववाराहशाशैर् मांसैर् यथाक्रमं /
मासवृद्ध्याभितृप्यन्ति दत्तैर् एव(2) पितामहाः //
163.m: and with the meat of black buck, the ruru deer, wild boar, and hare, in that order, / the ancestors are completely satisfied with an increase of one month [for each] when they are offered.

163.s:
khaḍgāmiṣaṃ mahāśalkaṃ madhuyuktānnameva ca(3) /
lohāmiṣaṃ kālaśākaṃ māṃsaṃ vārdhīnasasya ca //
163.d:
खड्गामिषं महाशल्कं मधुयुक्तान्नमेव च(3) /
लोहामिषं कालशाकं मांसं वार्धीनसस्य च //
163.m: Rhinoceros meat, large-scaled fish, food mixed with honey, / red meat, kālaśāka greens, and the meat of a rhinoceros or old goat,

163.s:
yaddadāti gayāsthañca sarvamānantyamucyate(4) /
tathā varṣātrayodaśyāṃ maghāsu ca na saṃśayaḥ //
163.d:
यद्ददाति गयास्थञ्च सर्वमानन्त्यमुच्यते(4) /
तथा वर्षात्रयोदश्यां मघासु च न संशयः //
163.m: and whatever one gives while staying at Gayā—all that is declared to grant infinity; / likewise on the thirteenth lunar day of the rainy season and in the Maghā constellation, without doubt.

163.s:
kanyāṃ prajāṃ vandinaś ca paśūn mukhyān sutānapi /
ghṛtaṃ kṛṣiṃ ca vāṇijyaṃ dviśaphaikaśaphaṃ tathā //
163.d:
कन्यां प्रजां वन्दिनश् च पशून् मुख्यान् सुतानपि /
घृतं कृषिं च वाणिज्यं द्विशफैकशफं तथा //
163.m: A maiden, offspring, panegyrists, cattle, and pre-eminent sons, / clarified butter, agriculture, commerce, cloven-hoofed and single-hoofed beasts,

163.s:
brahmavarcasvinaḥ putrān svarṇarūpye sakupyake /
jñātiśraiṣṭhyaṃ sarvakāmānāpnoti śrāddhadaḥ sadā //
163.d:
ब्रह्मवर्चस्विनः पुत्रान् स्वर्णरूप्ये सकुप्यके /
ज्ञातिश्रैष्ठ्यं सर्वकामानाप्नोति श्राद्धदः सदा //
163.m: sons endowed with spiritual luster, gold and silver along with base metal, / pre-eminence among kin, and all desires the giver of ancestral rites obtains at all times.

163.s:
pratipatprabhṛtiṣvetānvarjayitvā caturdaśīṃ /
śastreṇa tu hatā ye vai teṣāṃ tatra pradīyate //
163.d:
प्रतिपत्प्रभृतिष्वेतान्वर्जयित्वा चतुर्दशीं /
शस्त्रेण तु हता ये वै तेषां तत्र प्रदीयते //
163.m: On these [days] beginning with the first lunar day, excluding the fourteenth lunar day; / but for those who were killed by a weapon, [an ancestral rite] is offered on that [fourteenth day].

163.s:
svargaṃ(5) hy apatyamojaś ca śauryaṃ kṣetraṃ balaṃ tathā /
putraśraiṣṭhyaṃ sasaubhāgyamapatyaṃ mukhyatāṃ sutān //
:n
1 mātsyāvihāriṇaurabhraśākunacchāgapārṣatair iti cha..
2 dattair iheti gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
3 madhumudgānnameva veti ṅa..
4 sarvamānantyamaśnute iti gha.. , ṅa.. ca
5 svarṇamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 153
163.d:
स्वर्गं(5) ह्य् अपत्यमोजश् च शौर्यं क्षेत्रं बलं तथा /
पुत्रश्रैष्ठ्यं ससौभाग्यमपत्यं मुख्यतां सुतान् //
:न्
1 मात्स्याविहारिणौरभ्रशाकुनच्छागपार्षतैर् इति छ..
2 दत्तैर् इहेति घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
3 मधुमुद्गान्नमेव वेति ङ..
4 सर्वमानन्त्यमश्नुते इति घ.. , ङ.. च
5 स्वर्णमिति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 153
163.m:
Heaven, offspring, vigor, valor, land, and strength, / superiority among sons, good fortune, progeny, eminence, sons,
[Footnote]
1 "mātsyāvihāriṇaurabhraśākunacchāgapārṣataiḥ" in cha.
2 "dattair iha" in gha, ṅa, and ña.
3 "madhumudgānnameva vā" in ṅa.
4 "sarvamānantyamaśnute" in gha and ṅa.
5 "svarṇam" in kha and cha. / [p. 153]

163.s:
pravṛttacakratāṃ putrān vāṇijyaṃ prasutāṃ tathā /
arogitvaṃ yaśo vītaśokatāṃ paramāṅgatiṃ //
163.d:
प्रवृत्तचक्रतां पुत्रान् वाणिज्यं प्रसुतां तथा /
अरोगित्वं यशो वीतशोकतां परमाङ्गतिं //
163.m: unobstructed authority, sons, trade, and progeny, / freedom from illness, fame, freedom from sorrow, the highest state,

163.s:
ghanaṃ vidyāṃ bhiṣakasiddhiṃ rūpyaṃ gāścāpyajāvikaṃ /
aśvānāyuś ca vidhivat yaḥ śrāddhaṃ samprayacchati //
163.d:
घनं विद्यां भिषकसिद्धिं रूप्यं गाश्चाप्यजाविकं /
अश्वानायुश् च विधिवत् यः श्राद्धं सम्प्रयच्छति //
163.m: wealth, knowledge, medical success, silver, cows, goats and sheep, / horses, and long life—[all these] he who properly performs the ancestral rite receives.

163.s:
kṛttikādibharaṇyante sa kāmānāpnuyādimān /
vasurudrāditisutāḥ pitaraḥ śrāddhadevatāḥ //
163.d:
कृत्तिकादिभरण्यन्ते स कामानाप्नुयादिमान् /
वसुरुद्रादितिसुताः पितरः श्राद्धदेवताः //
163.m: Beginning with Kṛttikā and ending with Bharaṇī, he obtains these desires. / The Vasus, Rudras, and sons of Aditi are the ancestors, the deities of the ancestral rite.

163.s:
prīṇayanti manuṣyāṇāṃ(1) pitṝn śrāddhena tarpitāḥ /
āyuḥ prajāṃ dhanaṃ(2) vidyāṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ sukhāni ca //
163.d:
प्रीणयन्ति मनुष्याणां(1) पितॄन् श्राद्धेन तर्पिताः /
आयुः प्रजां धनं(2) विद्यां स्वर्गं मोक्षं सुखानि च //
163.m: Gratified by the ancestral rite, they please the ancestors of men; / they grant long life, offspring, wealth, knowledge, heaven, liberation, pleasures,

163.s:
prayacchanti tathā rājyaṃ prītā nṝṇāṃ pitāmahāḥ(3) //42//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe śrāddhakalpo nāma
triṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha catuḥṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
navagrahahomaḥ
163.d:
प्रयच्छन्ति तथा राज्यं प्रीता नॄणां पितामहाः(3) //42//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे श्राद्धकल्पो नाम
त्रिषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुःषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
नवग्रहहोमः
163.m:
and likewise sovereignty, when pleased, to men's forefathers. //42
Thus ends the one hundred sixty-third chapter, entitled 'Rules for the Ancestral Rite', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the one hundred sixty-fourth chapter.
Fire Oblation to the Nine Planets

164.s:
puṣkara uvāca
śrīkāmaḥ śāntikāmo vā grahayajñaṃ samārabhet /
vṛṣṭyāyuḥpuṣṭikāmo vā tathaivābhicaran punaḥ //
:n
1 manuṣyādīniti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 āyuḥ prajñādhanamiti ja.. / āyuḥ prajāṃ balamiti gha..
3 prītāḥ pitṛpitāmahā iti ṅa..
:p 154
164.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
श्रीकामः शान्तिकामो वा ग्रहयज्ञं समारभेत् /
वृष्ट्यायुःपुष्टिकामो वा तथैवाभिचरन् पुनः //
:न्
1 मनुष्यादीनिति ख.. , छ.. च
2 आयुः प्रज्ञाधनमिति ज.. / आयुः प्रजां बलमिति घ..
3 प्रीताः पितृपितामहा इति ङ..
:प् 154
164.m:
Puṣkara said: / One who desires prosperity or peace should undertake the planetary sacrifice, / or one who desires rain, longevity, and nourishment, or likewise when performing sorcery.
[Footnote]
1. kha and cha read 'manuṣyādīn'.
2. ja reads 'āyuḥ prajñādhanaṃ'; gha reads 'āyuḥ prajāṃ balam'.
3. ṅa reads 'prītāḥ pitṛpitāmahāḥ'.

164.s:
sūryaḥ somo maṅgalaś ca budhaścātha bṛhaspatiḥ /
śukraḥ śanaiś caro rāhuḥ ketuśceti grahāḥ smṛtāḥ //
164.d:
सूर्यः सोमो मङ्गलश् च बुधश्चाथ बृहस्पतिः /
शुक्रः शनैश् चरो राहुः केतुश्चेति ग्रहाः स्मृताः //
164.m: The Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, and Jupiter, / Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu—these are known as the planets.

164.s:
tāmrakāt sphaṭikādraktacandanāt svarṇarkādubhau /
rajatādayasaḥ śīśāt grahāḥ kāryāḥ kramādime //
164.d:
ताम्रकात् स्फटिकाद्रक्तचन्दनात् स्वर्णर्कादुभौ /
रजतादयसः शीशात् ग्रहाः कार्याः क्रमादिमे //
164.m: From copper, crystal, red sandalwood, gold, and gold [and iron], both / from silver, iron, and lead, these planets are to be fashioned in order.

164.s:
suvarṇair vāyajellikhya gandhamaṇḍalakeṣu vā /
yathāvarṇaṃ pradeyāni vāsāṃsi kusumāni ca //
164.d:
सुवर्णैर् वायजेल्लिख्य गन्धमण्डलकेषु वा /
यथावर्णं प्रदेयानि वासांसि कुसुमानि च //
164.m: Or one should worship them drawn in gold, or upon scented circles. / Garments and flowers are to be presented according to their respective colours,

164.s:
gandhāś ca valayaś caiva dhūpo deyastu gugguluḥ /
kartavyā mantrayantaś ca caravaḥ pratidaivataṃ //
164.d:
गन्धाश् च वलयश् चैव धूपो देयस्तु गुग्गुलुः /
कर्तव्या मन्त्रयन्तश् च चरवः प्रतिदैवतं //
164.m: as well as perfumes and offerings; and the incense to be given is bdellium. / Boiled rice offerings must be prepared for each deity while reciting the mantras.

164.s:
ākṛṣṇena imaṃ devā agnirmūrdhā divaḥ kakut /
udbuddhyasveti ca ṛco yathāsaṅkhyaṃ prakīrtitāḥ //
164.d:
आकृष्णेन इमं देवा अग्निर्मूर्धा दिवः ककुत् /
उद्बुद्ध्यस्वेति च ऋचो यथासङ्ख्यं प्रकीर्तिताः //
164.m: "ākṛṣṇena", "imaṃ devāḥ", "agnirmūrdhā divaḥ kakut", / and "udbuddhyasva" are the verses proclaimed in order,

164.s:
vṛhaspate atiyadaryastathaivālpāt pariśrutaḥ /
śanno devīs tathā kāṇḍāt ketuṃ kṛnvannimās tathā //
164.d:
वृहस्पते अतियदर्यस्तथैवाल्पात् परिश्रुतः /
शन्नो देवीस् तथा काण्डात् केतुं कृन्वन्निमास् तथा //
164.m: and likewise "bṛhaspate atiyadaryaḥ", "annāt pariśrutaḥ", / "śaṃ no devīḥ", as well as "kāṇḍāt kāṇḍāt", and "ketuṃ kṛṇvan".

164.s:
arkaḥ pālāśaḥ khadiro hy apāmārgotha(1) pippalaḥ /
udumbaraḥ śamī durvā kuśāś ca samidhaḥ kramāt //
164.d:
अर्कः पालाशः खदिरो ह्य् अपामार्गोथ(1) पिप्पलः /
उदुम्बरः शमी दुर्वा कुशाश् च समिधः क्रमात् //
164.m: Calotropis, flame-of-the-forest, catechu, apāmārga, peepal, / cluster fig, śamī, dūrvā grass, and kuśa grass are the firewood sticks in order.

164.s:
ekaikasyātrāṣṭaśatamaṣṭāviṃśatireva vā /
hotavyā madhusarpirbhyāṃ dadhnā caiva samanvitāḥ //
164.d:
एकैकस्यात्राष्टशतमष्टाविंशतिरेव वा /
होतव्या मधुसर्पिर्भ्यां दध्ना चैव समन्विताः //
164.m: For each one, one hundred and eight, or indeed twenty-eight, / should be offered into the fire, combined with honey, clarified butter, and curd.

164.s:
guḍaudanaṃ pāyasaṃ ca haviṣyaṃ kṣīrayaṣṭikaṃ /
dadhyodanaṃ haviḥ pūpān māṃsaṃ citrānnameva ca //
164.d:
गुडौदनं पायसं च हविष्यं क्षीरयष्टिकं /
दध्योदनं हविः पूपान् मांसं चित्रान्नमेव च //
164.m: Rice with jaggery, milk porridge, sacrificial food, milk rice, / curd rice, clarified butter, cakes, meat, and variegated food,

164.s:
dadyādgrahakramadetaddvijebhyo bhojanaṃ budhaḥ /
