śaktito vā yathālābhaṃ satkṛtya vidhipūrvakaṃ //
164.d:
दद्याद्ग्रहक्रमदेतद्द्विजेभ्यो भोजनं बुधः /
शक्तितो वा यथालाभं सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकं //
164.m: the wise man should give as food to the twice-born in order of the planets, / or according to his capacity, or as available, having honoured them according to the rules.

164.s:
dhenuḥ śaṅkhas tathānaḍvān hema vāso hayas tathā /
:n
1 khadirastvapāmārgo 'theti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 155
kṛṣṇā gaurāyasaśchāga etā vai dakṣiṇāḥ kramāt //
164.d:
धेनुः शङ्खस् तथानड्वान् हेम वासो हयस् तथा /
:न्
1 खदिरस्त्वपामार्गो ऽथेति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 155
कृष्णा गौरायसश्छाग एता वै दक्षिणाः क्रमात् //
164.m:
A cow, a conch, an ox, gold, a garment, a horse,
[Footnote]
1. ga, gha, and ña read 'khadirastvapāmārgo 'tha'.
a black cow, iron, and a goat—these are indeed the sacrificial fees in order.

164.s:
yaś ca yasya yadā dūṣyaḥ(1) sa taṃ yatnena pūjayet /
brahmaṇaiṣāṃ varo dattaḥ pūjitāḥ pūjitasya ca //
164.d:
यश् च यस्य यदा दूष्यः(1) स तं यत्नेन पूजयेत् /
ब्रह्मणैषां वरो दत्तः पूजिताः पूजितस्य च //
164.m: Whichever planet is harmful to whomever at any time, he should diligently worship that one. / A boon was granted to them by Brahmā: when worshipped, [they bring prosperity] to the worshipper.

164.s:
grahādhīnā narendrāṇā(2) muchrayāḥ patanāni ca /
bhāvabhāvo ca jagatastasmāt pūjyatamā grahāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe navagrahahomo nāma
catuḥṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcaṣaṣtyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānādharmāḥ
164.d:
ग्रहाधीना नरेन्द्राणा(2) मुछ्रयाः पतनानि च /
भावभावो च जगतस्तस्मात् पूज्यतमा ग्रहाः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नवग्रहहोमो नाम
चतुःषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चषष्त्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानाधर्माः
164.m:
The rise and fall of kings are subject to the planets, / as are the existence and non-existence of the world; therefore, the planets are most worthy of worship.
Thus ends the one hundred sixty-fourth chapter, entitled 'Fire Oblation to the Nine Planets', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the one hundred sixty-fifth chapter.
Miscellaneous Duties

165.s:
agnir uvāca
dhyeya ātmā sthito yo 'sau hṛdaye dīpavat prabhuḥ /
ananyaviṣayaṃ kṛtvā mano buddhismṛtīndriyaṃ //
165.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ध्येय आत्मा स्थितो यो ऽसौ हृदये दीपवत् प्रभुः /
अनन्यविषयं कृत्वा मनो बुद्धिस्मृतीन्द्रियं //
165.m: Agni said: / The sovereign Self, situated like a lamp in the heart, is to be meditated upon, / having made the mind, intellect, memory, and sense faculties free of any other object.

165.s:
śrāddhantu dhyāyine deyaṃ(3) gavyaṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ payaḥ /
priyaṅgavo masūrāś ca vārtākuḥ kodravo na hi //
165.d:
श्राद्धन्तु ध्यायिने देयं(3) गव्यं दधि घृतं पयः /
प्रियङ्गवो मसूराश् च वार्ताकुः कोद्रवो न हि //
165.m: In an ancestral rite, what should be given to a meditator is produce of cows: curd, clarified butter, and milk; / priyaṅgu and lentils [may be given], but definitely not eggplants or kodo millet.

165.s:
saiṃhikayo yadā sūryaṃ grasate parvasandhiṣu /
hasticchāyā tu sā jñeyā śrāddhadānādike 'kṣyā //
:n
1 sadā duḥstha iti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 manuṣyāṇāmiti ṅa..
3 vyāpine deyamiti ṅa..
:p 156
165.d:
सैंहिकयो यदा सूर्यं ग्रसते पर्वसन्धिषु /
हस्तिच्छाया तु सा ज्ञेया श्राद्धदानादिके ऽक्ष्या //
:न्
1 सदा दुःस्थ इति ख.. , छ.. च
2 मनुष्याणामिति ङ..
3 व्यापिने देयमिति ङ..
:प् 156
165.m:
When the son of Siṃhikā eclipses the sun at the conjunctions of the lunar phases, / that is known as the shadow of the elephant, yielding imperishable fruit in ancestral rites, gifts, and the like.
[Footnote]
1. kha and cha read 'sadā duḥsthaḥ'.
2. ṅa reads 'manuṣyāṇām'.
3. ṅa reads 'vyāpine deyam'.

165.s:
pitre caiva yadā somo haṃse caiva kare sthite /
tithirvaivasvato nāma sā chāyā kuñjarasya tu //
165.d:
पित्रे चैव यदा सोमो हंसे चैव करे स्थिते /
तिथिर्वैवस्वतो नाम सा छाया कुञ्जरस्य तु //
165.m: When the moon is in the asterism of the ancestors and the sun is situated in Hasta, / on the lunar day called Vaivasvata—that indeed is the shadow of an elephant.

165.s:
agnaukaraṇaśeṣantu na dadyādvaiśvadevike /
agnyabhāve tu viprasya haste dadyāttu dakṣiṇe //
165.d:
अग्नौकरणशेषन्तु न दद्याद्वैश्वदेविके /
अग्न्यभावे तु विप्रस्य हस्ते दद्यात्तु दक्षिणे //
165.m: One should not give the remnant of the offering into the fire during the Vaiśvadeva rite; / but in the absence of the fire, he should place it in the right hand of a brāhmaṇa.

165.s:
na strī duṣyati jāreṇa na vipro vedakarmaṇā /
balātkāropabhuktā cedvairihastagatāpi vā(1) //
165.d:
न स्त्री दुष्यति जारेण न विप्रो वेदकर्मणा /
बलात्कारोपभुक्ता चेद्वैरिहस्तगतापि वा(1) //
165.m: A woman is not defiled by an adulterer, nor a brāhmaṇa by Vedic rites; / if she was enjoyed by force, or even fallen into the hands of an enemy,

165.s:
santyajed dūṣitānnārīmṛtukāle na śuddhyati /
ya ātmatryatirekeṇa dvitīyaṃ nātra paśyati(2) //
165.d:
सन्त्यजेद् दूषितान्नारीमृतुकाले न शुद्ध्यति /
य आत्मत्र्यतिरेकेण द्वितीयं नात्र पश्यति(2) //
165.m: one should not abandon the defiled woman; she becomes purified at the time of her period. / One who sees no second reality here apart from the Self—

165.s:
brahmabhūtaḥ sa eveha yogī cātmarato 'malaḥ /
viṣayendriyasaṃyogāt kecid yogaṃ vadanti vai //
165.d:
ब्रह्मभूतः स एवेह योगी चात्मरतो ऽमलः /
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगात् केचिद् योगं वदन्ति वै //
165.m: he alone becomes one with Brahman in this world, an unblemished yogi delighting in the Self. / Some indeed say that yoga is the union of the sense organs with their objects;

165.s:
adharmo dharmabuddhyā tu gṛhītastair apaṇḍitaiḥ /
ātmano manasaś caiva saṃyogañca tathā pare //
165.d:
अधर्मो धर्मबुद्ध्या तु गृहीतस्तैर् अपण्डितैः /
आत्मनो मनसश् चैव संयोगञ्च तथा परे //
165.m: unrighteousness was grasped by those foolish people with the notion that it is righteousness. / Others likewise [say it is] the union of the mind and the Self.

165.s:
vṛttihīnaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā kṣetrajñaṃ paramātmani /
ekīkṛtya vimucyeta bandhādyogo 'yamuttamaḥ //
165.d:
वृत्तिहीनं मनः कृत्वा क्षेत्रज्ञं परमात्मनि /
एकीकृत्य विमुच्येत बन्धाद्योगो ऽयमुत्तमः //
165.m: Having rendered the mind free of mental modifications, unifying the knower of the field / with the Supreme Self, one is liberated from bondage; this is the supreme yoga.

165.s:
kuṭumbaiḥ pañcabhiryāmaḥ ṣaṣṭhastatra mahattaraḥ /
devāsuramanuṣyair vā sa jetuṃ naiva śakyate(3) //
165.d:
कुटुम्बैः पञ्चभिर्यामः षष्ठस्तत्र महत्तरः /
देवासुरमनुष्यैर् वा स जेतुं नैव शक्यते(3) //
165.m: Restraint is [practised] with five family members; the sixth among them is the greatest. / It cannot be conquered even by gods, demons, or men.

165.s:
vahirmukhāni sarvāṇi kṛtvā cābhimukhāni vai /
manasyevendriyagrāmaṃ manaścātmani yojayet //
165.d:
वहिर्मुखानि सर्वाणि कृत्वा चाभिमुखानि वै /
मनस्येवेन्द्रियग्रामं मनश्चात्मनि योजयेत् //
165.m: Having turned all outward-facing senses toward the inside, / one should unite the collection of senses in the mind, and the mind in the Self.

165.s:
sarvabhāvavinirmuktaṃ kṣetrajñaṃ brahmaṇi nyaset /
etajjñānañca dhyānañca śeṣo 'nyo granthavistaraḥ(4) //
:n
1 caurahastagatāpi veti kha.. , gha.. , ña ca
2 dvitīyaṃ nānupaśyatīti gha.. , ṭa.. ca
3 sa jetuṃ na ca śakyata iti ga.. , ṅa.. ca
4 śeṣā ye granthavistarā iti ṅa
:p 157
165.d:
सर्वभावविनिर्मुक्तं क्षेत्रज्ञं ब्रह्मणि न्यसेत् /
एतज्ज्ञानञ्च ध्यानञ्च शेषो ऽन्यो ग्रन्थविस्तरः(4) //
:न्
1 चौरहस्तगतापि वेति ख.. , घ.. , ञ च
2 द्वितीयं नानुपश्यतीति घ.. , ट.. च
3 स जेतुं न च शक्यत इति ग.. , ङ.. च
4 शेषा ये ग्रन्थविस्तरा इति ङ
:प् 157
165.m:
One should place the knower of the field, freed from all states of being, into Brahman. / This is knowledge and meditation; the rest is merely the expansion of texts.
[Footnote]
1. kha, gha, and ña read 'caurahastagatāpi vā'.
2 "he sees no second" in manuscripts gha and ṭa
3 "and he cannot be conquered" in manuscripts ga and ṅa
4 "the remaining text-expansions" in manuscript ṅa

165.s:
yannāsti sarvalokasya tadastīti virudhyate /
kathyamānaṃ tathānyasya hṛdaye nāvatiṣṭhate //
165.d:
यन्नास्ति सर्वलोकस्य तदस्तीति विरुध्यते /
कथ्यमानं तथान्यस्य हृदये नावतिष्ठते //
165.m: What does not exist for the whole world is contradicted by [saying] "it exists"; / likewise, being spoken, it does not remain in the heart of another.

165.s:
asaṃvedyaṃ hi tad brahma(1) kumārī strīmukhaṃ yathā /
ayogī naiva jānāti jātyandho hi ghaṭaṃ yathā //
165.d:
असंवेद्यं हि तद् ब्रह्म(1) कुमारी स्त्रीमुखं यथा /
अयोगी नैव जानाति जात्यन्धो हि घटं यथा //
165.m: For that Brahman is incomprehensible, just as the face of a woman is to a virgin maiden; / a non-yogin never knows it, just as a man blind from birth does not know a jar.

165.s:
satryasantaṃ dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthānāccalati bhāskaraḥ /
eṣa me maṇḍalaṃ bhittvā paraṃ brahmādhigacchati //
165.d:
सत्र्यसन्तं द्विजं दृष्ट्वा स्थानाच्चलति भास्करः /
एष मे मण्डलं भित्त्वा परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति //
165.m: Seeing a twice-born man terrified of birth and death, the sun departs from its station: / "This man, piercing through my disc, attains the supreme Brahman."

165.s:
upavāsavratañcaiva snānantīrthaṃ phalantapaḥ /
dvijasampādanañcaiva sampannantasya tat phalaṃ //
165.d:
उपवासव्रतञ्चैव स्नानन्तीर्थं फलन्तपः /
द्विजसम्पादनञ्चैव सम्पन्नन्तस्य तत् फलं //
165.m: The votive observance of fasting, bathing at a sacred ford, ascetic austerity as fruit, / and making gifts to twice-born men—that fruit belongs to him fully accomplished.

165.s:
ekākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma prāṇāyāmaḥ parantapaḥ /
sāvitryāstu paraṃ nāsti pāvanaṃ paramaṃ smṛtaḥ //
165.d:
एकाक्षरं परं ब्रह्म प्राणायामः परन्तपः /
सावित्र्यास्तु परं नास्ति पावनं परमं स्मृतः //
165.m: The single syllable is the supreme Brahman; breath control is the highest ascetic austerity; / but there is nothing higher than the Sāvitrī: it is remembered as the supreme purifier.

165.s:
pūrvaṃ striyaḥ surair bhuktāḥ somagandharvavahnibhiḥ /
bhuñjate mānuṣāḥ paścānnaitā duṣyanti kenacit //
165.d:
पूर्वं स्त्रियः सुरैर् भुक्ताः सोमगन्धर्ववह्निभिः /
भुञ्जते मानुषाः पश्चान्नैता दुष्यन्ति केनचित् //
165.m: Formerly women were enjoyed by the gods: by Soma, the Gandharvas, and Agni; / men enjoy them afterwards; they are not defiled by anything.

165.s:
asavarṇena yo garbhaḥ strīṇāṃ yonau niṣicyate /
aśuddhā tu bhavennārī yāvatchalyaṃ na muñcati //
165.d:
असवर्णेन यो गर्भः स्त्रीणां योनौ निषिच्यते /
अशुद्धा तु भवेन्नारी यावत्छल्यं न मुञ्चति //
165.m: When a fetus is deposited in the womb of women by a man of different caste, / the woman remains impure as long as she has not released that dart.

165.s:
niḥsṛte tu tataḥ śalye rajasā śuddhyate tataḥ /
dhyānena sadṛśannāsti śodhanaṃ pāpakarmaṇāṃ //
165.d:
निःसृते तु ततः शल्ये रजसा शुद्ध्यते ततः /
ध्यानेन सदृशन्नास्ति शोधनं पापकर्मणां //
165.m: Once that dart has come forth, she is purified by her menstrual flux thereafter. / There is no purification for sinful actions equal to meditation:

165.s:
śvapākeṣvapi bhuñjāno dhyānena hi viśuddhyati /
ātmā dhyātā mano dhyānaṃ dhyeyo viṣṇuḥ phalaṃ hariḥ //
165.d:
श्वपाकेष्वपि भुञ्जानो ध्यानेन हि विशुद्ध्यति /
आत्मा ध्याता मनो ध्यानं ध्येयो विष्णुः फलं हरिः //
165.m: Even one eating among dog-cookers is purified by meditation. / The self is the meditator, the mind is meditation, Viṣṇu is the object of meditation, and Hari is the fruit.

165.s:
akṣayāya yatiḥ śrāddhe paṅktipāvanapāvanaḥ /
ārūḍho naiṣṭhikandharmaṃ yastu pracyavate dvijaḥ //
:n
1 svasaṃvedyaṃ hi tad brahma iti ga.. , ṅa.. ca / susaṃvedyaṃ hi tad brahma
iti ja.. , ṭa.. ca / svayaṃ vedyaṃ hi tad brahma iti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 158
165.d:
अक्षयाय यतिः श्राद्धे पङ्क्तिपावनपावनः /
आरूढो नैष्ठिकन्धर्मं यस्तु प्रच्यवते द्विजः //
:न्
1 स्वसंवेद्यं हि तद् ब्रह्म इति ग.. , ङ.. च / सुसंवेद्यं हि तद् ब्रह्म
इति ज.. , ट.. च / स्वयं वेद्यं हि तद् ब्रह्म इति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 158
165.m:
An ascetic at an ancestral rite secures imperishable [benefit]; he purifies even those who purify the row. / But whichever twice-born man, having mounted the life-long stage, falls away [from it]—
[Apparatus note]
1 "that Brahman is self-known" in manuscripts ga and ṅa; "that Brahman is easily known" in manuscripts ja and ṭa; "that Brahman is self-to-be-known" in manuscripts gha and ña

165.s:
prāyaścittaṃ na paśyāmi yena śuddhyetsa ātmahā /
ye ca pravrajitāḥ patnyāṃ yā caiṣāṃ vījasantatiḥ //
165.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं न पश्यामि येन शुद्ध्येत्स आत्महा /
ये च प्रव्रजिताः पत्न्यां या चैषां वीजसन्ततिः //
165.m: I see no expiation by which that slayer of the self might be purified. / And those [ascetics] who have had intercourse with a wife, and whatever seed-lineage is theirs,

165.s:
vidurā nāma caṇḍālā jāyante nātra saṃśayaḥ /
śatiko mriyate gṛdhraḥ śvāsau dvādaśikas tathā //
165.d:
विदुरा नाम चण्डाला जायन्ते नात्र संशयः /
शतिको म्रियते गृध्रः श्वासौ द्वादशिकस् तथा //
165.m: are born as Caṇḍālas named viduras; there is no doubt about this. / He dies as a vulture of a hundred years, and likewise as a dog of twelve years;

165.s:
bhāso viṃśativarṣāṇi sūkaro daśabhis tathā /
apuṣpo viphalo vṛkṣo jāyate kaṇṭakāvṛtaḥ //
165.d:
भासो विंशतिवर्षाणि सूकरो दशभिस् तथा /
अपुष्पो विफलो वृक्षो जायते कण्टकावृतः //
165.m: a bird of prey for twenty years, and a pig for ten; / he is born as a flowerless, fruitless tree covered in thorns.

165.s:
tato dāvāgnidagdhastu sthāṇurbhavati sānugaḥ /
tato varṣaśatānyaṣṭau dve tiṣṭhatyacetanaḥ //
165.d:
ततो दावाग्निदग्धस्तु स्थाणुर्भवति सानुगः /
ततो वर्षशतान्यष्टौ द्वे तिष्ठत्यचेतनः //
165.m: Then, burnt by a forest fire, he becomes a stump along with his shoots; / then he remains senseless for two hundred and eight years.

165.s:
pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu jāyate brahmarākṣasaḥ /
plavena labhate mokṣaṃ kulasyotsādanena vā //
165.d:
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु जायते ब्रह्मराक्षसः /
प्लवेन लभते मोक्षं कुलस्योत्सादनेन वा //
165.m: When a thousand years are completed, he is born as a Brahmarākṣasa; / he obtains release by a raft, or by the destruction of his family.

165.s:
yogameva niṣeveteta nānyaṃ mantramaghāpahaṃ //29//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānādhamā nāma
pañcaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ṣaṭṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
varṇadharmādikathanaṃ
165.d:
योगमेव निषेवेतेत नान्यं मन्त्रमघापहं //29//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानाधमा नाम
पञ्चषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ षट्षष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
वर्णधर्मादिकथनं
165.m:
One should devote oneself only to yoga, and to no other mantra, for removing sin.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the one hundred and sixty-fifth chapter, entitled "Various Dharmas."
Now, the one hundred and sixty-sixth chapter.
The statement on the duties of the castes and stages of life

166.s:
puṣkara uvāca
vedasmārtaṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmaṃ vai pañcadhā smṛtaṃ(1) /
varṇatvamekamāśritya yo 'dhikāraḥ pravartate //
:n
1 dharmaṃ vai paramāmṛtamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 159
166.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
वेदस्मार्तं प्रवक्ष्यामि धर्मं वै पञ्चधा स्मृतं(1) /
वर्णत्वमेकमाश्रित्य यो ऽधिकारः प्रवर्तते //
:न्
1 धर्मं वै परमामृतमिति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 159
166.m:
Puṣkara said: / I shall declare the dharma of the Veda and tradition, which is recognized as fivefold: / the duty that proceeds based on caste-status alone
[Apparatus note]
1 "dharma as the supreme nectar" in manuscripts kha and cha

166.s:
varṇadharṃaḥ sa vijñyeyo yathopanayanantriṣu /
yastvāśramaṃ samāśritya padārthaḥ saṃvidhīyate //
166.d:
वर्णधर्ंअः स विज्ञ्येयो यथोपनयनन्त्रिषु /
यस्त्वाश्रमं समाश्रित्य पदार्थः संविधीयते //
166.m: is to be known as caste duty, such as the sacred thread ceremony among the three [castes]; / but that obligation which is prescribed based on the stage of life

166.s:
ukta āśramadharmastu bhinnapiṇḍādiko yathā /
ubhayena nimittena yo vidhiḥ sampravartate //
166.d:
उक्त आश्रमधर्मस्तु भिन्नपिण्डादिको यथा /
उभयेन निमित्तेन यो विधिः सम्प्रवर्तते //
166.m: is declared to be stage-of-life duty, such as [carrying] a distinct water-pot and so forth. / An injunction that proceeds on account of both causes

166.s:
naimittikaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ prāyaścittavidhiryathā /
brahmacārī gṛhī cāpi vānaprastho yatir nṛpa //
166.d:
नैमित्तिकः स विज्ञेयः प्रायश्चित्तविधिर्यथा /
ब्रह्मचारी गृही चापि वानप्रस्थो यतिर् नृप //
166.m: is to be known as occasional, such as the rule for expiation. / The student, the householder, the forest hermit, and the ascetic, O king—

166.s:
ukta āśramadharmastu dharmaḥ syāt pañcadhā paraḥ(1) /
ṣāḍguṇyasyābhidhāne yo dṛṣṭārthaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ //
166.d:
उक्त आश्रमधर्मस्तु धर्मः स्यात् पञ्चधा परः(1) /
षाड्गुण्यस्याभिधाने यो दृष्टार्थः स उदाहृतः //
166.m: this is declared as stage-of-life duty; but other dharma may be fivefold: / That which is in the statement of the six measures of policy is cited as having a visible purpose;

166.s:
sa tredhā mantrayāgādyadṛṣṭārtha iti mānavāḥ /
ubhayārtho vyavahārastu daṇḍadhāraṇameva ca //
166.d:
स त्रेधा मन्त्रयागाद्यदृष्टार्थ इति मानवाः /
उभयार्थो व्यवहारस्तु दण्डधारणमेव च //
166.m: that which consists of mantras, sacrifices, and so forth is of invisible purpose, threefold, say the followers of Manu. / But judicial procedure and the infliction of punishment have both purposes.

166.s:
tulyārthānāṃ vikalpaḥ syād yāgamūlaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
vede tu vihito dharmaḥ smṛtau tādṛśa eva ca //
166.d:
तुल्यार्थानां विकल्पः स्याद् यागमूलः प्रकीर्तितः /
वेदे तु विहितो धर्मः स्मृतौ तादृश एव च //
166.m: Among [injunctions] having an equal purpose, there may be an option; it is stated to be rooted in sacrifice. / The dharma prescribed in the Veda is just of such a nature in tradition as well.

166.s:
anuvādaṃ smṛtiḥ sūte(2) kāryārthamiti mānavāḥ /
guṇārthaḥ parisaṅkhyārtho vānuvādo viśeṣataḥ(3) //
166.d:
अनुवादं स्मृतिः सूते(2) कार्यार्थमिति मानवाः /
गुणार्थः परिसङ्ख्यार्थो वानुवादो विशेषतः(3) //
166.m: Tradition brings forth restatement for the sake of the act, say the followers of Manu; / restatement is especially for the sake of a secondary attribute or for restrictive enumeration.

166.s:
viśeṣadṛṣṭa evāsau phalārtha iti mānavāḥ /
syādaṣṭacatvāriṃśadbhiḥ saṃskārair brahmalokagaḥ //
166.d:
विशेषदृष्ट एवासौ फलार्थ इति मानवाः /
स्यादष्टचत्वारिंशद्भिः संस्कारैर् ब्रह्मलोकगः //
166.m: Seen as a specific rule, it is for the sake of the fruit, say the followers of Manu. / By forty-eight sacraments one goes to the world of Brahmā:

166.s:
garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaḥ tataḥ /
jātakarma nāmakṛtirannaprāśanacūḍakaṃ //
166.d:
गर्भाधानं पुंसवनं सीमन्तोन्नयनः ततः /
जातकर्म नामकृतिरन्नप्राशनचूडकं //
166.m: Garbhādhāna, Puṃsavana, then Sīmantonnayana, / Jātakarman, Nāmakaraṇa, Annaprāśana, Cūḍākaraṇa,

166.s:
saṃskāraścopanayanaṃ vedavratacatuṣṭayaṃ /
snānaṃ svadharmacāriṇyā yogaḥ syādyajñapañcakaṃ //
:n
1 dharma eṣa sanātana iti ṅa..
2 arthavādaṃ smṛtiḥ sūta iti kha.. , cha.. ca
3 vārthavādo viśeṣata iti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 160
166.d:
संस्कारश्चोपनयनं वेदव्रतचतुष्टयं /
स्नानं स्वधर्मचारिण्या योगः स्याद्यज्ञपञ्चकं //
:न्
1 धर्म एष सनातन इति ङ..
2 अर्थवादं स्मृतिः सूत इति ख.. , छ.. च
3 वार्थवादो विशेषत इति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 160
166.m:
and the sacrament of Upanayana, the set of four Vedic vows, / the bath, union with a wife following her own duty, and the set of five sacrifices:
[Apparatus note]
1 "this eternal dharma" in manuscript ṅa
2 "tradition brings forth commendatory text" in manuscripts kha and cha
3 "or commendatory text especially" in manuscripts kha and cha

166.s:
devayajñaḥ pitṛyajño manuṣyabhūtayajñakau /
brahmayajñaḥ saptapākayajñasaṃsthāḥ puro 'ṣṭakāḥ //
166.d:
देवयज्ञः पितृयज्ञो मनुष्यभूतयज्ञकौ /
ब्रह्मयज्ञः सप्तपाकयज्ञसंस्थाः पुरो ऽष्टकाः //
166.m: the sacrifice to the gods, the sacrifice to the ancestors, the sacrifices to men and beings, / and the sacrifice to Brahman; the seven forms of cooked sacrifices: first, the Aṣṭakās,

166.s:
pārvaṇaśrāddhaṃ śrāvaṇyāgrahāyaṇī ca caitryapi /
āśvayujī saptahaviryajñasaṃsthāstataḥ smṛtāḥ //
166.d:
पार्वणश्राद्धं श्रावण्याग्रहायणी च चैत्र्यपि /
आश्वयुजी सप्तहविर्यज्ञसंस्थास्ततः स्मृताः //
166.m: the Pārvaṇa-śrāddha, the Śrāvaṇī, the Āgrahāyaṇī, the Caitrī, / and the Āśvayujī; then are remembered the seven forms of oblation-sacrifices:

166.s:
agnyādheyamagnihotraṃ(1) darśaḥ syāt paśubandhakaḥ /
cāturmāsyāgrahāyeṣṭirnirūḍhaḥ paśubandhakaḥ //
166.d:
अग्न्याधेयमग्निहोत्रं(1) दर्शः स्यात् पशुबन्धकः /
चातुर्मास्याग्रहायेष्टिर्निरूढः पशुबन्धकः //
166.m: Agnyādheya, Agnihotra, the New-moon rite, the animal sacrifice, / the Cāturmāsyas, the Āgrahāyaṇeṣṭi, the independent animal sacrifice,

166.s:
sautrāmaṇisaptasomasaṃsthāgniṣṭoma āditaḥ /
atyagniṣṭoma ukthaś ca ṣoḍaśī vājapeyakaḥ //
166.d:
सौत्रामणिसप्तसोमसंस्थाग्निष्टोम आदितः /
अत्यग्निष्टोम उक्थश् च षोडशी वाजपेयकः //
166.m: the Sautrāmaṇī; the seven forms of Soma sacrifice: beginning with Agniṣṭoma, / Atyagniṣṭoma, Ukthya, Ṣoḍaśin, Vājapeya,

166.s:
atirātrās tathā stoma aṣṭau cātmaguṇāstataḥ /
dayā kṣamānasūyā ca anāyāso 'tha maṅgalaṃ //
166.d:
अतिरात्रास् तथा स्तोम अष्टौ चात्मगुणास्ततः /
दया क्षमानसूया च अनायासो ऽथ मङ्गलं //
166.m: Atirātra, and Aptoryāma; then the eight virtues of the soul: / compassion, patience, freedom from envy, ease, auspiciousness,

166.s:
akārpaṇyāspṛhāśaucaṃ yasyaite sa paraṃ vrajet /
pracāre maithune caiva prasrāve dantadhāvane //
166.d:
अकार्पण्यास्पृहाशौचं यस्यैते स परं व्रजेत् /
प्रचारे मैथुने चैव प्रस्रावे दन्तधावने //
166.m: generosity, detachment, and ritual purity; one who possesses these goes to the supreme state. / In evacuation, in sexual union, in urination, and in cleaning teeth,

166.s:
snānabhojanakāle ca paṭsu maunaṃ samācaret /
punardānaṃ pṛthakpānamājyena yapasā niśi //
166.d:
स्नानभोजनकाले च पट्सु मौनं समाचरेत् /
पुनर्दानं पृथक्पानमाज्येन यपसा निशि //
166.m: and at the time of bathing and eating, one should observe silence in these six. / Repeated giving, separate drinking, with ghee, with water at night,

166.s:
dantacchedanamuṣṇaṃ ca sapta śaktuṣu varjayet /
snātvā puṣpaṃ na gṛhṇīyād devāyogyantadīritaṃ //
166.d:
दन्तच्छेदनमुष्णं च सप्त शक्तुषु वर्जयेत् /
स्नात्वा पुष्पं न गृह्णीयाद् देवायोग्यन्तदीरितं //
166.m: cutting with teeth, and warm: one should avoid these seven regarding roasted barley-flour. / Having bathed, one should not take flowers [for oneself]; that is declared unfit for the gods.

166.s:
anyagotropyasambaddhaḥ(2) pretasyāgnindadāti yaḥ /
piṇḍañcodakadānañca sa daśāhaṃ samāpayet //
166.d:
अन्यगोत्रोप्यसम्बद्धः(2) प्रेतस्याग्निन्ददाति यः /
पिण्डञ्चोदकदानञ्च स दशाहं समापयेत् //
166.m: Even a person of another clan, unrelated, who gives fire to a deceased person, / and gives the rice-ball and water offering, should complete the ten-day period.

166.s:
udakañca tṛṇaṃ bhasma dvārampanthāstathaiva ca /
:n
1 agnyādhānamagnihotramiti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 anyagotro 'nyasambandha iti kha.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 161
ebhirantaritaṃ kṛtvā paṅktidoṣo na vidyate //
166.d:
उदकञ्च तृणं भस्म द्वारम्पन्थास्तथैव च /
:न्
1 अग्न्याधानमग्निहोत्रमिति ख.. , छ.. च
2 अन्यगोत्रो ऽन्यसम्बन्ध इति ख.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 161
एभिरन्तरितं कृत्वा पङ्क्तिदोषो न विद्यते //
166.m:
Water, grass, ash, a doorway, and likewise a path:
[Apparatus note]
1 "Agnyādhāna, Agnihotra" in manuscripts kha and cha
2 "of another clan, having another relation" in manuscripts kha, gha, and ña
by making an intervention with these, no impurity of the dining-row occurs.

166.s:
pañca prāṇāhutīrdadyādanāmāṅguṣṭhayogataḥ
//22//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe varṇadharmādirnāma
ṣaṭṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
ayutalakṣakoṭihomāḥ
166.d:
पञ्च प्राणाहुतीर्दद्यादनामाङ्गुष्ठयोगतः
//22//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे वर्णधर्मादिर्नाम
षट्षष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
अयुतलक्षकोटिहोमाः
166.m:
One should offer five vital-breath oblations by joining the ring finger and the thumb.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the one hundred and sixty-sixth chapter, entitled "The Duties of the Castes and Stages of Life."
Now, the one hundred and sixty-seventh chapter.
[The fire oblations of] ten thousand, one hundred thousand, and ten million.

167.s:
agnir uvāca
śrīśāntivijayādyarthaṃ grahayajñaṃ punarvade /
grahayajño 'yutahomalakṣakoṭyātmakastridhā //
167.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
श्रीशान्तिविजयाद्यर्थं ग्रहयज्ञं पुनर्वदे /
ग्रहयज्ञो ऽयुतहोमलक्षकोट्यात्मकस्त्रिधा //
167.m:
Agni said:
For the sake of prosperity, peace, victory, and the like, I shall explain the sacrifice to the planets again. / The sacrifice to the planets is threefold, consisting of fire oblations of ten thousand, one hundred thousand, and ten million.

167.s:
vederaiśe hy agnikuṇḍād grahānāvāhya maṇḍale /
saumye gururbudhaś caiśe śukraḥ pūrvadale śaśī //
167.d:
वेदेरैशे ह्य् अग्निकुण्डाद् ग्रहानावाह्य मण्डले /
सौम्ये गुरुर्बुधश् चैशे शुक्रः पूर्वदले शशी //
167.m: Having invoked the planets on the maṇḍala with Vedic mantras to the northeast from the fire-pit: / Jupiter in the north, Mercury in the northeast, Venus and the Moon on the eastern petal;

167.s:
āgneye dakṣiṇe bhaumo madhye syādbhāskaras tathā /
śanirāpye 'tha nairṛtye rāhuḥ ketuś ca vāyave //
167.d:
आग्नेये दक्षिणे भौमो मध्ये स्याद्भास्करस् तथा /
शनिराप्ये ऽथ नैरृत्ये राहुः केतुश् च वायवे //
167.m: in the southeast, Mars in the south, and the Sun should be in the center; / Saturn in the west, then Rāhu in the southwest, and Ketu in the northwest.

167.s:
īśaścomā guho viṣṇurbrahmendrau yamakālakau /
citraguptaścādhidevā agnirāpaḥ kṣitirhariḥ //
167.d:
ईशश्चोमा गुहो विष्णुर्ब्रह्मेन्द्रौ यमकालकौ /
चित्रगुप्तश्चाधिदेवा अग्निरापः क्षितिर्हरिः //
167.m: Śiva, Umā, Guha, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Indra, Yama, Kāla, / and Citragupta are the presiding deities. Agni, the Waters, the Earth, Hari,

167.s:
indra aindrī devatā ca prajeśo 'hirvidhiḥ kramāt /
ete pratyadhidevāś ca gaṇeśo durgayānilaḥ //
167.d:
इन्द्र ऐन्द्री देवता च प्रजेशो ऽहिर्विधिः क्रमात् /
एते प्रत्यधिदेवाश् च गणेशो दुर्गयानिलः //
167.m: Indra, the goddess Indrāṇī, the Lord of Creatures, the Serpent, and Vidhi, in order, / are these subordinate presiding deities. Gaṇeśa, Durgā, Vāyu,

167.s:
khamaśvinau ca sampūjya yajedvījaiś ca vedajaiḥ /
:p 162
arkaḥ palāśaḥ khadiro hy apāmārgaś ca pippalaḥ //
167.d:
खमश्विनौ च सम्पूज्य यजेद्वीजैश् च वेदजैः /
:प् 162
अर्कः पलाशः खदिरो ह्य् अपामार्गश् च पिप्पलः //
167.m:
Ether, and the Aśvins are to be worshipped; and one should sacrifice with seed-syllables and Vedic mantras.
[Page 162]
Arka, palāśa, khadira, apāmārga, pippala,

167.s:
udumbaraḥ śamī durvā kuśāś ca samidhaḥ kramāt /
madhvājyadadhisaṃmiśrā hotavyāścāṣṭadhā śatam //
167.d:
उदुम्बरः शमी दुर्वा कुशाश् च समिधः क्रमात् /
मध्वाज्यदधिसंमिश्रा होतव्याश्चाष्टधा शतम् //
167.m: udumbara, śamī, dūrvā-grass, and kuśa-grass are the sacrificial sticks in order. / Mixed with honey, clarified butter, and curd, they should be offered one hundred and eight times.

167.s:
ekāṣṭaśaturaḥ kumbhān pūrya pūrṇāhutintathā /
vasordhārāntato dadyāddakṣiṇāñca tato dadet //
167.d:
एकाष्टशतुरः कुम्भान् पूर्य पूर्णाहुतिन्तथा /
वसोर्धारान्ततो दद्याद्दक्षिणाञ्च ततो ददेत् //
167.m: Having filled one, eight, or four jars, and likewise having offered the full oblation, / he should then pour the continuous stream of clarified butter and bestow the sacrificial fee.

167.s:
yajamānaṃ caturbhistair abhiṣiñcet samantrakaiḥ /
surāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ //
167.d:
यजमानं चतुर्भिस्तैर् अभिषिञ्चेत् समन्त्रकैः /
सुरास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः //
167.m: He should consecrate the patron of the sacrifice by aspersion with those four jars accompanied by mantras: / 'May the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, consecrate you with aspersion!

167.s:
vāsudevo jagannāthas tathā saṅkarṣaṇaḥ prabhuḥ /
pradyumnaścāniruddhaś ca bhavantu vijayāya te //
167.d:
वासुदेवो जगन्नाथस् तथा सङ्कर्षणः प्रभुः /
प्रद्युम्नश्चानिरुद्धश् च भवन्तु विजयाय ते //
167.m: May Vāsudeva, the Lord of the Universe, and the Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa, / Pradyumna, and Aniruddha be for your victory!

167.s:
ākhaṇḍalo 'gnirbhagavān yamo vai nairṛtas tathā /
varuṇaḥ pavanaś caiva dhanādhyakṣas tathā śivaḥ //
167.d:
आखण्डलो ऽग्निर्भगवान् यमो वै नैरृतस् तथा /
वरुणः पवनश् चैव धनाध्यक्षस् तथा शिवः //
167.m: May Ākhaṇḍala, Lord Agni, Yama, and Nairṛta, / Varuṇa, Pavana, Kubera, and Śiva,

167.s:
brahmaṇā sahitaḥ śeṣo dikpālāḥ pāntu vaḥ sadā /
kīrtirlakṣmīrdhṛtirmedhā puṣṭiḥ śraddhā kriyā matiḥ //
167.d:
ब्रह्मणा सहितः शेषो दिक्पालाः पान्तु वः सदा /
कीर्तिर्लक्ष्मीर्धृतिर्मेधा पुष्टिः श्रद्धा क्रिया मतिः //
167.m: together with Brahmā, Śeṣa, and the guardians of the directions protect you always! / May Kīrti, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Medhā, Puṣṭi, Śraddhā, Kriyā, Mati,

167.s:
buddhir lajjā vapuḥ śāntistuṣṭiḥ kāntiś ca mātaraḥ /
etāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu dharmapatnyāḥ samāgatāḥ //
167.d:
बुद्धिर् लज्जा वपुः शान्तिस्तुष्टिः कान्तिश् च मातरः /
एतास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु धर्मपत्न्याः समागताः //
167.m: Buddhi, Lajjā, Vapuḥ, Śānti, Tuṣṭi, and Kānti—the divine Mothers— / may these wives of Dharma, assembled together, consecrate you with aspersion!

167.s:
ādityaś candramā bhaumo budhajīvaśitārkajāḥ /
grahāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rāhuḥ ketuś ca tarpitāḥ //
167.d:
आदित्यश् चन्द्रमा भौमो बुधजीवशितार्कजाः /
ग्रहास्त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु राहुः केतुश् च तर्पिताः //
167.m: May the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn, / the planets, and Rāhu and Ketu, being propitiated, consecrate you with aspersion!

167.s:
devadānavagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ /
ṛṣayo manavo gāvo devamātara eva ca //
167.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः /
ऋषयो मनवो गावो देवमातर एव च //
167.m: May the gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents, / the ṛṣis, Manus, cows, and the mothers of the gods,

167.s:
devapatnyo drumā nāgā daityāścāpsarasāṅgaṇāḥ /
astrāṇi sarvaśāstrāṇi rājāno vāhanāni ca //
167.d:
देवपत्न्यो द्रुमा नागा दैत्याश्चाप्सरसाङ्गणाः /
अस्त्राणि सर्वशास्त्राणि राजानो वाहनानि च //
167.m: the wives of the gods, trees, Nāgas, Daityas, and celestial nymphs, / missiles, all the scriptures, kings, mounts,

167.s:
auṣadhāni ca ratnāni kālasyāvayavāś ca ye /
saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailāstīrthāni jaladā nadāḥ //
:p 163
167.d:
औषधानि च रत्नानि कालस्यावयवाश् च ये /
सरितः सागराः शैलास्तीर्थानि जलदा नदाः //
:प् 163
167.m:
medicinal herbs, jewels, the divisions of time, / rivers, oceans, mountains, sacred fords, clouds, and streams—
[Page 163]

167.s:
ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu sarvakāmārthasiddhaye(1) /
alaṅkṛtastato dadyāddhemagonnabhuvādikaṃ //
167.d:
एते त्वामभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वकामार्थसिद्धये(1) /
अलङ्कृतस्ततो दद्याद्धेमगोन्नभुवादिकं //
167.m: may these consecrate you with aspersion for the attainment of all desires and purposes!' / Adorned, he should then give gold, cows, food, land, and the like.

167.s:
kapile sarvadevānāṃ pūjanīyāsi rohiṇi /
tīrthadevamayī yasmādataḥśāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
कपिले सर्वदेवानां पूजनीयासि रोहिणि /
तीर्थदेवमयी यस्मादतःशान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: 'O tawny cow Rohiṇī, you are worthy of worship by all the gods; / since you consist of sacred fords and deities, therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṇyānāṃ maṅgalānāñca maṅgalaṃ /
viṣṇunā vidhṛto nityamataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
पुण्यस्त्वं शङ्ख पुण्यानां मङ्गलानाञ्च मङ्गलं /
विष्णुना विधृतो नित्यमतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: O conch, you are pure among pure things, the auspiciousness of auspicious things, / held perpetually by Viṣṇu; therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
dharma tvaṃ vṛṣarūpeṇa jagadānandakārakaḥ /
aṣṭamūrteradhiṣṭānamataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
धर्म त्वं वृषरूपेण जगदानन्दकारकः /
अष्टमूर्तेरधिष्टानमतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: O Dharma, in the form of a bull you bring bliss to the world; / you are the abode of the Eight-formed Lord; therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
hiraṇyagarbhagarbhasthaṃ hemavījaṃ vibhāvasoḥ /
anantapuṇyaphaladamataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
हिरण्यगर्भगर्भस्थं हेमवीजं विभावसोः /
अनन्तपुण्यफलदमतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: Gold, seated in the womb of Hiraṇyagarbha, the seed of Agni, / grants the fruit of endless religious merit; therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
pītavastrayugaṃ yasmādvāsudevasya vallabhaṃ /
pradānāttasya vai viṣṇurataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
पीतवस्त्रयुगं यस्माद्वासुदेवस्य वल्लभं /
प्रदानात्तस्य वै विष्णुरतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: Since a pair of yellow garments is dear to Vāsudeva, / by its gift may Viṣṇu [be pleased]; therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
viṣṇustvaṃ matsyarūpeṇa yasmādamṛtasambhavaḥ /
candrārkavāhano nityamataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
विष्णुस्त्वं मत्स्यरूपेण यस्मादमृतसम्भवः /
चन्द्रार्कवाहनो नित्यमतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: O Viṣṇu, since as the Fish incarnation you were born of nectar, / constantly bearing the Sun and Moon; therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
yasmāttvaṃ pṛthivī sarvā dhenuḥ keśavasannibhā /
sarvapāpaharā nityamataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
यस्मात्त्वं पृथिवी सर्वा धेनुः केशवसन्निभा /
सर्वपापहरा नित्यमतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: Since you, the entire Earth, are a milch-cow resembling Keśava, / eternally removing all sins; therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
yasmādāyasakarmāṇi tavādhīnāni sarvadā /
lāṅgalādyāyudhādīni ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
यस्मादायसकर्माणि तवाधीनानि सर्वदा /
लाङ्गलाद्यायुधादीनि अतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: Since iron implements, plows, weapons, and the like, / are forever dependent on you; therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
yasmāttvaṃ ssarvayajñānāmaṅgatvena vyavasthitaḥ /
yonirvibhāvasornityamataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me //
167.d:
यस्मात्त्वं स्सर्वयज्ञानामङ्गत्वेन व्यवस्थितः /
योनिर्विभावसोर्नित्यमतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे //
167.m: Since you stand as a limb of all sacrifices, / the perpetual source of Agni; therefore grant me peace!

167.s:
gavāmaṅgeṣu tiṣṭhanti bhuvanāni caturdaśa /
yasmāttasmācchivaṃ me syādiha loke paratra ca //
:n
1 dharmakāmārthasiddhaye iti kha..
:p 164
167.d:
गवामङ्गेषु तिष्ठन्ति भुवनानि चतुर्दश /
यस्मात्तस्माच्छिवं मे स्यादिह लोके परत्र च //
:न्
1 धर्मकामार्थसिद्धये इति ख..
:प् 164
167.m:
The fourteen worlds reside in the limbs of cows; / because of that, may there be auspiciousness for me in this world and the next!'
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: Or dharmakāmārthasiddhaye in ms. kha.] / [Page 164]

167.s:
yasmādaśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ keśavasya śivasya ca /
śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu dattā janmani janmani(1) //
167.d:
यस्मादशून्यं शयनं केशवस्य शिवस्य च /
शय्या ममाप्यशून्यास्तु दत्ता जन्मनि जन्मनि(1) //
167.m: 'Since the couch of Keśava and Śiva is never empty, / may the bed given by me also never be empty in birth after birth!

167.s:
yathā ratneṣu sarveṣu sarve devāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
tathā śāntiṃ prayacchantu ratnadānena me surāḥ //
167.d:
यथा रत्नेषु सर्वेषु सर्वे देवाः प्रतिष्ठिताः /
तथा शान्तिं प्रयच्छन्तु रत्नदानेन मे सुराः //
167.m: Just as all the gods are situated in all jewels, / so may the gods grant me peace by this gift of jewels!

167.s:
yathā bhūmipradānasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīṃ /
dānānyanyāni me śāntirbhūmidānādbhavatviha //
167.d:
यथा भूमिप्रदानस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीं /
दानान्यन्यानि मे शान्तिर्भूमिदानाद्भवत्विह //
167.m: Just as other gifts are not worth a sixteenth part / of the gift of land, may peace come to me here through the gift of land!'

167.s:
grahayajño 'yutahomo dakṣiṇābhī raṇe jitiḥ /
vivāhotsavayajñeṣu pratiṣṭhādiṣu karmaṣu //
167.d:
ग्रहयज्ञो ऽयुतहोमो दक्षिणाभी रणे जितिः /
विवाहोत्सवयज्ञेषु प्रतिष्ठादिषु कर्मषु //
167.m: The sacrifice to the planets with ten thousand fire oblations, with sacrificial fees, brings victory in battle, / in marriages, festivals, sacrifices, and rites such as consecration.

167.s:
sarvakāmāptaye lakṣakoṭihomadvayaṃ mataṃ /
gṛhadeśe maṇḍape 'tha(2) ayute hastamātrakaṃ //
167.d:
सर्वकामाप्तये लक्षकोटिहोमद्वयं मतं /
गृहदेशे मण्डपे ऽथ(2) अयुते हस्तमात्रकं //
167.m: The two fire oblations—of one hundred thousand and ten million—are taught for the attainment of all desires. / In the house or in a pavilion, for the rite of ten thousand, [a fire-pit of] only one cubit,

167.s:
mekhalāyonisaṃyuktaṃ kuṇḍañcatvāra ṛtvijaḥ /
svayameko 'pi vā lakṣe sarvaṃ daśaguṇaṃ hi tat //
167.d:
मेखलायोनिसंयुक्तं कुण्डञ्चत्वार ऋत्विजः /
स्वयमेको ऽपि वा लक्षे सर्वं दशगुणं हि तत् //
167.m: furnished with stepped girdles and a spout, and four officiating priests [are required], / or even oneself alone; but for a hundred thousand, all that is tenfold.

167.s:
caturhastaṃ dvihastaṃ vā tārkṣañcātrādhikaṃ yajet /
sāmadhvaniśīrastvaṃ vāhanaṃ pameṣṭhinaḥ //
167.d:
चतुर्हस्तं द्विहस्तं वा तार्क्षञ्चात्राधिकं यजेत् /
सामध्वनिशीरस्त्वं वाहनं पमेष्ठिनः //
167.m: One should worship [in a fire-pit of] four cubits or two cubits; and here one should additionally worship Garuḍa: / 'You whose head is the sound of the Sāmaveda, mount of the Supreme Lord,

167.s:
viṣayāpaharo nityamataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me /
pūrvavat kuṇḍamāmantrya lakṣahomaṃ samācaret //
167.d:
विषयापहरो नित्यमतः शान्तिं प्रयच्छ मे /
पूर्ववत् कुण्डमामन्त्र्य लक्षहोमं समाचरेत् //
167.m: who constantly destroys worldly attachments, therefore grant me peace!' / Having consecrated the fire-pit as before, one should perform the fire oblation of one hundred thousand.

167.s:
vasordhārāṃ tato dadyācchayyābhūṣādikaṃ dadet /
tatrāpi daśa cāṣṭau ca lakṣahome tathartvijaḥ //
167.d:
वसोर्धारां ततो दद्याच्छय्याभूषादिकं ददेत् /
तत्रापि दश चाष्टौ च लक्षहोमे तथर्त्विजः //
167.m: He should then pour the continuous stream of clarified butter and give beds, ornaments, and the like. / There also, in the oblation of one hundred thousand, there are ten or eight officiating priests.

167.s:
putrānnarājyavijayabhuktimuktyādi(3) cāpnuyāt /
dakṣiṇābhiḥ phalenāsmācchatrughnaḥ koṭihomakaḥ //
:n
1 tathā janmani janmanīti ṅa..
2 gṛhādau maṇḍape vātheti kha.. / gṛhādau maṇḍape caivamiti
ña..
3 putrārtharājyavijayabhuktimuktyādīti kha.. , ṅa.. ca
:p 165
167.d:
पुत्रान्नराज्यविजयभुक्तिमुक्त्यादि(3) चाप्नुयात् /
दक्षिणाभिः फलेनास्माच्छत्रुघ्नः कोटिहोमकः //
:न्
1 तथा जन्मनि जन्मनीति ङ..
2 गृहादौ मण्डपे वाथेति ख.. / गृहादौ मण्डपे चैवमिति
ञ..
3 पुत्रार्थराज्यविजयभुक्तिमुक्त्यादीति ख.. , ङ.. च
:प् 165
167.m:
He obtains sons, food, kingdom, victory, worldly enjoyment, liberation, and so on. / By its sacrificial fees and fruit, the rite of ten million fire oblations destroys enemies.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: Or tathā janmani janmani in ms. ṅa.]
[Footnote 2: Or gṛhādau maṇḍape vātha in ms. kha; gṛhādau maṇḍape caivam in ms. ña.]
[Footnote 3: Or putrārtharājyavijayabhuktimuktyādi in mss. kha and ṅa.] / [Page 165]

167.s:
caturhastaṃ cāṣṭahastaṃ kuṇḍandvādaśa ca dvijāḥ /
pañcaviṃśaṃ ṣoḍaśaṃ vā paṭe dvāre catuṣṭayaṃ //
167.d:
चतुर्हस्तं चाष्टहस्तं कुण्डन्द्वादश च द्विजाः /
पञ्चविंशं षोडशं वा पटे द्वारे चतुष्टयं //
167.m: The fire-pit is of four cubits or eight cubits, and twelve brahmins [are employed], / or twenty-five or sixteen; on the cloth and at the four doors,

167.s:
koṭihomī sarvakāmī viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati /
homastu grahamantrair vā gāyatryā vaiṣṇavair api //
167.d:
कोटिहोमी सर्वकामी विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति /
होमस्तु ग्रहमन्त्रैर् वा गायत्र्या वैष्णवैर् अपि //
167.m: the performer of the ten million oblations attains all desires and goes to the realm of Viṣṇu. / The fire oblation may be performed with mantras of the planets, the Gāyatrī, Vaiṣṇava mantras,

167.s:
jātavedomukhaiḥ śaivaiḥ(1) vaidikaiḥ prathitair api /
tilair yavair ghṛtair aśvamedhaphalādibhāk //
167.d:
जातवेदोमुखैः शैवैः(1) वैदिकैः प्रथितैर् अपि /
तिलैर् यवैर् घृतैर् अश्वमेधफलादिभाक् //
167.m: with celebrated Vedic mantras beginning with Jātavedas, or Śaiva mantras, / using sesame, barley, and clarified butter; he attains the fruit of an horse sacrifice and the like.

167.s:
vidveṣaṇābhicāreṣu trikoṇaṃ kuṇḍamiṣyate /
samidho vāmahastena śyenāsthyanalasaṃyutāḥ //
167.d:
विद्वेषणाभिचारेषु त्रिकोणं कुण्डमिष्यते /
समिधो वामहस्तेन श्येनास्थ्यनलसंयुताः //
167.m: In rites of causing hatred and malevolent sorcery, a triangular fire-pit is prescribed. / Sacrificial sticks mixed with bones of hawks and fire [are offered] with the left hand,

167.s:
raktabhūṣair muktakeśair dhyāyadbhiraśivaṃ ripoḥ /
durmitriyāstasmai santu yo dveṣṭi huṃ phaḍiti ca //
167.d:
रक्तभूषैर् मुक्तकेशैर् ध्यायद्भिरशिवं रिपोः /
दुर्मित्रियास्तस्मै सन्तु यो द्वेष्टि हुं फडिति च //
167.m: wearing red ornaments, with disheveled hair, meditating on the misfortune of the enemy, / reciting: 'May those who hate [us] be without friends, huṃ phaṭ!'

167.s:
chindyāt kṣureṇa pratimāṃ piṣṭarūpaṃ ripuṃ hanet(2) /
yajedekaṃ pīḍakaṃ vā yaḥ sa kṛtvā divaṃ vrajet //
:e ity āgneye mahapurāṇe 'yutalakṣakoṭihomā nāma
saptaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athāṣṭaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mahāpātakādikathanam
167.d:
छिन्द्यात् क्षुरेण प्रतिमां पिष्टरूपं रिपुं हनेत्(2) /
यजेदेकं पीडकं वा यः स कृत्वा दिवं व्रजेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महपुराणे ऽयुतलक्षकोटिहोमा नाम
सप्तषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथाष्टषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
महापातकादिकथनम्
167.m:
He should cut the image with a razor and slay the enemy made of flour. / He who worships one planet or the tormentor [of planets], having done so, goes to heaven.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-seventh chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'The Fire Oblations of Ten Thousand, One Hundred Thousand, and Ten Million'.
Now begins the one hundred and sixty-eighth chapter.
Account of the Great Sins and Related Matters

168.s:
puṣkara uvāca
daṇḍaṃ kuryānnṛpo nṝṇāṃ prāyaścittamakurvatāṃ /
kāmato 'kāmato vāpi prāyaścittaṃ kṛtaṃ caret //
:n
1 jātavedomukhaiḥ saurair iti kha..
2 ripuṃ harediti ṅa.. , ña.. ca
:p 166
168.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
दण्डं कुर्यान्नृपो नॄणां प्रायश्चित्तमकुर्वतां /
कामतो ऽकामतो वापि प्रायश्चित्तं कृतं चरेत् //
:न्
1 जातवेदोमुखैः सौरैर् इति ख..
2 रिपुं हरेदिति ङ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 166
168.m:
Puṣkara said: / The king should inflict punishment upon men who do not perform expiation. / Whether committed intentionally or unintentionally, one must perform the prescribed expiation.
[Footnote]
1. "jātavedomukhaiḥ saurair" in Kha.
2. "ripuṃ harediti" in Ṅa. and Ña. / p. 166

168.s:
mattakruddhāturāṇāṃ ca na bhuñjīta kadācana /
mahāpātakināṃ spṛṣṭaṃ yacca spṛṣṭamudakyayā //
168.d:
मत्तक्रुद्धातुराणां च न भुञ्जीत कदाचन /
महापातकिनां स्पृष्टं यच्च स्पृष्टमुदक्यया //
168.m: One should never eat the food of the intoxicated, the enraged, or the diseased, / nor what is touched by those guilty of great sins, nor what is touched by a menstruating woman;

168.s:
gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca(1) vārdhuṣergāyanasya ca /
abhiśaptasya ṣaṇḍasya yasyāścopapatirgṛhe //
168.d:
गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च(1) वार्धुषेर्गायनस्य च /
अभिशप्तस्य षण्डस्य यस्याश्चोपपतिर्गृहे //
168.m: nor the food of a corporate guild, nor the food of a courtezan, nor of a usurer, nor of a singer, / nor of an accused person, nor of a eunuch, nor of a man in whose house a paramour dwells;

168.s:
rajakasya nṛśaṃsasya vandinaḥ kitavasya ca /
mithyātapasvinaś caiva cauradaṇḍikayos tathā(2) //
168.d:
रजकस्य नृशंसस्य वन्दिनः कितवस्य च /
मिथ्यातपस्विनश् चैव चौरदण्डिकयोस् तथा(2) //
168.m: nor of a washerman, nor of a cruel person, nor of a bard, nor of a gambler, / nor indeed of a false ascetic, nor of a thief, nor of a rod-bearer [policeman];

168.s:
kuṇḍagolastrījitānāṃ vedavikrayiṇas tathā /
śailūṣatantravāyānnaṃ kṛtaghnasyānnameva ca //
168.d:
कुण्डगोलस्त्रीजितानां वेदविक्रयिणस् तथा /
शैलूषतन्त्रवायान्नं कृतघ्नस्यान्नमेव च //
168.m: nor of sons of adulteresses, sons of widows, or henpecked men, nor of a seller of the Veda, / nor the food of an actor, nor of a weaver, nor the food of an ungrateful person;

168.s:
karmārasya niṣādasya celanirṇejakasya ca /
mithyāpravrajitasyānnampuṃś calyāstailikasya ca //
168.d:
कर्मारस्य निषादस्य चेलनिर्णेजकस्य च /
मिथ्याप्रव्रजितस्यान्नम्पुंश् चल्यास्तैलिकस्य च //
168.m: nor of a blacksmith, nor of a Niṣāda, nor of a clothes-washer, / nor the food of a false renunciant, nor of an unchaste woman, nor of an oilman;

168.s:
ārūḍhapatitasyānnaṃ vidviṣṭānnaṃ ca varjayet /
tathaiva brāhmaṇasyānnaṃ brāhmaṇenānimantritaḥ //
168.d:
आरूढपतितस्यान्नं विद्विष्टान्नं च वर्जयेत् /
तथैव ब्राह्मणस्यान्नं ब्राह्मणेनानिमन्त्रितः //
168.m: nor the food of an apostate ascetic; and one should avoid food offered with malice; / likewise, the food of a brāhmaṇa, if uninvited by that brāhmaṇa.

168.s:
brāhmaṇānnañca śūdreṇa nādyāccaiva nimantritaḥ /
eṣāmanyatamasyānnamamatyā vā tryahaṃ kṣapet //
168.d:
ब्राह्मणान्नञ्च शूद्रेण नाद्याच्चैव निमन्त्रितः /
एषामन्यतमस्यान्नममत्या वा त्र्यहं क्षपेत् //
168.m: And the food of a brāhmaṇa should not be eaten by a śūdra, even when invited. / If one eats the food of any of these unwittingly, one should fast for three days;

168.s:
matyā bhuktvā caret kṛcchraṃ retoviṇmūtrameva ca /
caṇḍālaśvapacānnantu bhuktvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret //
168.d:
मत्या भुक्त्वा चरेत् कृच्छ्रं रेतोविण्मूत्रमेव च /
चण्डालश्वपचान्नन्तु भुक्त्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् //
168.m: having eaten it wittingly, one should perform a kṛcchra penance; likewise for [consuming] semen, feces, or urine. / But having eaten the food of a Caṇḍāla or a Śvapāca, one should perform a cāndrāyaṇa penance.

168.s:
anirdiśaṃ ca pretānnaṃ gavāghrātaṃ tathaiva ca /
śūdrocchiṣṭaṃ śunocchiṣṭaṃ patitānnaṃ tathaiva ca //
168.d:
अनिर्दिशं च प्रेतान्नं गवाघ्रातं तथैव च /
शूद्रोच्छिष्टं शुनोच्छिष्टं पतितान्नं तथैव च //
168.m: And food during the ten days of mourning, food smelled by a cow, / the leavings of a śūdra, the leavings of a dog, and likewise the food of an outcaste:

168.s:
taptakṛcchraṃ prakurvīta aśauce kṛcchramācaret /
aśauce yasya yo bhuṅkte sopyaśuddhas tathā bhavet //
168.d:
तप्तकृच्छ्रं प्रकुर्वीत अशौचे कृच्छ्रमाचरेत् /
अशौचे यस्य यो भुङ्क्ते सोप्यशुद्धस् तथा भवेत् //
168.m: one should perform a taptakṛcchra penance, [and] during ritual impurity one should perform a kṛcchra penance. / Whoever eats [the food] of someone during ritual impurity, he too becomes impure in like manner.

168.s:
mṛtapañcanakhāt kūpādamedhyena sakṛdyutāt /
:n
1 gaṇānāṃ gaṇikānāñceti ṅa.. , ña.. ca
2 cauradāmbhikayostatheti ña..
:p 167
apaḥ pītvā tryahaṃ tiṣṭhet sopavāso dvijottamaḥ //
168.d:
मृतपञ्चनखात् कूपादमेध्येन सकृद्युतात् /
:न्
1 गणानां गणिकानाञ्चेति ङ.. , ञ.. च
2 चौरदाम्भिकयोस्तथेति ञ..
:प् 167
अपः पीत्वा त्र्यहं तिष्ठेत् सोपवासो द्विजोत्तमः //
168.m:
From a well containing a dead five-nailed animal, or tainted with feces once,
[Footnote]
1. "gaṇānāṃ gaṇikānāñceti" in Ṅa. and Ña.
2. "cauradāmbhikayostatheti" in Ña. / p. 167
having drunk the water, the best of the twice-born should remain fasting for three days.

168.s:
sarvatra śūdre pādaḥ syād dvitrayaṃ vaiśyabhūpayoḥ(1) /
viḍvarāhakharoṣṭrāṇāṃ gomāyoḥ kapikākayoḥ //
168.d:
सर्वत्र शूद्रे पादः स्याद् द्वित्रयं वैश्यभूपयोः(1) /
विड्वराहखरोष्ट्राणां गोमायोः कपिकाकयोः //
168.m: Everywhere for a śūdra there should be a quarter [penance], two and three [quarters] for a vaiśya and a king [kṣatriya]. / Having consumed the urine and feces of a domesticated pig, a donkey, a camel,

168.s:
prāśya mūtrapurīṣāṇi dvijaścāndrāyaṇaṃ caret /
śuṣkāṇi jagdhvā māṃsāni(2) pretānnaṃ karakāṇi ca //
168.d:
प्राश्य मूत्रपुरीषाणि द्विजश्चान्द्रायणं चरेत् /
शुष्काणि जग्ध्वा मांसानि(2) प्रेतान्नं करकाणि च //
168.m: a jackal, a monkey, or a crow, a twice-born should perform a cāndrāyaṇa penance; / likewise having eaten dried meat, food during mourning, or hail-stones;

168.s:
kravyādaśūkaroṣṭrāṇāṃ gomāyoḥ kapikākayoḥ /
gonarāśvakharoṣṭrāṇāṃ chatrākaṃ grāmakukkuṭaṃ //
168.d:
क्रव्यादशूकरोष्ट्राणां गोमायोः कपिकाकयोः /
गोनराश्वखरोष्ट्राणां छत्राकं ग्रामकुक्कुटं //
168.m: or having eaten the meat of carnivores, boars, camels, jackals, monkeys, crows, / cows, humans, horses, donkeys, camels, or mushrooms, or a village rooster,

168.s:
māṃsaṃ jagdhvā kuñjarasya taptakṛcchreṇa śuddhyati /
āmaśrāddhe tathā bhuktvā brahmacārī madhu tvadan //
168.d:
मांसं जग्ध्वा कुञ्जरस्य तप्तकृच्छ्रेण शुद्ध्यति /
आमश्राद्धे तथा भुक्त्वा ब्रह्मचारी मधु त्वदन् //
168.m: or the meat of an elephant, one is purified by a taptakṛcchra penance. / Likewise, having eaten at an uncooked-grain ancestral rite, or a celibate student having consumed honey,

168.s:
laśunaṃ guñjanaṃ cādyāt prājāpatyādinā śuciḥ(3) /
bhuktvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ kuryān māṃsañcātmakṛtantathā //
168.d:
लशुनं गुञ्जनं चाद्यात् प्राजापत्यादिना शुचिः(3) /
भुक्त्वा चान्द्रायणं कुर्यान् मांसञ्चात्मकृतन्तथा //
168.m: or if one should eat garlic or turnips, one becomes pure through a prājāpatya or other [penance]. / Having eaten meat prepared for oneself, one should perform a cāndrāyaṇa penance;

168.s:
pelugavyañca peyūṣaṃ tathā śleṣmātakaṃ mṛdaṃ /
vṛthākṛśarasaṃyāvapāyasāpūpaśaṣkulīḥ //
168.d:
पेलुगव्यञ्च पेयूषं तथा श्लेष्मातकं मृदं /
वृथाकृशरसंयावपायसापूपशष्कुलीः //
168.m: and [milk of a cow within ten days of calving], colostrum, the fruit of the śleṣmātaka, earth, / kṛśara, saṃyāva, rice-pudding, sweet cakes, and fried pastries made in vain [not offered to deities];

168.s:
anupākṛṭamāṃsāni devānnāni havīṃṣi ca /
gavāñca mahiṣīṇāṃ ca varjayitvā tathāpyajāṃ //
168.d:
अनुपाकृटमांसानि देवान्नानि हवींषि च /
गवाञ्च महिषीणां च वर्जयित्वा तथाप्यजां //
168.m: meat from an animal not consecrated for sacrifice, food offered to deities, and oblations. / Except for cows, buffaloes, and also she-goats,

168.s:
sarvakṣīrāṇi varjyāṇi tāsāñcaivāpyannirdaśaṃ /
śaśakaḥ śalyakī godhā khaḍgaḥ kūrmastathaiva ca //
168.d:
सर्वक्षीराणि वर्ज्याणि तासाञ्चैवाप्यन्निर्दशं /
शशकः शल्यकी गोधा खड्गः कूर्मस्तथैव च //
168.m: all kinds of milk are to be avoided, and even their milk within ten days [of calving]. / The hare, porcupine, monitor lizard, rhinoceros, and tortoise:

168.s:
bhakṣyāḥ pañcanakhāḥ proktāḥ pariśeṣāś ca varjitāḥ /
pāṭhīnarohitānmatsyān siṃhatuṇḍāṃś ca bhakṣayet //
168.d:
भक्ष्याः पञ्चनखाः प्रोक्ताः परिशेषाश् च वर्जिताः /
पाठीनरोहितान्मत्स्यान् सिंहतुण्डांश् च भक्षयेत् //
168.m: these five-nailed animals are declared edible, and the remaining ones are forbidden. / One may eat the pāṭhīna and rohita fishes, and the siṃhatuṇḍa.

168.s:
yavagodhūmajaṃ sarvaṃ payasaś caiva vikriyāḥ /
vāgaṣāḍgavacakrādīn sasnehamuṣitaṃ tathā //
:n
1 dvitīyaṃ vaiśyaśūdrayoreti ka.. , kha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
2 śuṣkāṇi dagdhamaṃsāni iti ṅa..
3 prājāpatyāddvijaḥ śuciriti kha..
:p 168
168.d:
यवगोधूमजं सर्वं पयसश् चैव विक्रियाः /
वागषाड्गवचक्रादीन् सस्नेहमुषितं तथा //
:न्
1 द्वितीयं वैश्यशूद्रयोरेति क.. , ख.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
2 शुष्काणि दग्धमंसानि इति ङ..
3 प्राजापत्याद्द्विजः शुचिरिति ख..
:प् 168
168.m:
All products made of barley and wheat, modifications of milk, / [dishes like] vāgaṣāḍga, vacakra, and the like, even if kept overnight, provided they contain oil or ghee, [may be eaten].
[Footnote]
1. "dvitīyaṃ vaiśyaśūdrayoreti" in Ka., Kha., Ṅa., and Ña.
2. "śuṣkāṇi dagdhamaṃsāni iti" in Ṅa.
3. "prājāpatyāddvijaḥ śuciriti" in Kha. / p. 168

168.s:
agnihotraparīddhāgnirbrāhmaṇaḥ kāmacārataḥ /
cāndrāyaṇaṃ carenmāsaṃ vīravadhvāsanaṃ hitaṃ //
168.d:
अग्निहोत्रपरीद्धाग्निर्ब्राह्मणः कामचारतः /
चान्द्रायणं चरेन्मासं वीरवध्वासनं हितं //
168.m: A brāhmaṇa whose fire is kindled for the agnihotra, who acts willfully, / should perform a cāndrāyaṇa penance for a month; the posture of a hero's wife is beneficial.

168.s:
brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṅganāgamaḥ /
mahānti pātakānyāhuḥ saṃyogaś caiva taiḥ saha //
168.d:
ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं स्तेयं गुर्वङ्गनागमः /
महान्ति पातकान्याहुः संयोगश् चैव तैः सह //
168.m: Killing a brāhmaṇa, drinking liquor, theft, and intercourse with the guru's wife: / they call these the great sins, as well as association with those [who commit them].

168.s:
anṛte ca samutkarṣo rājagāmi ca paiśunaṃ /
guroścālīkanirbandhaḥ samānaṃ brahmahatyayā(1) //
168.d:
अनृते च समुत्कर्षो राजगामि च पैशुनं /
गुरोश्चालीकनिर्बन्धः समानं ब्रह्महत्यया(1) //
168.m: Exalting oneself falsely, slander reaching the king, / and obstinate false accusation against a guru are equal to killing a brāhmaṇa.

168.s:
brahmojjhyavedanindā ca kauṭasākṣyaṃ suhṛdbadhaḥ /
garhitānnājyayorjagdhiḥ(2) surāpānasamāni ṣaṭ //
168.d:
ब्रह्मोज्झ्यवेदनिन्दा च कौटसाक्ष्यं सुहृद्बधः /
गर्हितान्नाज्ययोर्जग्धिः(2) सुरापानसमानि षट् //
168.m: Abandoning the Veda, reviling the Veda, false testimony, slaying a friend, / eating condemned food or condemned clarified butter: these six are equal to drinking liquor.

168.s:
nikṣepasyāpaharaṇaṃ narāśvarajatasya ca /
bhūmivajramaṇīnāñca rukmasteyasamaṃ smṛtaṃ //
168.d:
निक्षेपस्यापहरणं नराश्वरजतस्य च /
भूमिवज्रमणीनाञ्च रुक्मस्तेयसमं स्मृतं //
168.m: Misappropriation of a deposit, or of a man, a horse, silver, / land, diamonds, or gems is remembered as equal to the theft of gold.

168.s:
retaḥsekaḥ svayonyāṣu kumārīṣvantyajāsu ca /
sakhyuḥ putrasya ca(3) strīṣu gurutalpasamaṃ viduḥ //
168.d:
रेतःसेकः स्वयोन्याषु कुमारीष्वन्त्यजासु च /
सख्युः पुत्रस्य च(3) स्त्रीषु गुरुतल्पसमं विदुः //
168.m: Discharging semen into women of one's own family, maidens, low-caste women, / or the wives of a friend or a son, they know to be equal to violating the guru's bed.

168.s:
gobadho 'yājya saṃyājyaṃ pāradāryātmavikriyaḥ /
gurumātṛpitṛtyāgaḥ svādhyayāgnyoḥ sutasya ca //
168.d:
गोबधो ऽयाज्य संयाज्यं पारदार्यात्मविक्रियः /
गुरुमातृपितृत्यागः स्वाध्ययाग्न्योः सुतस्य च //
168.m: Killing a cow, sacrificing for those unfit to sacrifice, adultery, selling oneself, / abandoning one's guru, mother, or father, or one's Vedic study, sacred fires, or son;

168.s:
parivittitānujena parivedanameva ca /
tayordānañca kanyāyāstayoreva ca yājanaṃ //
168.d:
परिवित्तितानुजेन परिवेदनमेव च /
तयोर्दानञ्च कन्यायास्तयोरेव च याजनं //
168.m: letting a younger brother marry first, marrying before an elder brother, / giving a maiden to either of these two, or sacrificing for either of them;

168.s:
kanyāyā dūṣaṇañcaiva vārdhuṣyaṃ vratalopanaṃ /
taḍāgārāmadārāṇāmapatyasya ca vikriyaḥ //
168.d:
कन्याया दूषणञ्चैव वार्धुष्यं व्रतलोपनं /
तडागारामदाराणामपत्यस्य च विक्रियः //
168.m: defiling a maiden, usury, breaking a votive observance, / selling a tank, a grove, a wife, or offspring;

168.s:
vrātyatā bāndhavatyāgo bhṛtādhyāpanameva ca /
bhṛtāccādhyayanādānamavikreyasya vikrayaḥ //
:n
1 samāni brahmahatyayeti kha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
2 garhitānāmannajagdhiriti ṅa..
3 sakhyuḥ sutasya ceti ṅa..
:p 169
168.d:
व्रात्यता बान्धवत्यागो भृताध्यापनमेव च /
भृताच्चाध्ययनादानमविक्रेयस्य विक्रयः //
:न्
1 समानि ब्रह्महत्ययेति ख.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
2 गर्हितानामन्नजग्धिरिति ङ..
3 सख्युः सुतस्य चेति ङ..
:प् 169
168.m:
becoming an outcaste through neglect of rites, abandoning kinsmen, teaching for a salary, / studying from one who teaches for a salary, selling what is forbidden to sell;
[Footnote]
1. "samāni brahmahatyayeti" in Kha., Ṅa., and Ña.
2. "garhitānāmannajagdhiriti" in Ṅa.
3. "sakhyuḥ sutasya ceti" in Ṅa. / p. 169

168.s:
sarvākāreṣvadhīkāro mahāyantrapravartanaṃ /
hiṃsauṣadhīnāṃ stryājīvaḥ kriyālaṅganameva ca //
168.d:
सर्वाकारेष्वधीकारो महायन्त्रप्रवर्तनं /
हिंसौषधीनां स्त्र्याजीवः क्रियालङ्गनमेव च //
168.m: superintending mines and works of all kinds, operating large mechanical apparatuses, / destroying medicinal herbs, living off one's wife, omitting rites;

168.s:
indhanārthamaśuṣkāṇāṃ dumāṇāñcaiva pātanaṃ /
yoṣitāṃ grahaṇañcaiva strīnindakasamāgamaḥ //
168.d:
इन्धनार्थमशुष्काणां दुमाणाञ्चैव पातनं /
योषितां ग्रहणञ्चैव स्त्रीनिन्दकसमागमः //
168.m: felling unseasoned trees for firewood, / abducting women, associating with a reviler of women;

168.s:
ātmārthañca kriyārambho ninditānnadanantathā /
anāhitāgnitāsteyamṛṇānāñcānapakriyā //
168.d:
आत्मार्थञ्च क्रियारम्भो निन्दितान्नदनन्तथा /
अनाहिताग्नितास्तेयमृणानाञ्चानपक्रिया //
168.m: undertaking rituals solely for oneself, eating condemned food, / not maintaining the sacred fires, theft, non-payment of debts;

168.s:
asacchāstrādhigamanaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ vyasanakriyā /
dhānyakupyapaśusteyaṃ madyapastrīniṣevaṇaṃ //
168.d:
असच्छास्त्राधिगमनं दौःशील्यं व्यसनक्रिया /
धान्यकुप्यपशुस्तेयं मद्यपस्त्रीनिषेवणं //
168.m: studying bad scriptures, vicious conduct, addiction to vices, / theft of grain, base metals, or cattle, consorting with women who drink liquor;

168.s:
strīśūdraviṭkṣatrabadho nāstikyañcopapātakaṃ /
brāhmaṇasya rujaḥ kṛtyaṃ ghrātiraghreyamadyayoḥ //
168.d:
स्त्रीशूद्रविट्क्षत्रबधो नास्तिक्यञ्चोपपातकं /
ब्राह्मणस्य रुजः कृत्यं घ्रातिरघ्रेयमद्ययोः //
168.m: killing a woman, a śūdra, a vaiśya, or a kṣatriya, and atheism are minor sins. / Causing bodily pain to a brāhmaṇa, smelling what ought not to be smelled or liquor,

168.s:
jaiṃbhaṃ puṃsi ca maithunyaṃ jātibhraṃśakaraṃ smṛtaṃ /
śvakharoṣṭramṛgendrāṇāmajāvyoś caiva māraṇaṃ(1) //
168.d:
जैंभं पुंसि च मैथुन्यं जातिभ्रंशकरं स्मृतं /
श्वखरोष्ट्रमृगेन्द्राणामजाव्योश् चैव मारणं(1) //
168.m: deceitfulness, and homosexual intercourse among men are remembered as causing loss of caste. / The slaughter of dogs, donkeys, camels, lions, goats, and sheep,

168.s:
saṅkīrṇakaraṇaṃ jñeyaṃ mīnāhinakulasya ca /
ninditebhyo dhanādānaṃ bāṇijyaṃ śūdrasevanaṃ //
168.d:
सङ्कीर्णकरणं ज्ञेयं मीनाहिनकुलस्य च /
निन्दितेभ्यो धनादानं बाणिज्यं शूद्रसेवनं //
168.m: and of fish, snakes, and mongooses is known as causing degraded status. / Receiving wealth from blameworthy persons, trade, serving śūdras,

168.s:
apātrīkaraṇaṃ jñeyamasatyasya ca bhāṣaṇaṃ /
kṛmikīṭavayohatyā madyānugatabhojanaṃ //
168.d:
अपात्रीकरणं ज्ञेयमसत्यस्य च भाषणं /
कृमिकीटवयोहत्या मद्यानुगतभोजनं //
168.m: and speaking falsehood are known as causing unfitness to receive gifts. / Killing worms, insects, and birds, eating food associated with liquor,

168.s:
phalaidhaḥkusumasteyamadhair yañca malāvahaṃ //41//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe mahāpātakādikathanaṃ
nāmāṣṭaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 mārjārasyaiva māraṇamiti ṅa..
:p 170
:ś athaikonasaptatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
prāyaścittāni
168.d:
फलैधःकुसुमस्तेयमधैर् यञ्च मलावहं //41//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे महापातकादिकथनं
नामाष्टषष्ट्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 मार्जारस्यैव मारणमिति ङ..
:प् 170
:श् अथैकोनसप्तत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
प्रायश्चित्तानि
168.m:
theft of fruits, firewood, and flowers, and lack of fortitude cause defilement. // 41
:e Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-eighth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled "Account of the Great Sins and Related Matters."
[Footnote]
[Variant: 1. "killing a cat indeed", thus ms. ṅa.]
[Page 170]
Now begins the one hundred and sixty-ninth chapter:
Expiations.

169.s:
puṣkara uvāca
etatprabhṛtipāpānāṃ prāyaścittaṃ vadāmi te /
brahmahā dvādaśābdāni kuṭīṅkṛtvā vane vaset //
169.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
एतत्प्रभृतिपापानां प्रायश्चित्तं वदामि ते /
ब्रह्महा द्वादशाब्दानि कुटीङ्कृत्वा वने वसेत् //
169.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare to you the expiation for sins beginning with these. / A killer of a Brahmin should dwell in the forest for twelve years, having constructed a hut,

169.s:
bhikṣetātmaviśuddhyarthaṃ kṛtvā śavaśirodhvajaṃ /
prāsyedātmānamagnau vā samiddhe triravākśirāḥ //
169.d:
भिक्षेतात्मविशुद्ध्यर्थं कृत्वा शवशिरोध्वजं /
प्रास्येदात्मानमग्नौ वा समिद्धे त्रिरवाक्शिराः //
169.m: he should beg for alms to purify himself, bearing the skull of a corpse as his banner; / or he should cast himself thrice head downwards into a blazing fire,

169.s:
yajeta vāśvamedhena svarjitā gosavena vā /
japanvānyatamaṃ vedaṃ yojanānāṃ śataṃ brajet //
169.d:
यजेत वाश्वमेधेन स्वर्जिता गोसवेन वा /
जपन्वान्यतमं वेदं योजनानां शतं ब्रजेत् //
169.m: or he should sacrifice with an horse sacrifice, a Svarjit, or a Gosava; / or, reciting any one of the Vedas, he should walk a hundred yojanas,

169.s:
sarvasvaṃ vā vedavide brāhmaṇāyopapādayet /
vratair etair vyapohanti mahāpātakino malaṃ //
169.d:
सर्वस्वं वा वेदविदे ब्राह्मणायोपपादयेत् /
व्रतैर् एतैर् व्यपोहन्ति महापातकिनो मलं //
169.m: or he should bestow his entire property upon a Brahmin who knows the Veda. / By these votive observances, those guilty of major sins remove their stain.

169.s:
upapātakasaṃyukto goghno māsaṃ yavān pivet /
kṛtavāpo vasedgoṣṭhe carmaṇā tena saṃvṛtaḥ //
169.d:
उपपातकसंयुक्तो गोघ्नो मासं यवान् पिवेत् /
कृतवापो वसेद्गोष्ठे चर्मणा तेन संवृतः //
169.m: One guilty of a minor sin who has killed a cow should drink [gruel of] barley for a month; / having shaved his head, he should live in a cowpen, covered with that [cow’s] hide.

169.s:
caturthakālamaśrīyādakṣāralavaṇaṃ mitaṃ /
gomūtreṇa caret snānaṃ dvau māsau niyatendriyaḥ //
169.d:
चतुर्थकालमश्रीयादक्षारलवणं मितं /
गोमूत्रेण चरेत् स्नानं द्वौ मासौ नियतेन्द्रियः //
169.m: He should eat a measured amount at the fourth mealtime, free from pungent flavors and salt; / he should perform ablutions with cow urine for two months, restraining his senses.

169.s:
divānugacchedgāś caiva tiṣṭhannūrdhvaṃ rajaḥ pivet /
vṛṣabhaikādaśā gāstu dadyādvicāritavrataḥ(1) //
169.d:
दिवानुगच्छेद्गाश् चैव तिष्ठन्नूर्ध्वं रजः पिवेत् /
वृषभैकादशा गास्तु दद्याद्विचारितव्रतः(1) //
169.m: By day he should follow the cows, and standing upright, he should drink their dust; / having completed the votive observance, he should give away cows with a bull as the eleventh.

169.s:
avidyamāne sarvasvaṃ vedavidbhyo nivedayet /
pādamekañcaredrodhe dvau pādau bandhane caret //
:n
1 dadyāt sucaritavrata iti ṅa..
:p 171
169.d:
अविद्यमाने सर्वस्वं वेदविद्भ्यो निवेदयेत् /
पादमेकञ्चरेद्रोधे द्वौ पादौ बन्धने चरेत् //
:न्
1 दद्यात् सुचरितव्रत इति ङ..
:प् 171
169.m:
If [cattle are] not available, he should offer all his possessions to knowers of the Veda. / He should perform one quarter [of the penance] for confining [a cow], and two quarters for tying it up;
[Footnote]
[Variant: 1. "he should give, having well performed the votive observance", thus ms. ṅa.]
[Page 171]

169.s:
yojane pādahīnaṃ syāccaret sarvaṃ nipātane /
kāntāreṣvatha durgeṣu viṣameṣu bhayeṣu ca //
169.d:
योजने पादहीनं स्याच्चरेत् सर्वं निपातने /
कान्तारेष्वथ दुर्गेषु विषमेषु भयेषु च //
169.m: it should be less by a quarter [if death occurs] in yoking; he should perform the whole [expiation] in case of causing death. / In wildernesses, in difficult terrain, in rough places, and in perils,

169.s:
yadi tatra vipattiḥ syādekapādo vidhīyate /
ghaṇṭābharaṇadoṣeṇa tathaivardhaṃ vinirdiśat //
169.d:
यदि तत्र विपत्तिः स्यादेकपादो विधीयते /
घण्टाभरणदोषेण तथैवर्धं विनिर्दिशत् //
169.m: if death should occur there, one quarter is prescribed; / similarly, one should assign half for the fault of [decorating with] a bell-ornament.

169.s:
damane damane rodhe śakaṭasya niyojane /
stambhaśṛṅkhalapāśeṣu mṛte pādonamācaret //
169.d:
दमने दमने रोधे शकटस्य नियोजने /
स्तम्भशृङ्खलपाशेषु मृते पादोनमाचरेत् //
169.m: In training, in breaking in, in confining, in harnessing to a cart, / or if it dies in a post, chain, or noose, one should perform three-quarters.

169.s:
śṛṅgabhaṅge 'sthibhaṅge ca lāṅgūlacchedane tathā /
yāvakantu pivettāvadyāvat susthā tu gaurbhavet //
169.d:
शृङ्गभङ्गे ऽस्थिभङ्गे च लाङ्गूलच्छेदने तथा /
यावकन्तु पिवेत्तावद्यावत् सुस्था तु गौर्भवेत् //
169.m: If a horn is broken, or a bone is broken, or likewise if the tail is severed, / he should drink barley gruel until the cow becomes healthy again.

169.s:
gomatīñca japedvidyāṃ gostutiṃ gomatīṃ smaret /
ekā cedbahubhirdaivād yatra vyāpāditā bhavet //
169.d:
गोमतीञ्च जपेद्विद्यां गोस्तुतिं गोमतीं स्मरेत् /
एका चेद्बहुभिर्दैवाद् यत्र व्यापादिता भवेत् //
169.m: He should recite the Gomatī formula, and recollect the Gomatī hymn to the cow. / If by chance a single [cow] should be killed by many,

169.s:
pādaṃ pādantu hatyāyāś careyuste pṛthak pṛthak /
upakāre kriyamāṇe vipattau nāsti pātakaṃ //
169.d:
पादं पादन्तु हत्यायाश् चरेयुस्ते पृथक् पृथक् /
उपकारे क्रियमाणे विपत्तौ नास्ति पातकं //
169.m: they should each separately perform one quarter of [the penance for] the slaughter. / When doing an act of aid, there is no sin if death occurs.

169.s:
etadeva vrataṃ kuryurupapātakinas tathā /
avakīrṇavarjaṃ śuddhyarthañcāndrāyaṇamathāpi vā //
169.d:
एतदेव व्रतं कुर्युरुपपातकिनस् तथा /
अवकीर्णवर्जं शुद्ध्यर्थञ्चान्द्रायणमथापि वा //
169.m: Those guilty of minor sins should perform this same votive observance for purification, / with the exception of one who has broken his vow of chastity; or else a cāndrāyaṇa penance.

169.s:
avakīrṇī tu kālena gardhabhena catuṣpathe /
pākayajñavidhānena yajeta nirṛtiṃ niśi //
169.d:
अवकीर्णी तु कालेन गर्धभेन चतुष्पथे /
पाकयज्ञविधानेन यजेत निरृतिं निशि //
169.m: One who has broken his vow of chastity, however, should in due time sacrifice a donkey at a crossroads / to Nirṛti at night, in accordance with the rule of cooked sacrifices.

169.s:
kṛtvāgniṃ vidhivaddhīmānantatastu samittṛcā /
candrendraguruvahnīnāṃ juhuyāt sarpiṣāhutiṃ(1) //
169.d:
कृत्वाग्निं विधिवद्धीमानन्ततस्तु समित्तृचा /
चन्द्रेन्द्रगुरुवह्नीनां जुहुयात् सर्पिषाहुतिं(1) //
169.m: The wise man, having prepared the fire according to rule, and then with a triplet of kindling verses, / should offer an oblation of clarified butter to the Moon, Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Agni.

169.s:
athavā gārdhabhañcarma vasitvābdañcarenmahīṃ /
hatvā garbhamavijñātaṃ brahmahatyāvrataṃ caret //
:n
1 juhuyātsarpiṣāhutīriti kha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. ca
:p 172
169.d:
अथवा गार्धभञ्चर्म वसित्वाब्दञ्चरेन्महीं /
हत्वा गर्भमविज्ञातं ब्रह्महत्याव्रतं चरेत् //
:न्
1 जुहुयात्सर्पिषाहुतीरिति ख.. , ङ.. , ज.. च
:प् 172
169.m:
Or, clad in an ass’s hide, he should wander over the earth for a year. / Having killed an embryo of unknown sex, he should perform the votive observance for killing a Brahmin.
[Footnote]
[Variant: 1. "should offer oblations of clarified butter", thus mss. kha, ṅa, and ja.]
[Page 172]

169.s:
sarāṃ pītvā dvijo mohādagnivarṇāṃ surāṃ pivet /
gomūtramagnivarṇaṃ vā pivedudakameva vā //
169.d:
सरां पीत्वा द्विजो मोहादग्निवर्णां सुरां पिवेत् /
गोमूत्रमग्निवर्णं वा पिवेदुदकमेव वा //
169.m: Having drunk spirituous liquor out of delusion, a twice-born should drink fire-hot liquor, / or he should drink fire-hot cow urine, or simply water.

169.s:
suvarṇasteyakṛdvipro rājānamabhigamya tu /
svakarma khyāpayan vrūyānmāṃ bhavānanuśāstviti //
169.d:
सुवर्णस्तेयकृद्विप्रो राजानमभिगम्य तु /
स्वकर्म ख्यापयन् व्रूयान्मां भवाननुशास्त्विति //
169.m: A Brahmin who commits theft of gold, having approached the king, / declaring his own deed, should say: "May your majesty punish me!"

169.s:
gṛhītvā muśalaṃ rājā sakṛddhanyāt svayaṅgataṃ /
badhena śuddhyate steyo brāhmaṇastapasaiva vā //
169.d:
गृहीत्वा मुशलं राजा सकृद्धन्यात् स्वयङ्गतं /
बधेन शुद्ध्यते स्तेयो ब्राह्मणस्तपसैव वा //
169.m: Taking a club, the king should strike once him who came on his own. / By death the thief is purified, or a Brahmin [is purified] through ascetic austerity alone.

169.s:
gurutalpo nikṛtyaiva śiśnañca vṛṣaṇaṃ svayaṃ /
nidhāya cāñcalau gacchedānipātācca nairṛtiṃ //
169.d:
गुरुतल्पो निकृत्यैव शिश्नञ्च वृषणं स्वयं /
निधाय चाञ्चलौ गच्छेदानिपाताच्च नैरृतिं //
169.m: One who violates his guru’s bed, having himself cut off his penis and testicles, / and placed them in his cupped hands, should walk toward the southwest until he drops down dead.

169.s:
cāndrāyaṇān vā trīnmāsānabhyasenniyatendriyaḥ /
jātibhraṃśakaraṃ karma kṛtvānyatamamicchayā //
169.d:
चान्द्रायणान् वा त्रीन्मासानभ्यसेन्नियतेन्द्रियः /
जातिभ्रंशकरं कर्म कृत्वान्यतममिच्छया //
169.m: Or, with restrained senses, he should practice cāndrāyaṇa penances for three months. / Having intentionally performed any action that causes loss of caste,

169.s:
carecchāntapanaṃ kṛcchraṃ prājāpatyamanicchayā /
saṅkarīpātrakṛtyāsu māsaṃ śodhanamaindavaṃ //
169.d:
चरेच्छान्तपनं कृच्छ्रं प्राजापत्यमनिच्छया /
सङ्करीपात्रकृत्यासु मासं शोधनमैन्दवं //
169.m: he should perform the śāntapana kṛcchra penance; if unintentionally, the prājāpatya penance. / For deeds causing degradation to a mixed class, a lunar penance of one month is the purifier.

169.s:
malinīkaraṇīyeṣu taptaṃ syādyāvakaṃ tryahaṃ /
turīyo brahmahatyāyāḥ kṣatriyasya badhe smṛtaḥ //
169.d:
मलिनीकरणीयेषु तप्तं स्याद्यावकं त्र्यहं /
तुरीयो ब्रह्महत्यायाः क्षत्रियस्य बधे स्मृतः //
169.m: For deeds causing defilement, there should be hot barley gruel for three days. / For killing a kṣatriya, one-fourth of [the penance for] killing a Brahmin is remembered;

169.s:
vaiśye 'ṣṭamāṃśe vṛttasthe śūdre jñeyastu ṣoḍaśaḥ /
mārjaranakulau hatvā cāsaṃ maṇḍūkameva ca //
169.d:
वैश्ये ऽष्टमांशे वृत्तस्थे शूद्रे ज्ञेयस्तु षोडशः /
मार्जरनकुलौ हत्वा चासं मण्डूकमेव च //
169.m: for a vaiśya who lives properly, an eighth part; and for a śūdra, a sixteenth part is to be known. / Having killed a cat, a mongoose, a blue jay, or a frog,

169.s:
śvagodholūkakākāṃś ca śūdrahatyāvrataṃ caret /
caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ nārīṃ hatvānavasthitāṃ //
169.d:
श्वगोधोलूककाकांश् च शूद्रहत्याव्रतं चरेत् /
चतुर्णामपि वर्णानां नारीं हत्वानवस्थितां //
169.m: a dog, an iguana, an owl, or a crow, he should perform the votive observance for killing a śūdra. / Having killed a woman of any of the four castes who is unchaste,

169.s:
amatyaiva pramāpya strīṃ śūdrahatyāvrataṃ caret /
sarpādīnāṃ badhe naktamanasthnāṃ vāyusaṃyamaḥ //
169.d:
अमत्यैव प्रमाप्य स्त्रीं शूद्रहत्याव्रतं चरेत् /
सर्पादीनां बधे नक्तमनस्थ्नां वायुसंयमः //
169.m: or having unintentionally slain a woman, he should perform the votive observance for killing a śūdra. / In killing snakes and the like, [there is fasting] at night; for boneless creatures, breath-control.

169.s:
dravyāṇāmalpasārāṇāṃ steyaṃ kṛtvānyaveśmataḥ /
carecchāntapanaṃ kṛcchaṃ vrataṃ nirvāpya siddhyati //
:p 173
169.d:
द्रव्याणामल्पसाराणां स्तेयं कृत्वान्यवेश्मतः /
चरेच्छान्तपनं कृच्छं व्रतं निर्वाप्य सिद्ध्यति //
:प् 173
169.m:
Having stolen items of little value from another's house, / he should perform the śāntapana kṛcchra; having discharged the votive observance, he is purified.
[Page 173]

169.s:
bhakṣabhojyāpaharaṇe yānaśayyāsanasya ca /
puṣpamūlaphalānāñca pañcagavyaṃ viśodhanaṃ //
169.d:
भक्षभोज्यापहरणे यानशय्यासनस्य च /
पुष्पमूलफलानाञ्च पञ्चगव्यं विशोधनं //
169.m: In the case of stealing foods to be chewed or eaten, or a vehicle, bed, or seat, / or flowers, roots, and fruits, the five products of the cow are the purifier.

169.s:
tṛṇakāṣṭhadrumāṇāntu śuṣkānnasya guḍasya ca /
celacarmāmiṣāṇāntu(1) trirātraṃ syādabhojanaṃ //
169.d:
तृणकाष्ठद्रुमाणान्तु शुष्कान्नस्य गुडस्य च /
चेलचर्मामिषाणान्तु(1) त्रिरात्रं स्यादभोजनं //
169.m: For [the theft of] grass, wood, trees, dried grain, molasses, / clothes, skins, or meat, there should be a three-night fast.

169.s:
maṇimuktāpravālānāṃ tāmrasya rajatasya ca /
ayaḥkāṃsyopalānāñca dvādaśāhaṃ kaṇānnabhuk //
169.d:
मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानां ताम्रस्य रजतस्य च /
अयःकांस्योपलानाञ्च द्वादशाहं कणान्नभुक् //
169.m: For gems, pearls, corals, copper, silver, / iron, bell-metal, and stones, he should eat broken grain for twelve days.

169.s:
kārpāsakīṭajīrṇānāṃ dviśaphaikaśaphasya ca /
pakṣigandhauṣadhīnāntu rajvā caiva tryahampayaḥ //
169.d:
कार्पासकीटजीर्णानां द्विशफैकशफस्य च /
पक्षिगन्धौषधीनान्तु रज्वा चैव त्र्यहम्पयः //
169.m: For cotton, silk, worn-out garments, cloven-hoofed and single-hoofed animals, / birds, perfumes, medicinal herbs, and ropes, [he should drink only] milk for three days.

169.s:
gurutalpavrataṃ kuryādretaḥ siktvā svayoniṣu /
sakhyuḥ putrasya ca strīṣu kumāroṣvantyajāsu ca //
169.d:
गुरुतल्पव्रतं कुर्याद्रेतः सिक्त्वा स्वयोनिषु /
सख्युः पुत्रस्य च स्त्रीषु कुमारोष्वन्त्यजासु च //
169.m: He should perform the vow of a violator of the guru’s bed if he emits semen into women of his own lineage, / among the wives of a friend or a son, or among unmarried maidens and outcaste women.

169.s:
pitṛsvasreyīṃ bhaginīṃ svasrīyāṃ mātureva ca /
mātuś ca bhrāturāptasya gatvā cāndrāyaṇañcaret //
169.d:
पितृस्वस्रेयीं भगिनीं स्वस्रीयां मातुरेव च /
मातुश् च भ्रातुराप्तस्य गत्वा चान्द्रायणञ्चरेत् //
169.m: Having had sexual intercourse with a paternal aunt's daughter, a sister, a maternal aunt's daughter, / or the wife of a maternal uncle or of a trusted friend, he should perform the cāndrāyaṇa penance.

169.s:
amānuṣīṣu puruṣa udakyāyāmayoniṣu /
retaḥ siktvā jale caiva kṛcchraṃ śāntapanañcaret //
169.d:
अमानुषीषु पुरुष उदक्यायामयोनिषु /
रेतः सिक्त्वा जले चैव कृच्छ्रं शान्तपनञ्चरेत् //
169.m: If a man emits semen in non-human females, in a menstruating woman, in unnatural orifices, / or in water, he should perform the śāntapana kṛcchra penance.

169.s:
maithunantu samāsevya puṃsi yoṣiti vā dvijaḥ /
goyāne 'psu divā caiva savāsāḥ snānamācaret //
169.d:
मैथुनन्तु समासेव्य पुंसि योषिति वा द्विजः /
गोयाने ऽप्सु दिवा चैव सवासाः स्नानमाचरेत् //
169.m: Having practiced sexual intercourse in a male or in a woman, / in a bullock cart, in water, or by day, a twice-born should perform an ablution with his clothes on.

169.s:
caṇḍālāntyastriyo gatvā bhuktvā ca pratigṛhya ca /
patatyajñānato vipro jñānāt sāmyantu gacchati //
169.d:
चण्डालान्त्यस्त्रियो गत्वा भुक्त्वा च प्रतिगृह्य च /
पतत्यज्ञानतो विप्रो ज्ञानात् साम्यन्तु गच्छति //
169.m: Having had sexual intercourse with Caṇḍāla or outcaste women, having eaten their food, or accepted [gifts from them], / a Brahmin falls through ignorance; through intentional action, he becomes equal to them.

169.s:
vipraduṣṭāṃ striyaṃ bhartā nirundhyādekaveśmani /
yat puṃsaḥ paradāreṣu tadenāñcārayedvrataṃ //
169.d:
विप्रदुष्टां स्त्रियं भर्ता निरुन्ध्यादेकवेश्मनि /
यत् पुंसः परदारेषु तदेनाञ्चारयेद्व्रतं //
169.m: A husband should confine an unfaithful wife to a single dwelling; / that penance which applies to a man who commits adultery with another's wife, he should make her perform.

169.s:
sācetpunaḥ praduṣyeta sadṛśenopamantritā /
kṛcchrañcādrāyaṇañcaiva tadasyāḥ pāvanaṃ smṛtaṃ //
:n
1 veṇucarmāmiṣāṇāñceti jha..
:p 174
169.d:
साचेत्पुनः प्रदुष्येत सदृशेनोपमन्त्रिता /
कृच्छ्रञ्चाद्रायणञ्चैव तदस्याः पावनं स्मृतं //
:न्
1 वेणुचर्मामिषाणाञ्चेति झ..
:प् 174
169.m:
If she should again be corrupted when solicited by an equal, / the kṛcchra and cāndrāyaṇa penances are remembered as her purifier.
[Footnote]
[Variant: 1. "bamboo, skins, or meat", thus ms. jha.]
[Page 174]

169.s:
yat karotyekarātreṇa vṛṣalīsevanaṃ dvijaḥ /
tadbhaikṣyabhuk japennityaṃ tribhirvaṣair vyapohati //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe prāyaścittāni nāma
ekonasaptatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
prāyaścittāni
169.d:
यत् करोत्येकरात्रेण वृषलीसेवनं द्विजः /
तद्भैक्ष्यभुक् जपेन्नित्यं त्रिभिर्वषैर् व्यपोहति //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे प्रायश्चित्तानि नाम
एकोनसप्तत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
प्रायश्चित्तानि
169.m:
[The guilt] that a twice-born incurs by spending a single night with a śūdra woman, / he removes in three years by living on alms and continually reciting sacred texts.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-ninth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named "Expiations."
Now begins the one hundred and seventieth chapter:
Expiations.

170.s:
puṣkara uvāca
mahāpāpānuyuktānāṃ(1) prāyaścittāni(2) vacmite /
saṃvatsareṇa patati patitena sahācaran //
170.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
महापापानुयुक्तानां(1) प्रायश्चित्तानि(2) वच्मिते /
संवत्सरेण पतति पतितेन सहाचरन् //
170.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare to you the expiations for those associated with major sins. / By associating with a fallen person for a year, one becomes fallen,

170.s:
yājanāddhyāpanādyaunānna tu yānāśanāsanāt /
yo yena patitenaiṣāṃ saṃsargaṃ yāti mānavaḥ //
170.d:
याजनाद्ध्यापनाद्यौनान्न तु यानाशनासनात् /
यो येन पतितेनैषां संसर्गं याति मानवः //
170.m: through officiating at his sacrifice, teaching him, or entering marital alliance with him, but not through sharing a vehicle, food, or a seat. / Whichever person forms an association with any of these fallen people,

170.s:
sa tasyaiva vrataṃ kuryāttatsaṃsargasya śuddhaye /
patitasyodakaṃ kāryaṃ sapiṇḍair bāndhavaiḥ saha //
170.d:
स तस्यैव व्रतं कुर्यात्तत्संसर्गस्य शुद्धये /
पतितस्योदकं कार्यं सपिण्डैर् बान्धवैः सह //
170.m: He should perform the very votive observance [prescribed] for that [sinner] to purify himself of that association. / Water offerings for an outcaste must be made by his sapiṇḍas along with his kinsmen.

170.s:
nindite 'hani sāyāhṇe jñātyṛtvig gurusannidhau /
dāso ghaṭamapāṃ pūrṇaṃ paryasyet pretavatpadā(3) //
170.d:
निन्दिते ऽहनि सायाह्णे ज्ञात्यृत्विग् गुरुसन्निधौ /
दासो घटमपां पूर्णं पर्यस्येत् प्रेतवत्पदा(3) //
170.m: On an inauspicious day, at dusk, in the presence of relatives, officiating priests, and elders, / a servant should overturn a pot full of water with his foot, as for a dead man.

170.s:
ahorātramupāsītannaśaucaṃ bāndhavaiḥ saha /
nivartayeraṃstasmāttu jyeṣṭhāṃśambhāṣaṇādike //
170.d:
अहोरात्रमुपासीतन्नशौचं बान्धवैः सह /
निवर्तयेरंस्तस्मात्तु ज्येष्ठांशम्भाषणादिके //
170.m: They should observe ritual impurity for a day and a night along with their kinsmen. / Moreover, they should exclude him from the eldest son's share, conversation, and the like;

170.s:
jyeṣṭhāṃśamprāpnuyāccāsya yavīyān guṇato 'dhikaḥ /
:n
1 mahāpāpopapannānāmiti ṅa..
2 prāyaścittaṃ vadāmi ta iti jha..
3 pretavat sadeti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
:p 175
prāyaścitte tu carite pūrṇaṃ kumbhamapāṃ navaṃ //
170.d:
ज्येष्ठांशम्प्राप्नुयाच्चास्य यवीयान् गुणतो ऽधिकः /
:न्
1 महापापोपपन्नानामिति ङ..
2 प्रायश्चित्तं वदामि त इति झ..
3 प्रेतवत् सदेति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
:प् 175
प्रायश्चित्ते तु चरिते पूर्णं कुम्भमपां नवं //
170.m:
and a younger brother who is superior in virtue should obtain his eldest share.
[Footnote]
1. 'mahāpāpopapannānām' in manuscript ṅa.
2. 'prāyaścittaṃ vadāmi te' in manuscript jha.
3. 'pretavat sadā' in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, and ṅa. / [p. 175]
When, however, the expiation has been performed, [they should take] a new pot full of water;

170.s:
tenaiva sārdhaṃ prāśyeyuḥ snātvā puṇyajalāśaye /
evameva vidhiṃ kuryuryoṣitsu papitāsvapi //
170.d:
तेनैव सार्धं प्राश्येयुः स्नात्वा पुण्यजलाशये /
एवमेव विधिं कुर्युर्योषित्सु पपितास्वपि //
170.m: having bathed in a sacred pool, they should drink [from it] together with him. / They should carry out this very rite even for women who have fallen [from caste].

170.s:
vastrānnapānandeyantu vaseyuś ca gṛhāntike /
teṣāṃ dvijānāṃ sāvitrī nānūdyeta(1) yathāvidhi //
170.d:
वस्त्रान्नपानन्देयन्तु वसेयुश् च गृहान्तिके /
तेषां द्विजानां सावित्री नानूद्येत(1) यथाविधि //
170.m: Clothing, food, and drink should be given [to them], and they should dwell near the house. / For those twice-born whose Sāvitrī [mantra] has not been recited according to rule,

170.s:
tāṃścārayitvā trīn kṛchrān yathāvidhyupanāyayet /
vikarmasthāḥ parityaktāsteṣāṃ mapyetadādiśet //
170.d:
तांश्चारयित्वा त्रीन् कृछ्रान् यथाविध्युपनाययेत् /
विकर्मस्थाः परित्यक्तास्तेषां मप्येतदादिशेत् //
170.m: having made them perform three kṛcchra penances, one should initiate them according to rule. / One should also prescribe this for those fallen into illicit deeds or abandoned.

170.s:
japitvā trīṇi sāvitryāḥ sahastrāṇi samāhitaḥ /
māsaṅgoṣṭhe payaḥ pītvā mucyate 'satpratigrahāt //
170.d:
जपित्वा त्रीणि सावित्र्याः सहस्त्राणि समाहितः /
मासङ्गोष्ठे पयः पीत्वा मुच्यते ऽसत्प्रतिग्रहात् //
170.m: Having recited three thousand [repetitions] of the Sāvitrī [mantra] with concentrated mind / and lived on milk in a cowpen for a month, one is freed from [the sin of accepting an] improper gift.

170.s:
brātyānāṃ yājanaṃ kṛtvā pareṣāmantyakarma ca /
abhicāramahīnānāntribhiḥ kṛcchair vyapohati(2) //
170.d:
ब्रात्यानां याजनं कृत्वा परेषामन्त्यकर्म च /
अभिचारमहीनानान्त्रिभिः कृच्छैर् व्यपोहति(2) //
170.m: Having officiated at sacrifices for the uninitiated (vrātyas), performed funeral rites for unrelated persons, / and [practiced] sorcery on unimpaired persons, one removes [the sin] by three kṛcchra penances.

170.s:
śaraṇāgataṃ parityajya vedaṃ viplāvya ca dvijaḥ /
saṃvatsaṃ yatāhārastatpāpamapasedhati //
170.d:
शरणागतं परित्यज्य वेदं विप्लाव्य च द्विजः /
संवत्सं यताहारस्तत्पापमपसेधति //
170.m: A twice-born man who abandons someone seeking refuge or misrepresents the Veda / wards off that sin [by being] restrained in diet for a year.

170.s:
śvaśṛgālakharair daṣṭo grāmyaiḥ kravyādbhireva ca /
naroṣṭrāśvair varāhaiś ca(3) prāṇāyāmena śuddhyati //
170.d:
श्वशृगालखरैर् दष्टो ग्राम्यैः क्रव्याद्भिरेव च /
नरोष्ट्राश्वैर् वराहैश् च(3) प्राणायामेन शुद्ध्यति //
170.m: A man bitten by dogs, jackals, or donkeys, or by domestic carnivorous animals, / camels, horses, or boars, becomes pure by breath-control (prāṇāyāma).

170.s:
snātakavratalope ca karmatyāge hy abhojanaṃ /
huṅkāraṃ(4) brāhmaṇasyoktvā tvaṅkarañca garīyasaḥ //
170.d:
स्नातकव्रतलोपे च कर्मत्यागे ह्य् अभोजनं /
हुङ्कारं(4) ब्राह्मणस्योक्त्वा त्वङ्करञ्च गरीयसः //
170.m: Upon the violation of a snātaka's vows or the abandonment of prescribed rites, fasting [is prescribed]. / Having uttered a grunt of contempt (huṅkāra) at a brāhmaṇa or addressed a superior disrespectfully ('thou'),

170.s:
snātvānaśnannahaḥśeṣamabhivādya prasādayet /
avagūrya carekṣacchramatikṛcchrannipātane //
170.d:
स्नात्वानश्नन्नहःशेषमभिवाद्य प्रसादयेत् /
अवगूर्य चरेक्षच्छ्रमतिकृच्छ्रन्निपातने //
170.m: bathing and fasting for the remainder of the day, having saluted [him], he should propitiate him. / Raising a hand [against a brāhmaṇa], he should perform a kṛcchra; upon striking him down, an atikṛcchra;

170.s:
